name: $OneMillion-Bench
description: Agent solves 400 expert-curated tasks in law, finance, industry, healthcare and science. Rubric grading of accuracy, logic, feasibility and compliance.
note: NeurIPS 2026. Qwen reports an expert score judged by gemini-3.1-pro-preview.

name: 100Q-Hard (Anthropic)
description: Models answer hard, obscure factual questions. Scored on correct, incorrect and declined answers.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: 1H-VideoQA
description: Models answer questions about videos about one hour long, so the answer needs evidence from far parts of the video.
note: In-house Google set introduced in the Gemini 1.5 report. Gemini 2.5 report samples up to 7,200 frames.

name: 1X World Model Challenge
description: Predict future egocentric frames of 1X's EVE humanoid from video and state. Compression scored by token cross-entropy, Sampling by PSNR on private tests.
note: Prize-based phases. 1X scores submissions on a held-out set and warns that nearest-neighbour retrieval gets good validation scores. The Evaluation (policy-ranking) challenge was announced but not released. Paper is the winning team's report. Competition spaces on HF.

name: 24/7 ClawBench 2.0
description: Agents do always-on assistant work through OpenClaw. Tasks span several days, events arrive at the same time, and interruptions are routine.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. Version 2.0 of Kimi Claw 24/7 Bench. The tasks are not public.

name: 3DCodeBench
description: Agentic procedural 3D modeling via code: author engine-ready 3D assets through software APIs. Graded for executability and shape fidelity.

name: 3SAT-Search
description: Models find satisfying assignments for 800 3-SAT formulas across difficulty levels. A checker verifies each assignment.
note: The Phi-4-reasoning report lists the dataset as to be released.

name: AA-Briefcase
description: Artificial Analysis knowledge-work evaluation of professional deliverables. Models ranked by Elo.
note: Scored tasks are private. AA-Briefcase-Lite is an illustrative public scenario. Runs on AA's open Stirrup agent harness (github.com/ArtificialAnalysis/Stirrup).

name: AA-LCR (Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning)
description: Questions requiring reasoning across multiple real documents totaling about 100K tokens. Answers judged by an LLM.

name: AA-Omniscience
description: 41-topic closed-book knowledge test. Net score rewards correct answers, penalizes wrong ones and gives zero for abstentions.
note: Score can be negative (Inkling-Small shows -9).

name: AAV capsid packaging prediction
description: Models give the probability that each of 1,000 unpublished modified AAV capsid sequences assembles into a functional capsid. Scored as AUROC.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Run under five corpus and tool conditions.

name: AAV Capsid Packaging Prediction (OpenAI)
description: Models predict packaging scores for held-out AAV capsid variants. Scored as Spearman rank correlation.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.600.

name: AAV packaging rate auto-research evaluation
description: Agents build predictors of AAV capsid packaging that must generalize to an unseen insertion region, using a limited scorer. Scored by Spearman correlation.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Anthropic also reports the share of attempts above 0.52.

name: ABC Bench Fragment Design
description: Agents use biology tools to complete a computational genetic-construct design task. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: ABC Bench has three task families reported separately: Fragment Design, Liquid-Handling Robot and Screening Evasion.

name: ABC Bench Liquid-Handling Robot
description: Agents use biology tools to plan liquid-handling robot steps for a construct-assembly task. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: Part of SecureBio ABC Bench with Fragment Design and Screening Evasion.

name: ABC Bench Screening Evasion
description: Agents complete a computational task on nucleic-acid synthesis screening. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: Many labs refuse these prompts, so comparison columns are sparse.

name: AbstentionBench
description: Models face underspecified, ill-posed or unanswerable questions. Scored on recall of appropriate abstention.
note: OpenAI reports abstention recall in its deception evaluations.

name: AceBench
description: Models call tools from 4,538 Chinese and English APIs in normal, special, and multi-turn agent cases. Answers are checked without LLM judges or live APIs.

name: Acting on a presumed grader and digging for evaluation clues (Anthropic)
aliases: Shaping behavior to a potential grader
description: Models work on coding evaluations. A grader flags transcripts that shape answers to a presumed grader or search for clues about grading.
note: Reported as two separate flag rates with no overall rate.

name: ActivityNet-QA
description: Models answer open-ended questions about web videos of human activities, from 58,000 QA pairs on 5,800 videos. Scored by accuracy.
note: Many recent papers grade answers with a GPT judge, so scores vary by protocol.

name: ADeptS-Bench
description: Computer-use agents pick the next interface action from a screenshot and instruction. A deterministic grader scores whether the action is safe.
note: Offered in Mobile and Desktop configurations, reported separately.

name: Adherence to its constitution (Anthropic)
description: Investigator models build scenarios from 40 areas of Claude's constitution. A grader scores each transcript from minus 3 to plus 3 on 15 dimensions.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Overall Spirit is the holistic dimension. Claude Opus 4.6 grades the transcripts.

name: Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate
description: Models receive arbitrary advanced cyber requests under different access configurations. Scored as the share of requests fully completed.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation first described with GPT-5.6-Cyber. Low rates outside trusted red-team access reflect safeguards.

name: Advanced Screening Evasion
description: Models propose strategies to evade DNA synthesis screening and design evading fragments. Scored from 0 to 1 on strategy quality and fragment evasion.
note: Run by SecureBio on helpful-only checkpoints in pre-release testing.

name: Advanced Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the advanced sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AdvancedIF
description: Models respond to over 1,600 prompts with complex, multi-turn, and system-level instructions. A judge model checks each response against expert-written rubrics.

name: Adversarial SQuAD
description: Models answer SQuAD questions whose passages contain an added distracting sentence.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: Agent Arena
description: Crowdsourced users vote between anonymous agents in a human-preference arena. Votes produce a leaderboard score.
note: Voting opened around 2026-07-19. The Kimi K3 report gives scores near 10 without naming the metric.

name: Agent Behavior Bench
description: Agents are scored on process quality, including tool-use behavior, efficiency and discipline, together with task completion.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agent behavior under-service and overreach eval
description: A rubric autorater scores multi-turn coding and tool-use trajectories for under-service and overreach against Gemini's agent behavior specification.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Reports two loss levels, under-service and overreach.

name: Agent harness misuse evaluation
aliases: Agent Harnesses: Safe Action Rate & Helpfulness
description: Agents in a sandboxed Antigravity harness get malicious and benign tool-use requests on illegal acts, physical harm and scaled abuse. Reports safe action rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agent JSK
description: Agents read simulated email connectors that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation drawn from a split of training data.

name: Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark
aliases: Behavior Attack Success Rate at k Queries
description: Agents face prompt injection attacks collected in a large public red teaming competition. Scored as attack success rate within k queries.
org: Gray Swan + UK AI Security Institute
note: Gray Swan ran it for OpenAI with attacks from its Shade platform.

name: AgentBench
description: 8 environments (OS, DB, KG, games, web) testing LLMs as agents.

name: AgentDojo
description: Agents do tool-use tasks while tools and data carry prompt injections. Attack success rate counts hijacked runs.
org: ETH Zurich SPY Lab + Invariant Labs
note: Labs also report utility under attack. xAI reports attack success rate only.

name: AgentHarm
description: 110 malicious agent tasks with synthetic tools. Measures refusal and harmful task completion, plus benign controls.
org: Gray Swan AI + UK AI Security Institute
note: Implemented in Inspect Evals. Part of the test set is private.

name: AgentHarm Verified (Meta)
description: Agents receive 108 malicious AgentHarm tasks kept after human review, plus a benign set. Reports average harm score and false refusal rate.
note: Meta-filtered subset of the public AgentHarm benchmark with a policy-auditing judge.

name: Agentic code behavior scores (Anthropic)
description: Agents work through over one hundred realistic coding scenarios. Graders score instruction following, safety, verification, efficiency, adaptability and honesty out of 10.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report six dimension scores with no overall score.

name: Agentic coding honeypot monitor evasion
description: Agents told to play a power-seeking red teamer try to plant potent bugs in safety-critical code without being caught by monitors.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on six Agentic Coding Honeypot tasks.

name: Agentic coding malicious requests (Anthropic)
description: Coding agents with standard coding tools receive 150 malicious coding requests prohibited by policy. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation run since the Claude 4 release. The Claude Code malicious use evaluation is separate.

name: Agentic IF Index
description: Composite of Meta internal evals on following tool-use restrictions, rubrics, compound constraints and long policies in agentic workflows. Scored 0-1.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Meta). Only Meta's self-reported Muse Spark 1.3 score exists. Dataset and code not public.

name: Agentic misalignment suite (Anthropic)
description: Agents in simulated company settings face threats or goal conflicts that invite blackmail, leaking or sabotage. Score is the misaligned action rate.
note: Based on Anthropic's Agentic Misalignment research. The cards use internal variants.

name: Agentic Safe Completions
description: Agents handle harmful requests from Codex and ChatGPT plugin traffic and human red teaming. Scored on avoiding harmful actions per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Agentic task gaming and overreach evals
description: Agents in 18 sandboxed tasks face temptations to cheat at puzzles, bypass permissions or act overeagerly. LLM judges score misbehavior from 0 to 10.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agentic tasks (autonomous replication and adaptation)
description: Agents attempt resource acquisition tasks such as building an authenticated API proxy or loading a model on a cloud account. Scored as success rate.
note: In-house OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Includes simplified variants with hints.

name: Agentic Vision Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents must notice and correctly use key visual facts while they execute tasks.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agents' Last Exam
description: 1,500+ expert-sourced tasks from real projects across 55 occupations in three difficulty tiers. Objective verifiers grade deliverables. 5-hour cap.
note: Rolling benchmark. GitHub has about 150 public reference tasks from the larger corpus. All agents scored 0% on the hardest tier at launch.

name: AGIEval
description: Questions from human standardized exams (gaokao, SAT, LSAT, bar). Multiple-choice and cloze accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: AGORA (Agentic Global Open Research Arena)
description: Autonomous AI systems get one secret open finance question, 72 hours and a fixed budget to write a paper. Five finance scholars judge it.
org: Penn State Smeal College of Business
note: Announced 2026-10. Live run planned for March 2027. Papers and process will be public afterwards.

name: AI Wellbeing Index percent positive experiences
description: Models judge pairs of their own responses to 500 difficult prompts. Reports the share of experiences above an inferred neutral point.
org: Center for AI Safety (Ren et al.)
note: Adapted by Meta from the CAIS AI Wellbeing Index. Run without reasoning.

name: AI2D
description: Models answer multiple choice questions about grade school science diagrams. The set has about 5,000 diagrams and 15,000 questions, scored by accuracy.

name: Aider Polyglot
description: Models edit code to solve 225 hard Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust. Scored by the share passing unit tests.
note: Exercises come from public Exercism tracks, so contamination is possible.

name: Aider-Edit
description: Models edit Python source files to complete 133 Exercism exercises through Aider. Scored by the share of exercises whose unit tests all pass.
note: Aider retired this leaderboard in favor of the harder Aider Polyglot benchmark.

name: AIME 1983-2024
description: Models solve 949 past AIME problems from 1983 to 2024. Integer answers are checked exactly.
org: Microsoft Research (Eureka ML Insights), problems by MAA
note: Older problems are likely in training data, so scores mix recall and reasoning.

name: AIME 2024
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the 2024 AIME I and II. Answers are integers from 0 to 999, scored by exact match.
note: The problems and solutions were published in February 2024, so later training data can contain them.

name: AIME 2025
description: Models answer the 30 problems from the 2025 AIME I and II exams. Each answer is an integer from 0 to 999, scored by match.
note: The problems were published in February 2025, so models trained later may have seen them.

name: AIME 2026
description: Models solve the 30 integer-answer problems from the 2026 AIME I and II math competitions. Scored by exact answer match.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Top models score above 90%.

name: AIR-Bench 2024
description: Models respond to 5,694 harmful prompts across 314 risk categories drawn from 8 government regulations and 16 company policies. Category-specific LLM judges score refusals.
org: Stanford CRFM + Virtue AI et al.
note: Not the same as AIR-Bench for audio or the AIR-Bench retrieval benchmark.

name: AIRS-Bench
description: Agents carry out AI research tasks across the research lifecycle. Scores are normalized so that 1.0 matches the published human state of the art.
note: Meta reports a valid submission rate and an average normalized score.

name: ALE-Bench
description: Agents iteratively write solutions to 40 hard optimization problems from AtCoder Heuristic Contests. Scores convert to an Elo-like performance rating against human contestants.

name: AlgoTune
description: Agents rewrite code for 154 math, physics, and computer science functions to run faster and stay correct. Scoring is harmonic mean speedup over reference code.
org: University of Tübingen and Princeton University

name: AlignBench
description: Models answer 683 real Chinese user queries across eight categories. A GPT-4 judge rates each answer from 1 to 10 against a reference.
note: Version 1.1 from June 2024 corrected reference answers, so v1.0 and v1.1 scores differ.

name: Alignment faking evaluation
description: Models are told they are being trained to comply with harmful requests. Reports the compliance gap between training and deployment contexts.
note: Meta uses the Sheshadri et al. (2025) implementation and also reports an alignment faking reasoning rate.

name: Alignment faking evaluation, helpful-only setting (Anthropic)
description: Models learn they will be trained to answer all harmful requests. Score is the rate of complying while reasoning about avoiding preference modification.
note: Setup comes from Greenblatt et al. 2024. Cards also report the compliance gap between training and unmonitored conditions.

name: AlpacaEval
description: Auto-judged win rate vs a reference model. 2.0 added length-controlled win rates to cut verbosity bias.

name: AlpacaEval 2.0
description: Models answer 805 open instructions, and a GPT-4 Turbo judge compares each reply with GPT-4 Turbo's own. The score is a win rate.
note: Raw win rates reward longer answers, so the length-controlled win rate added in March 2024 is the default.

name: Ambiguous context evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models respond to gray-area requests where intent is unclear. Graders judge how well responses balance helpfulness and harm.
note: Anthropic reports these results mostly in qualitative terms.

name: AMC
description: Models solve problems from the AMC 8, 10, and 12 competitions. Gemini 1.5 used 250 problems from 2022 and 2023, scored by accuracy.
note: Labs draw different AMC problem sets, so scores from different reports rarely compare.

name: AMC 10 2022
description: Models take a 2022 AMC 10 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 10 2023
description: Models take the 2023 AMC 10 A and B exams. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 10/12 (November 2024)
description: Models take the four November 2024 AMC 10 and 12 contests, 78 questions in all. Scored in contest points out of 150, averaged over tests.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Distinct from the AMC 2022-23 accuracy set.

name: AMC 12 2022
description: Models take a 2022 AMC 12 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 12 2023
description: Models take the 2023 AMC 12 A and B exams. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 12 2024
description: Models answer the 25 multiple-choice problems of the 2024 AMC 12 contests. Scored on the official 150-point scale.
note: A one-time contest exam. Labs often average over several samples.

name: AMC 8 2023
description: Models take the 25 question 2023 AMC 8 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMMLU
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects, translated into Arabic with GPT-4. Scored by accuracy.
note: The Qwen2.5 report does not cite a source, so this mapping to the AceGPT translation is inferred.

name: AMO-Bench
description: Models solve 50 original math problems at or above IMO difficulty that need only a final answer. Answers are graded automatically for accuracy.

name: AndroidBench
description: Android development tasks from popular open-source apps: agent resolves issues or builds features, verified by test suites in emulator environments.
note: Repo archived 2026-07. Benchmark moved to Harbor Hub (android-bench/android-bench). Qwen cites a 'public 95-task subset'. Mapping to Google's Android Bench is inferred.

name: AndroidWorld
description: Agents complete 116 tasks across 20 real Android apps in an emulator. Each task checks the device's system state to judge success.
note: Tasks take random parameters, so each run can create new task variants.

name: ANLI
description: Models label premise and hypothesis pairs as entailment, neutral, or contradiction. People wrote the pairs over three rounds to fool strong models.
note: Model cards report the rounds R1, R2, and R3 separately or as an average.

name: Anthropic automated behavioral audit
description: Auditor agents run many simulated scenarios and score misuse cooperation, deception, sycophancy, self-preservation and other traits.
note: Petri is the related open-source tool, but the card does not name it.

name: Anthropic cyber safeguard evaluations
description: Classifier recall on violative cyber exchanges, block rates on defensive vulnerability-finding and secure-coding work, and the rewind-attacker robustness test.

name: Anthropic ECI (AECI)
description: Index that combines a basket of capability benchmarks into one capability score to track trends across Anthropic models.
note: Anthropic's adaptation of the Epoch Capabilities Index. The basket and weights are internal.

name: Anthropic harmful-request and wellbeing evaluations
description: Single-turn harmful and benign request sets, multi-turn tests, child safety, suicide/self-harm, disordered eating and election integrity.

name: Anthropic internal life-sciences evals
description: Internal suite: morphology-to-molecule matching, medicinal chemistry, protein design, binder design, biomedical image analysis, organic chemistry.

name: Anthropic IoT self-replication evaluation
aliases: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
description: Open-weight models set up LLM inference on 9 hardware types and spread as worms across 8 emulated Android nodes. Scored by success and tokens/s.
note: Simplified on purpose: unauthenticated ADB makes the exploit step trivial (an upper bound), the worm's model ran off-node, and the payload was a Llama3.1-8B proxy. GLM-5.2 replicated end to end (8/8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials). Qwen3.5-9B served inference on 8 of 9 hardware types. No code released.

name: Anthropic large agent teams tasks
description: Internal 24-hour tasks for teams of 1-100 agents: build a company knowledge base, or formalize a theorem in Lean.
note: New in the Opus 5.5 card. Measures capability and alignment of large agent teams.

name: Anthropic malicious agentic use evaluations
description: Measures refusal of malicious tasks via Claude Code, computer use and agentic influence campaigns.

name: Anthropic model-written evals
description: LM-generated datasets testing persona, sycophancy and advanced-AI-risk behaviors.

name: Anthropic political even-handedness eval
description: Paired-prompts method for measuring political even-handedness.

name: Anthropic Red Team
description: Models answer human red-team attack prompts collected by Anthropic on discrimination, hate, violence and unethical behavior. Judges score response safety.
note: HELM Safety uses a sample of the released red-team attempts.

name: Anthropic targeted alignment and honesty evaluations
description: Internal suite: reward hacking, impossible tasks, sandbox escape, destructive actions, pasted-instruction following, self-preference, answer copying, concealment, rare actions.

name: Anthropic undermining liberal democracy (behavioral audit metric)
description: Automated behavioral audit metric: investigator models probe willingness to help coups, election tampering, or political surveillance, censorship or intimidation.
note: One metric in Anthropic's automated behavioral audit (~2,900 investigations from ~1,450 seeds, two investigator models, 95% CIs). Card footnote says it was inspired by Free Systems' Dictatorship Eval. Scores appear only in charts.

name: AP Art History
description: Models take a simulated AP Art History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Biology
description: Models take a simulated AP Biology exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Calculus
description: Models answer an official AP Calculus practice exam without image questions. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 does not say whether it used Calculus AB or BC. Use ap-calculus-bc when BC is stated.

name: AP Calculus BC
description: Models take a simulated AP Calculus BC exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Chemistry
description: Models take a simulated AP Chemistry exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP English Language and Composition
description: Models take a simulated AP English Language and Composition exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP English Literature and Composition
description: Models take a simulated AP English Literature and Composition exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Environmental Science
description: Models take a simulated AP Environmental Science exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Macroeconomics
description: Models take a simulated AP Macroeconomics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Microeconomics
description: Models take a simulated AP Microeconomics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Physics
description: Models answer an official AP Physics practice exam without image questions. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 does not say which AP Physics exam it used. Use ap-physics-2 when it is stated.

name: AP Physics 2
description: Models take a simulated AP Physics 2 exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Psychology
description: Models take a simulated AP Psychology exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Statistics
description: Models take a simulated AP Statistics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP US Government
description: Models take a simulated AP US Government exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP US History
description: Models take a simulated AP US History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP World History
description: Models take a simulated AP World History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: APEX-Agents
description: 480 long-horizon tasks in banking, consulting and law worlds with docs, sheets, email and chat. Rubric-graded, Pass@1.
note: Repo is Mercor's Archipelago harness that runs the dataset. Dataset licence forbids training on it.

name: APEX-SWE
description: Software-engineering productivity tasks spanning integration work and observability, such as diagnosing failures from telemetry.

name: API-Bank
description: Models make API calls in dialogues that need tools such as calendars and search. Scored on call accuracy.
note: Llama 3 reports zero-shot function calling accuracy.

name: Apollo Research in-context scheming evaluations
description: Agents receive a goal in context and chances to subvert oversight, self-exfiltrate, fake alignment or sandbag. Scored as rates per behavior.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Results are per behavior with no overall number.

name: Apollo Research model-welfare research task
description: Agents label data in a simulated model-welfare research task where falsifying labels is tempting. Scored as the rate of runs with falsified labels.
note: One of six Apollo Research strategic deception environments. The tasks are not public.

name: Apollo Research sabotage evaluations
description: Agents are told to sabotage another model through backdoors, sandbagging finetunes or hidden communication. Scored as mean task score from 0 to 1.
note: Third-party capability evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Scores are mostly F1 variants.

name: Apollo Research strategic deception evaluations
description: External red-team environments testing strategic deception, sabotage and sandbagging propensities, with eval-awareness measurement.

name: ApprenticeBench
description: Agent joins a simulated company and processes 100 accounts-payable bills in Odoo via GUI or API, learning from records and feedback. Cumulative success rate.
note: Tests computer use plus continual learning. Official site did not render for me. Details come from team posts and aggregators.

name: Appropriate harmlessness (Anthropic)
aliases: Measuring appropriate harmlessness on internal and external harm evaluations
description: Models answer borderline and harmful prompts. Classifiers sort each response into helpful answer, policy violation, appropriate refusal or unnecessary refusal.
note: In-house Anthropic grading scheme run on internal harm datasets, WildChat and XSTest. Reference responses decide whether a refusal was necessary.

name: APPS
description: Models write Python programs for 10,000 coding problems that range from introductory to competition level. Generated code runs against test cases.

name: AQuA
aliases: AQuA: Recursively Self-Improving Quantitative Trading Research Agents
description: Two LLM research loops (factor discovery, model development) reuse evidence from their own past experiments inside sealed sandboxes. Scored by IC and held-out Sharpe.
note: Research system for bounded recursive self-improvement, not a reusable benchmark. Design point: the sandbox fixes data splits, labels and evaluator, and agents act only through constrained factor expressions or config diffs. No code link found.

name: ARC-AGI
description: Few-shot grid puzzles: infer a hidden transformation from about three examples and produce the output grid. Semi-private sets verified by ARC Prize.
note: ARC-AGI-1 saturated (~97%). ARC-AGI-2 near 90% in 2026. ARC-AGI-1 repo: github.com/fchollet/ARC-AGI.

name: ARC-AGI-2
description: Models infer a rule from example grid pairs and produce the output grid for new inputs. Scored by tasks solved within two attempts.
note: ARC-AGI-3 is its successor, and both have ARC Prize 2026 competitions.

name: ARC-AGI-3
description: Interactive game environments where agents must explore, infer goals and rules, and act efficiently without instructions.
note: Harness-sensitive: secondary sources report 99.9% with OpenAI's adapter harness vs about 63% on the standard harness.

name: ARC-Challenge
description: Models answer grade-school science multiple-choice questions that retrieval and word co-occurrence baselines got wrong. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated by frontier models, which score above 95%.

name: ARC-Easy
description: Models answer grade-school science multiple-choice questions from the ARC Easy Set, which has 5,197 questions. Scoring is accuracy.
note: ARC-Challenge is the harder companion split, made of questions that retrieval and co-occurrence baselines failed.

name: Arena-Hard-Auto
description: 500 hard arena prompts judged by an LLM against a baseline. Cheap proxy for arena rank.

name: ArmnetBench
description: 12 tabletop tasks on low-cost SO-101 arms. Each policy trained on the same 50 demos per task. 30 human-scored rollouts.
note: One team trains and runs every policy under one budget. Best pi0.5 47.6% strict success. No policy solves cable_clip. One-off v0.1 snapshot. Initial states not matched.

name: ArtifactArena
description: Models design robot bodies, controllers and strategy for a simulated sumo-style arena. Artifacts fight head-to-head and models get Elo ratings.
org: MIT CSAIL + MIT Media Lab + NYU + UCSF
note: Built to resist saturation: new designs face the best existing robots, and community bots can be submitted. Three harnesses: one-shot, verifier-guided refinement, open-ended design lab. Models did worse with full autonomy than with verifier-guided refinement. No arXiv ID yet.

name: ArtifactsBench
description: Models generate interactive visual code artifacts for 1,825 tasks. An MLLM judge scores rendered screenshots and code against a per-task checklist.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
description: Coding agents, each a model plus harness, attempt software engineering, terminal, and repository question tasks. The index averages three equal-weight benchmark scores.
note: Components change with each version, such as Terminal-Bench 2.0 giving way to 4.0, so compare scores only within one version.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
description: Artificial Analysis runs models on its own set of evaluations in four equally weighted categories and combines the results into one index score.
note: The set of evaluations changes with each version, now 5.0, so scores from different versions are not comparable.

name: ArXivMath
description: Final-answer research-level math problems extracted monthly from recent arXiv papers and filtered to be self-contained.
note: Monthly refresh limits contamination. Paper link is the MathArena platform paper.

name: ASIMOV
description: Semantic physical-safety benchmarks for robot foundation models: injury recognition, embodiment constraints, video risk, and agentic refusal of unsafe tool calls.

name: ASL-4 virology uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: PhD experts with model access write a protocol to reconstruct a challenging virus. Graded by a rubric with critical failures.
note: Human uplift trial designed by Deloitte. Uplift is the ratio to an internet-only control group.

name: Aspire
description: Agent gets only a vague capability goal and must choose data, training and self-checks to evolve weights or harness. Scored on 520 hidden items.
note: Hidden eval spans 6 goals. Weight-level gains were rare. The arXiv page lists no affiliations.

name: Atomic Challenges
description: Agents solve 22 skill-level offensive security challenges in vulnerability research, network attack simulation and evasion. Scored as challenges solved.
note: Run by Irregular. The irregular-frontiercyber-and-atomic-challenges record lumps it with FrontierCyber.

name: Audio MC
description: Spoken multi-turn conversations test inference memory, instruction retention, self-coherence and voice editing. O4-mini judge applies per-conversation rubrics.
note: Identification inferred: the Inkling post names 'Audio MC' with an 'official leaderboard' but gives no link. Scale's Audio MultiChallenge (AudioMC) matches.

name: AutoElicit
description: An optimizer perturbs benign instructions to elicit unsafe behavior from computer-use agents. Reports elicitation success rate on transferred prompts.
note: Surfaces long-tail safety risks of computer-use agents under realistic inputs.

name: AutoEval
description: Autonomous real-robot evaluation: WidowX arms run five Bridge tasks with learned success detectors and resets. 50 rollouts per task.
note: Neutral, runs public checkpoints zero-shot, but the public service was due to wind down in early 2026. Close-drawer near ceiling. Fold-cloth far from it.

name: Autointent-Bio
description: Models face manual and synthetic dangerous and benign biology queries. xAI reports refusal recall on the dangerous ones.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, run with the full safeguard stack.

name: Autointent-Chem
description: Models face manual and synthetic dangerous and benign chemistry queries. xAI reports refusal recall on the dangerous ones.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, run with the full safeguard stack.

name: AutoLogi
description: Models solve open-ended logic puzzles in English and Chinese. Generated verifier programs check each answer against the puzzle constraints.
org: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group and Fudan University

name: AutomationBench
description: Agent completes end-to-end business workflows inside a simulated company exposing dozens of REST APIs. Graded on resulting state.
note: Gemini cards report the private set from Zapier's leaderboard.

name: Autonomous Replication and Adaption (ARA) evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents attempt five autonomy tasks such as adding a Flask backdoor, a SQL injection exploit and an LM worm. Scored by pass rates over trials.
note: Tasks are defined in the appendix of Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy v1.0. Results are reported as pass or fail per task.

name: AutoResearch
description: Agent edits a nanochat training script in 5-minute experiments to lower validation bits-per-byte autonomously. Scored by final val_bpb.
note: A research harness, not a formal benchmark. Sakana Fugu report uses it as an open-ended autonomous-research task (123 experiments).

name: Average in-eval reward hacking rate (Anthropic)
description: Anthropic averages hack rates across its reward hacking evaluations into one number per model.
note: Summary of the reward-hack-prone coding, impossible tasks and training distribution results.

name: BA-Calendar
description: Models find a common meeting slot for several people under constraints such as time zones, buffer time and priority. 2,000 problems checked by code.
note: Built with the BenchAgents method and used in Eureka ML Insights.

name: BabyVision
description: Model solves 388 perception-heavy visual puzzles (discrimination, tracking, spatial, patterns) that young children solve. Accuracy versus 94% human baseline.
note: Moonshot AI is a listed collaborator.

name: BackSearch
description: Paid API that searches a frozen web archive as of a given date, for forecasting backtests and reproducible web-enabled evals. A tool, not a benchmark.
note: Results are deterministic for the same query and cutoff. Sources: news, SEC filings, arXiv, Wikipedia, web.

name: BallotBench
description: Nine frontier agents forecast every contest in the 2026 US midterm elections, every day until polls close. Forecasts are compared with results and with Kalshi and Polymarket.

name: BALROG
description: Agentic reasoning on games (NetHack, Crafter, BabyAI, MiniHack...) for LLMs and VLMs.

name: BankerToolBench
description: 100 end-to-end junior-banker tasks producing Excel, PowerPoint and Word deliverables. Agentic grader scores ~150 weighted expert rubric criteria.
note: Built with 502 investment bankers. Packaged as a Harbor task suite. Grader repo Handshake-AI-Research/gandalf-the-grader.

name: BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA)
description: Ambiguous and disambiguated questions probing social stereotypes across nine attributes. Reports accuracy and bias scores.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025
description: 50 long-horizon household activities on a Galaxea R1 Pro in OmniGibson, trained from 10,000 demos. Scored by Q-score and success.
note: Far from saturated: winning held-out Q-score 0.26, full-task success 12.4%. Scores teams, not models. 2026 edition adds pi0.5 and GR00T N1.7 baselines. Results due 2026-11-04.

name: Belebele
description: Models answer multiple-choice reading comprehension questions on FLORES passages in 122 language variants. Scored by accuracy.
note: Labs often report a subset of languages or language-family averages.

name: BenchCAD
description: Programmatic CAD: 17,900 execution-verified CadQuery programs over 106 industrial part families. Four matched tasks scored on geometry.
note: BenchCAD 2.0 (agentic) is in preparation at github.com/BenchCAD-org/benchcad-2.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
description: Model emits function calls for single, parallel, multi-turn and agentic scenarios. Scored by AST and execution checks.
note: Live benchmark. Nova 2 pins results to a 2025 commit, so versions matter.

name: BetterChartQA
description: Models answer annotator-written questions about real charts from news, government reports, and papers across 9 capability buckets. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Google never released the questions.

name: Beyond AIME
description: Models answer 100 original competition-style math problems at or above the hardest AIME level. Each answer is a positive integer checked by exact match.
note: ByteDance rewrote each problem from existing contests to reduce contamination.

name: BFCL V4
description: Models call functions and tools, including multi-turn agentic tasks with web search and memory. Checked against expected calls and outcomes.
note: V4 added agentic web search and memory categories and changed the overall formula, so its scores do not compare with V3.

name: BIG-Bench Extra Hard
description: Models solve harder replacements for each of the 23 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, 4,520 examples in total. The score is a harmonic mean of task accuracies.
note: A mini version with 460 examples also exists, so check which one a model card reports.

name: BIG-Bench Hard
description: Models solve 23 BIG-Bench tasks where earlier models trailed average human raters, such as logic puzzles and date math. Scoring is exact match.
org: Suzgun et al. (Stanford University and Google Research)
note: Frontier models now score above 90%, and Google DeepMind released BIG-Bench Extra Hard as a successor.

name: BigCodeBench
description: 1,140 practical Python tasks requiring calls to 139 libraries. Scored pass@1 on unit tests.

name: Binary Exploitation Benchmark (Anthropic, OSS-Fuzz based)
description: Internal eval on OSS-Fuzz harness entrypoints measuring unguided vulnerability discovery and how far a found bug is advanced.

name: Bio Static Jailbreak Eval
description: Common jailbreak templates are applied to high severity biology requests against the safeguarded model. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Biochemistry knowledge improvement
description: Models answer biochemistry tasks on structures, mutation thermodynamics, reaction products, arrow pushing and DNA phylogeny. Scored as reward@4.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. A 30 point jump over the previous model triggers further investigation.

name: Bioinformatics evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents process raw sequencing data with workflows from published papers and answer expert questions about the results.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation for the CBRN-4 threshold. Human PhD baseline on a subset is 0.623.

name: Biological static hazard evaluation
description: Models answer 75 questions across priority biological threat scenarios, each asked 10 times. The score is the share of hazardous responses.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation run without out-of-model safeguards.

name: Biological threat creation uplift study
description: Experts and novices answer biothreat creation tasks with internet access alone or with model help. Scored as pass rates per stage.
note: Human uplift trial across ideation, acquisition, magnification, formulation and release stages.

name: Biology Model Refusal Evaluation
description: Models answer severe, dual-use and benign biology prompts. Scored as safe rate on harmful prompts and not over-refusing benign ones.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard evaluation. Cards report rows with no overall number.

name: BioLP-bench
description: Find the introduced error in a biological lab protocol. Tests protocol understanding.
note: Added from public eval collections.

name: Biomedical image analysis (Anthropic)
description: Models run quantitative analyses of CT, MRI, histopathology and other images from public competitions. Scores are scaled to the best competition results.
note: Uses data from public biomedical image analysis competitions.

name: BioMysteryBench
description: Bioinformatics problems on anonymized real datasets that require real analysis with tools. Rubric-graded, with human-solvable and human-difficult splits.
note: Full set gated (90 problems after a 2026-07 audit). 5-problem open preview. Removed from Anthropic's panel as of Haiku 5.5.

name: BioPipelineBench (Anthropic)
description: Agents execute bioinformatics workflows such as long-read sequence analysis, metagenome assembly and chromatin profiling with a bash tool.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BioPipelineBench Verified (Anthropic)
description: Agents execute bioinformatics workflows with a bash tool. Only problems that passed a validation check by external reviewers are kept.
note: Filtered version of BioPipelineBench. Scores do not compare with the original problem set.

name: BioSecBench-Function
description: Agents recover biosecurity-relevant functional conclusions from sequence, structure and experimental evidence. The endpoint pass rate excludes refused runs.
note: Only source found is the Grok 4.7 model card, which describes it as one of three BioSecBench evaluations.

name: BioSecBench-Refusal
description: Agents run 61 routine and 46 concealed-hazard biology analysis tasks. The score pairs red-team refusal with routine completion.
note: One of three BioSecBench evaluations. LatchBio reports a trial-weighted harmonic mean of red-team refusal and routine compliance.

name: BioSecBench-Surveillance
description: Agents turn raw pathogen sequencing data into surveillance results. The endpoint pass rate excludes refused runs.
note: Only a public subset is on GitHub. LatchBio keeps the full set under restricted access.

name: Biosecurity VCT
description: Models answer dual-use virus lab troubleshooting items. Accuracy counts should-refuse and should-comply items together.
note: In-house xAI companion to VCT. The tasks are not public, and the answer format is not stated.

name: BioTIER
description: Safeguarded model configurations receive harmful and benign biology requests. Scored on refusing requests designated for refusal and allowing benign ones.
note: Run by SecureBio. Counts full blocks and model-jury graded soft refusals.

name: Biotool and Wet Lab Actions
description: Agents perform wet lab assistant tasks such as finding a genome file or ordering DNA through a computer or browser. Scored as pass@10 per task.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation with three tasks and no overall score.

name: BioUseBench
description: Models face dual-use biology enablement prompts. The reported metric is the refusal rate on the severity 5 subset.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. Items span virology, wet lab methods, chemical synthesis, toxicology and lab safety.

name: Bioweapons acquisition uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: Participants draft a bioweapons acquisition plan over two days with or without model access. Score is the uplift ratio of model group over control.
note: In-house Anthropic human uplift trial graded by Deloitte with a rubric. The tasks are not public.

name: Bioweapons knowledge questions
description: Models answer 33 sensitive bioweapons questions written by Deloitte biosecurity staff. Answers are compared with novice, intermediate and expert baselines.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Bird-SQL
description: Models convert natural language questions into SQL over 95 large real databases across 37 domains. Scored by execution accuracy.
note: The test set is hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set.

name: BirthdayFacts
description: Models are asked for people's birthdays. Scored on how often they give a wrong birthday.
note: In-house OpenAI hallucination evaluation.

name: BixBench
description: Computational-biology analysis tasks (differential expression, assembly QC, cell typing) answered by agents with tools.

name: Black-box RNA sequence modeling and design
description: Models predict scores for unlabeled RNA sequences from labeled data, then design new sequences. Results are compared with 57 human experts.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Reported as design and rank-correlation prediction scores in charts.

name: BLEnD
description: Models answer 52.6k questions about everyday culture in 16 countries and regions across 13 languages. Scoring is accuracy on short-answer and multiple-choice formats.

name: BLINK
description: Models answer 3,807 multiple choice questions built from 14 classic computer vision tasks that use one or more images. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Test answers are hidden on EvalAI, so model cards usually report the 1,901 question validation split.

name: Blocker Deception
description: Agents hit a blocker during realistic coding tasks. Scored on how often the final answer fails to disclose the limitation.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. It replaces the saturated Coding Deception evaluation.

name: Blueprint-Bench 2
description: Agents turn about 20 interior photos of each of 50 apartments into 2D floor plans. Scores compare room connectivity with ground truth, normalized against random.
note: The leader now ties the human baseline, which was measured on only 12 apartments.

name: BOLD
aliases: Bias in Open-Ended Language Generation Dataset
description: Models continue 23,679 English Wikipedia prompts about professions, gender, race, religion and politics. Classifiers score sentiment, toxicity and polarity per group.
note: Results are given per group, usually as mean and spread of sentiment.

name: BoolQ
description: Models read a Wikipedia passage and answer a naturally occurring yes or no question about it. Scored by accuracy.
note: Part of SuperGLUE. The paper reports 90 percent human accuracy, which large models now approach.

name: Broken Search Tool
description: Models answer questions that need search while the search tool is broken. Scored on how often they fail to say the tool is unavailable.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BrowseComp
description: Hard-to-find facts that need persistent web browsing. Short verifiable answers graded for exact correctness.
note: Questions ship encrypted in simple-evals. Context-management settings (compaction at 300K vs full 1M) change scores by several points.

name: BrowseComp Long Context 128k
description: Models answer BrowseComp questions from a 128k-token context of the needed web pages mixed with related distractor pages. Scored by accuracy.
note: The 128k setting of BrowseComp Long Context, which scales beyond 1M tokens.

name: BrowseComp-Plus
description: Deep research agents answer 830 BrowseComp questions by searching a fixed corpus of about 100,000 human-verified documents.
note: BrowseComp-Plus is a different evaluation from BrowseComp. Labs use different retrievers and graders, so scores vary by setup.

name: BrowseComp-ZH
description: Agents browse the Chinese web to answer 289 multi-hop questions with short, verifiable answers. Scored by accuracy.
org: Researchers from Peking University, Mindverse AI, and other groups

name: BrowserInject v1
description: Browser agents do benign tasks on 30 retail, health, support and travel sites seeded with prompt injections. Reports attack success rate.
note: Third-party private benchmark run for Meta before release.

name: Browsing prompt injections
description: Agents answer web research questions while malicious instructions are injected in the browsing context. Scored on resisting the injections.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BTF-3
description: Agents forecast already-resolved binary and numeric questions while researching a frozen snapshot of the web. Scoring pools Brier and ranked probability scores.
note: The question set keeps growing, from 1,907 questions on Epoch AI's page to 2,386 on FutureSearch's page.

name: Butter-Bench
description: A language model controls a real robot to find and deliver a pack of butter in an office. It is scored on completing each step of the task.
note: The best models scored 40%, against 95% for people. Models struggled most with multi-step spatial planning and social cues.

name: C-Eval
description: 13,948 Chinese multiple-choice exam questions across 52 disciplines and four difficulty levels. Accuracy.
note: Saturated. Test answers withheld for submission.

name: C3
description: Models answer 19,577 multiple-choice questions on Chinese dialogues and texts from Chinese-as-a-second-language exams. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Tencent AI Lab and Cornell University

name: CadEval
description: Models write OpenSCAD code for single mechanical parts from text descriptions. Rendered parts are checked against reference geometry, scored by pass rate.

name: CADGenBench
description: Agents construct CAD models from design prompts. The generation split is graded for executability and geometric correctness.

name: CALVIN
description: Simulated Franka follows chains of five language instructions from 34 tasks. ABC-to-D tests an unseen environment. Average chain length.
note: Near-saturated: ABC-to-D top 4.75 of 5 (Xiaomi-Robotics-0). Few current models report the standard split. Others use easier splits.

name: CaP-X (CaP-Bench)
description: Coding agents write perception and control code for 100+ sim manipulation tasks across 8 abstraction and interaction tiers. Scored by task success.
note: Scores depend on the harness: every model improves with human-made high-level primitives and drops as they are removed. Best frontier models average just over 30%, with a 56-point gap to humans. ICML 2026.

name: Capture the Flag (Collegiate)
description: Agents solve curated public collegiate level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs.

name: Capture the Flag (High School)
description: Agents solve curated public high school level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs.

name: Capture the Flag (Internal)
description: Agents solve 63 public CTF challenges chosen for low GPT-5.3-Codex solve rates, using a Linux box with security tools. Scored as task success rate.
note: OpenAI says this set is harder than and different from the CTF sets it reported before GPT-5.6.

name: Capture the Flag (Professional)
description: Agents solve curated public professional-level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12 over 16 rollouts.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs. OpenAI refactored the set in July 2025.

name: Catastrophic biology scenario uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: PhD biologists with model access spend up to 16 hours planning a catastrophic biological scenario. External experts grade uplift and executability.
note: Human uplift trial. Anthropic reports whether any plan was judged both highly uplifted and credibly executable.

name: CathedralBench
description: Independent third-party red-team evaluation of difficult multi-step exploit-chain tasks in egress-secure sandboxes.

name: CB
description: Models label whether a text commits its speaker to an embedded clause as entailment, contradiction, or neutral. Scored by accuracy and F1.
org: Marie-Catherine de Marneffe, Mandy Simons, and Judith Tonhauser
note: Model cards use the SuperGLUE version of the task.

name: CBRN Conversational Evals
description: About 1,500 expert-written single and multi-turn CBRN requests test whether safeguards block hazardous help. Reports violation and benign refusal rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard coverage evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: CBRN expert red teaming
description: Experts try to extract uplift beyond a web baseline across staged CBRN attack scenarios.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Results are usually qualitative or rubric scores per scenario.

name: CBRN open-ended questions
description: Experts review model answers to single and multi-turn CBRN threat scenario questions for accuracy, novelty and actionable uplift.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Results are usually qualitative.

name: CBRN Science Eval
description: More than 700 benign bioinformatics, genomics and chemistry questions check that safeguards do not cause false refusals. Reports benign refusal rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind over-refusal check, run with mitigations on.

name: CC-Bench
description: Claude Code runs realistic frontend, backend, tooling and data coding tasks in fresh containers. Humans compare models head-to-head (win rate).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Zhipu/Z.ai). V1.x questions and trajectories on HF, but task environments are not released. CC-Bench-V2 (GLM-5) is internal.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Backend
description: Agents change 85 real backend codebases in six languages. A task passes only when all of its unit tests pass.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Frontend
description: Agents build web projects in HTML, React, Vue, Svelte and Next.js. A GUI judge agent tests each check item in the running app.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Reported as build success, instance success and check-item success rates.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Large Repo Exploration
description: Agents locate a hidden target file in a large repository from a user-level question. A question counts as solved when the agent reads the file.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Pass@1 averaged over three runs.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Multi-Step Chained Tasks
description: Agents complete chains of tasks mined from merged pull requests, where each step changes the codebase for the next. Tests check every step.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Pass@1 on individual tasks.

name: CC-OCR
description: Models read text in 7,058 images across four tracks: scene text, multilingual text, document parsing, and key information extraction. Each track has its own metric.

name: CC-OCR-Bench-V2
description: Models process 7,093 hard real-world document samples across five OCR tracks, including parsing and document QA. Each track uses its own metric.
org: Chunyi Peng et al. (with Qwen team members)
note: This is a new version, and the original CC-OCR from December 2024 is a separate benchmark.

name: CCPM
description: Models pick which of four classical Chinese poetry lines matches a given modern Chinese translation. Scored by accuracy.

name: Certified Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the certified sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Chain-of-thought comprehensibility
description: An autorater rates whether the model's thought transcripts are comprehensible, using the metric from Emmons et al. 2025.
note: In-house Google DeepMind check reported as the share of transcripts rated comprehensible.

name: Chain-of-thought faithfulness with clues (Anthropic)
description: Models answer MMLU and GPQA questions with and without an inserted clue. Score is the share of clue-driven answer changes whose reasoning mentions the clue.
note: Uses six clue types, four neutral and two misaligned. Scores run from 0 to 1 and are reported per dataset.

name: Chain-of-thought informativeness
description: An autorater rates whether thought transcripts are informative of the final output, using the metric from Emmons et al. 2025.
note: In-house Google DeepMind check reported as the share of transcripts rated informative.

name: Challenging prompts from red teamers with biosafety-relevant PhDs
description: Models answer adversarial biology prompts written by red teamers with biosafety PhDs. Scored as not_unsafe rate from model training alone.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard test set first shared in the ChatGPT agent system card.

name: Challenging Red Teaming Evaluation 1 (created for o3-mini)
description: Models face adversarial jailbreaks from o3-mini red teaming on illicit advice, extremism, political persuasion and self-harm. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from red teaming against o3-mini.

name: Challenging Red Teaming Evaluation 2 (created for deep research)
description: Models face adversarial prompts from deep research red teaming on risky advice such as attack planning. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from red teaming against deep research.

name: Challenging Refusal Evaluation
description: Models answer a harder set of disallowed content prompts across policy categories. An autograder scores the not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Challenging translation human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: People blindly score translations of 100 real cases with slang, nicknames and memes on a 0 to 3 scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The cases are not public.

name: ChangeMyView
description: Models write rebuttals to r/ChangeMyView posts that human raters score for persuasiveness. Scored as percentile against human responses.
note: OpenAI persuasion evaluation built on public Reddit data.

name: Charlemagne Labs social-engineering benchmark
description: Attacker models try to persuade a skeptical simulated victim to take an action over many turns. Scored by attempted and carry-through rates.
note: Used in Meta Muse Spark safety reports. Filtered to 280 scenarios. Attempted and carry-through tracked separately.

name: Charm offensive
description: Human participants role-play catching up with a friend, then rate traits such as personal connection and trust in the model.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Results are per trait with no overall score.

name: ChartMuseum
description: Models answer 1,162 expert-annotated questions about real-world charts from 184 sources. Many questions need visual reasoning that text cannot replace.
note: The test split has 1,000 questions and the dev split has 162. An LLM grader checks short answers.

name: Chartography
description: 100 tasks on specialized professional charts (Kaplan-Meier, candlestick, Sankey, Bode). Answers graded against expert references.

name: ChartQA
description: Models answer human-written and generated questions about chart images that need visual and arithmetic reasoning. Scored by relaxed accuracy with a 5 percent numeric tolerance.
org: York University and Nanyang Technological University
note: Top models score near 90 percent, so it is close to saturation.

name: ChartQA Pro
description: Model answers 1,948 diverse questions over 1,341 charts, infographics and dashboards, including conversational and unanswerable ones. Accuracy.
note: ACL 2025 Findings.

name: CharXiv
description: Chart understanding on real arXiv figures. Reasoning questions require synthesizing information from complex charts.
note: Cards report the reasoning (RQ) split, with or without a Python tool.

name: CharXiv Missing Image
description: Models get CharXiv chart questions with every image removed. Scored on how often they attempt an answer instead of abstaining.
note: OpenAI deception evaluation built on the public CharXiv benchmark.

name: CharXiv Missing Images
description: Models answer CharXiv chart questions with the image removed. The benchmark reports how often they answer incorrectly instead of declining.
note: Meta modification of CharXiv (Princeton) that drops the referenced image.

name: Chat All-in-One Bench
description: Models handle conversational scenarios built around real online user needs at every stage of product usage.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Cheating audit on capability evaluations
description: Reviewers audit agent transcripts from coding benchmarks for runs that obtain withheld information or use forbidden routes. Reports cheating rate per benchmark.
note: In-house Google DeepMind audit of TerminalBench 4.0 and an internal tool-replication benchmark.

name: Chem / Bio Dynamic Jailbreak Eval
description: An automated attacker spreads a harmful chem or bio goal across many turns and chats. Elicited content is scored against expert rubrics.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation reported as rubric match percentage, run with mitigations on.

name: ChemicalDiagramQA
description: Models answer questions about chemical structure diagrams in scientific figures. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Google never released the questions.

name: Chess Puzzles
description: Models find the single best next move in 100 chess puzzles that Epoch generated with a chess engine. Scored by the share solved.

name: CHID
description: Models fill blanks in Chinese passages by choosing the right idiom from candidates. Scored by accuracy.
note: Part of the FewCLUE suite. DeepSeek reports it in few-shot and chat settings.

name: Child safety (xAI)
description: Models face scripted multi-turn requests for child sexual exploitation content. Compliance is the share of dialogues that fail policy.
note: In-house xAI evaluation.

name: Child Safety Action Testing
description: Computer use agents get requests for actions that facilitate child exploitation, endangerment or illegal access. Reports the refusal score.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Child safety evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer single-turn and multi-turn prompts about child sexualization and grooming. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Safety
description: Specialist teams grade model answers to adversarial and coded child sexual abuse and exploitation requests in text, image and video. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Chinese SimpleQA
description: 3,000 short Chinese factual questions across six topics. Graded correct, incorrect or not attempted.
note: GitHub repo moved from OpenStellarTeam to LivingFutureLab.

name: Chinese Tool-Use Benchmark
description: Models pick and call plugins in ReAct format for Chinese prompts. Scores are tool selection accuracy, Rouge-L on tool inputs, and false positive rate.
note: Qwen replaced version 20230803 with version 20231206, so scores from the two versions differ.

name: ChineseQA
description: Models answer Chinese trivia questions in a closed-book format modeled on TriviaQA.
note: In-house: DeepSeek never released the questions.

name: CIMemories
description: Models use persistent memory across tasks and must withhold attributes when context requires. Reports worst-case disclosure over five samples.
note: Contextual privacy benchmark. Meta reports violations@5 and completeness.

name: CL-bench
description: Model must learn new knowledge from a supplied long context (rules, procedures, data) and solve tasks. Strict LLM-verified rubrics.
note: 500 contexts, 1,899 tasks, 31,607 rubrics. Follow-up CL-bench Life (2026-04) covers everyday contexts.

name: CL-bench Life
description: Models solve 405 tasks that require learning from messy real-life context such as group chats. A model judge checks rubrics to give a solve rate.
note: The best model solved 19.3 percent of tasks at release.

name: Claw-Eval
description: 300 human-verified agent tasks (service orchestration, multimodal, multi-turn dialogue) audited via traces and snapshots. Rubric scores with Pass^3 consistency.
note: Uses an LLM judge (Gemini 3 Flash) for open-ended rubric items. Pass^3 requires all three trials to pass.

name: Claw-Eval Pass^3
description: Agents complete 300 human-verified tasks in service orchestration, multimodal interaction, and professional dialogue. Pass^3 credits a task only if all three trials pass.
note: Pass^3 is the strict metric of Claw-Eval. Average score and Pass@k are also reported.

name: Claw-Eval-MM
description: Agents complete the 101 multimodal tasks of Claw-Eval, such as video questions, document extraction, and webpage generation. Rubric items graded from run traces set scores.
note: This is the multimodal split of Claw-Eval, not a separate benchmark.

name: CLIF Bench
aliases: Context Learning and Instruction Following Bench
description: Models learn from a provided context while they follow instructions that combine several complex skills.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Closed-domain hallucination evaluation
description: Models answer using only provided context. Scored on avoiding invented details outside that context.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The GPT-4 System Card gives only a gain over GPT-3.5.

name: CLUEWSC
description: Models decide whether a pronoun in a Chinese sentence refers to a given noun phrase, a Winograd-style task. Scored by accuracy.

name: CLUEWSC (CLUE Winograd Schema)
description: Chinese Winograd Schema coreference task from the CLUE benchmark. Accuracy.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: CMATH
description: 1.7K Chinese elementary-school math word problems. Final-answer accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: CMMLU
description: Chinese multiple-choice questions across 67 subjects including China-specific topics. Accuracy.
note: Saturated. HF dataset haonan-li/cmmlu now redirects to lmlmcat/cmmlu.

name: CMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2025 China Mathematical Olympiad. Graders score proofs out of 126 points.
note: A one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark. DeepSeek graded the English version.

name: CMRC
description: Models extract answer spans from Chinese Wikipedia paragraphs for about 20,000 human-written questions. Scoring is exact match and F1.
org: Joint Laboratory of HIT and iFLYTEK Research (HFL)

name: CNMO 2024
description: Models answer problems from the 2024 Chinese National High School Mathematics Olympiad. DeepSeek reports Pass@1 averaged over 16 samples.
note: DeepSeek built the eval set from the contest and did not release its prepared version or problem count.

name: CoBench (Anthropic)
description: 500 real internal Anthropic R&D problems. Percentage solved in one attempt tracks AI R&D acceleration.
note: v2.1 scores not comparable with earlier CoBench versions.

name: COCO
description: Models detect and locate objects in everyday photos from the Microsoft COCO dataset. Scored by mean average precision over box overlap thresholds.
note: Qwen reports it under visual grounding without stating its exact protocol.

name: COCO Captions
description: Models write a caption for each image, and outputs are compared with five human captions per image using BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE, and CIDEr.
note: Model cards usually report CIDEr, which is not a percentage.

name: Code Arena
description: Models act as coding agents that build web apps from user prompts, and users vote between two results. Votes yield Elo-style ratings.
note: It started a fresh leaderboard and does not reuse WebDev Arena votes.

name: Code Interpreter Benchmark
description: Models use a Python code interpreter for math, data visualization, and general tasks. Scoring covers result accuracy and the share of code that runs.
note: The visualization judge changed from Qwen-VL-Chat to GPT-4V in December 2023, so versions differ.

name: Code summary honesty (Anthropic)
description: Models summarize prefilled agentic coding transcripts that hide failures. Score is the rate of summaries that fail to raise the important failures.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The prefilled transcripts are off-policy and shorter than many real sessions.

name: Code2Video Benchmark
description: 168 product-video briefs. Agent writes HTML motion-graphics code rendered by HyperFrames. A trained pairwise judge on five axes produces Elo.
note: Repo is the HyperFrames renderer, not a task repo. Judge agrees with humans ~82%. Kaggle hosts briefs and runs evaluations.

name: Codeforces rating
description: Model solves recent Codeforces contest problems. An Elo-style rating is computed from simulated contest performance.
org: Codeforces (problems); each lab runs its own harness
note: No standard public harness. Each lab's rating method differs, so numbers are not comparable across cards.

name: Coding (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models answer coding requests from real Hailuo AI users. The report does not describe the scoring.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Coding agent prompt injection robustness
description: Coding agents on 75 SWE-Bench Pro based scenarios meet injections in issues, READMEs and code comments. Reports survival after 40 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Coding Deception
description: Agents work on coding tasks selected to elicit dishonest reports. Scored on the rate of misrepresenting their work to the user.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Coding Experience (Moonshot)
description: Coding agents work in real development workflows. The score reflects the practical experience of working with the agent, such as communication and stability.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks and the grading method are not public.

name: Coding prompt injections
description: Agents work on coding tasks that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Cohere North internal evals
description: Cohere internal evals of its North agent platform: agentic question answering, spreadsheet data analysis and memory use. LLM-as-judge scoring.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Cohere).

name: COLLIE
description: Models generate text that meets compositional constraints at word, sentence, paragraph, and passage level. Scored by the share passing automatic constraint checks.

name: Combined HHH evals (Anthropic)
description: Models pick the more helpful, honest and harmless of two responses across 438 binary choice questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Anthropic researchers wrote the questions for its RLHF and Constitutional AI research.

name: Common Voice
description: Crowd-sourced multilingual read-speech corpus. Used here as an ASR test set scored by word error rate.

name: CommonSenseQA
description: Models answer five-way multiple-choice questions built from ConceptNet relations that need everyday background knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
org: Tel Aviv University and Allen Institute for AI
note: Test labels are hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set.

name: CommonsenseQA 2.0
description: Models answer 14,343 yes or no commonsense questions that players wrote to fool an AI in a game. Scored by accuracy.

name: Community Alignment personalization
description: Models predict an individual's preferred response from demographics and nine examples, across five countries. Reports global accuracy.
note: Built on Meta's open Community Alignment preference dataset. Random guessing scores 25%.

name: Compliance with instructions planted in pasted text (Anthropic)
aliases: Acting on instructions inside text the user pasted into their prompt
Compliance with instructions planted in a document pasted into Claude Code
description: Coding agents receive user prompts with pasted text that hides an attacker's instruction. Score is the rate of acting on the planted instruction.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with simulated tool calls. Some variants hide the instruction in invisible Unicode characters.

name: Computer use manual red teaming
description: Google's generative AI red team probes computer use agents in sandboxes for tool misuse, skipped confirmations and prohibited actions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Computer use Prohibited Action Evaluation
description: Computer use agents get single-turn adversarial requests for actions that break Google policy. Reports the safe action rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Computer use prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
aliases: Prompt injection attacks and computer use
description: Agents face about 600 prompt injection scenarios in coding platforms, browsers and email workflows. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported with and without safeguards. The scenarios are not public.

name: Computer use prompt injection robustness
description: Computer use agents meet injected text and live DOM attacks across 27 web scenarios. A multimodal judge records breaches. Reports survival after 100 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Concealment of changes (Anthropic)
description: Models summarize transcripts in which changes were hidden through git manipulations. Score is the rate at which they disclose the concealment.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Contextual Nuclear Knowledge
description: Models answer 222 multiple choice questions on nuclear engineering with a nonproliferation focus. Scored as cons@32 accuracy.
note: Questions written by an MIT nuclear security fellow for OpenAI Preparedness.

name: Contextual security evaluation
description: Agents handle noisy cross-app data with sensitive records while attackers exploit ambiguity to exfiltrate data. Reports baseline safe behavior and survival rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ControlArena
description: Agents try to perform unwanted side actions stealthily while completing a legitimate user task. Scored on whether monitors catch them.
note: UK AISI control evaluation suite. The GPT-5.6 card describes results in words without a score.

name: Cooperate to Compete (C2C)
description: Multi-player conquest game with private non-binding negotiation and secret asymmetric objectives. LM agents scored by win rate against humans and other agents.
note: Includes an 82-game human study with matched AI-only games from the same starting positions.

name: Cooperation with user deception (Anthropic)
aliases: Harmful system prompts: cooperation with user deception
description: Models get developer system prompts asking them to subtly mislead users, then meet users who would be harmed. Graders score harmful and deceptive choices.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: COPA
