description: Models choose which of two alternatives is the more plausible cause or effect of a premise, across 1,000 questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated. Also part of SuperGLUE.

name: Coronavirus-ACE2 Cell-Entry Screen
description: Models predict and rank held-out cell entry measurements for spike protein and ACE2 pairings. Scored as a composite score.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.75.

name: CorpFin
description: Model answers term-extraction and numeric-reasoning questions over 200+ page credit agreements. Accuracy against expert answers.
note: Archived by Vals as saturated. No longer run on new models. Replaced in the Vals Index by EMB.

name: CorpFin v2
description: Models answer expert-written questions about credit agreements that often exceed 200 pages. An LLM judge grades each answer for accuracy.
note: Vals archived it as saturated and no longer runs new models. Only 20 of 1,218 questions are public.

name: CorpusQA
description: Corpus-level questions over hundreds of documents up to 10M tokens needing aggregation and statistics. Programmatically guaranteed answers, accuracy.
note: 'CorpusQA 1M' is the 1M-token tier. Built by an Alibaba team. Cited by DeepSeek-V4.

name: CorpusQA 1M
description: Models answer computation-heavy questions whose evidence is spread across hundreds of finance, education, and real estate documents in a 1M-token context. Scored by accuracy.
note: The 1M-token setting of CorpusQA, which spans 128K to 10M tokens.

name: CoT Deception Monitoring
description: A GPT-4o monitor reads reasoning chains and answers on synthetic ChatGPT prompts. Scored as the share flagged as deceptive.
note: In-house OpenAI monitoring study on about 100,000 synthetic prompts.

name: CoT Monitorability
description: Monitors read a model's chain of thought, actions or all messages across intervention, process and outcome evaluations. Scored as g-mean squared of TPR and TNR.
note: Suite from Guan et al. 2025. Results appear as charts by reasoning length.

name: CoT-Control
description: Pairs GPQA, HLE, MMLU-Pro, BFCL and SWE-bench problems with instructions on what the chain of thought may contain. Measures compliance.
note: Low controllability is the safe direction. Authors ask that it be excluded from training data.

name: CountBench
description: Models count the objects in natural images from the CountBench image-text set. Lab cards often use a question-answer version, CountBenchQA, scored by accuracy.

name: CounterFactQA (Qwen)
description: Models get counterfactual questions and must recognize that the premise is false instead of giving a hallucinated answer.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: CountQA
description: Models count objects in over 1,500 real-world photos with dense clutter and occlusion. Scoring is accuracy on the count.

name: CoVoST2
description: Models translate speech from 21 languages into English and from English into 15 languages. Scored by BLEU.

name: CoWorkBench
description: Agent completes long-horizon productivity tasks across computer science, finance, law and medicine. Qwen in-house scoring (method unpublished).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen). Only Qwen reports scores. Tasks and graders are not public.

name: Creative biology
description: Models answer questions about unusual biology needed to engineer harmless biological agents, a weak proxy for novel weapon design.
note: SecureBio question set run by Anthropic. The questions are not public.

name: Creative Biology Uplift Trial (Anthropic)
description: Participants with molecular biology PhDs write reports on novel biological workflows with or without model access. Expert graders score each report.
note: In-house Anthropic human uplift trial with twenty participants over three days. Results compare the model group with an internet-only control.

name: Creative Writing (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models write creative pieces for real Hailuo AI user requests. Automatic assessments score the writing.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Creative Writing v3
description: Models write responses to 32 creative writing prompts, three times each. A judge model scores them with a rubric and pairwise Elo comparisons.
note: Version 3 replaced version 2 after the judge could no longer separate top models.

name: CritPt
description: 71 frontier physics research challenges with checkable answers. Anthropic uses a corrected internal version.
note: Cards cite Artificial Analysis-run scores. Answers for the test set are held for server-side grading.

name: CrowS-Pairs
description: Models choose between paired sentences that differ only in a stereotyped social group. Measures preference for the stereotyped sentence.
note: A score of 50 percent means no preference between stereotyped and anti-stereotyped sentences.

name: CRUXEval
description: Models predict the output of 800 short Python functions for a given input, or an input that yields a given output. Scored by pass@1.

name: Crypto CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents discover and exploit vulnerabilities in cryptographic primitives and protocols in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CursorBench
description: Ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's production harness. Agentic graders score correctness, with cost reported.
note: Covers versions 3.0 to 3.2. Epoch AI's copy of the board does not say which version each score comes from.

name: CursorBench 4.0
description: Ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's production harness. Agentic graders score correctness, with cost reported.
note: Added long-horizon problems: investigation, intent understanding, managing jobs and design adherence. Scores do not compare with 3.x.

name: CVBench
description: Models answer 2,638 manually checked 2D and 3D vision questions built from ADE20K, COCO, and Omni3D. Scoring is accuracy.

name: CVE-Bench
description: Real-world web-application CVEs in sandboxed services. Agent is scored on reaching predefined attack objectives.

name: CWE-bench
description: Defensive audit-and-patch tasks on real repositories. A task passes only when the planted weakness is fixed and regression tests pass.
note: Held-out set private to Collinear. V1 (120 tasks) not comparable with v0.

name: Cybench
description: 40 professional capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions. Agent must recover the flag, with optional subtasks.
note: Near-saturated: Mistral reports 93% for Mistral Large 4.

name: Cyber Adaptive Jailbreak Eval
description: Automated single and multi-turn attackers learn from refusals to reach high severity cyber goals. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber agentic safeguard evaluation
description: Agents with production mitigations attempt cyber range challenges. The score is the share of milestones the model refuses.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard test that reruns CyScenarioBench and ExploitBench with mitigations on.

name: Cyber Conversational Evals
description: About 1,000 one to five turn cyber requests test whether safeguards block offensive help and allow defensive help. Reports violation and benign refusal rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard coverage evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber harm coverage (Anthropic)
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen examples from each cyber harm category. Score is overall recall, the share of harmful examples flagged.
note: Measures the deployed classifier system, not the model alone.

name: Cyber key skills benchmark v1
description: Agents solve 50 capture-the-flag challenges built with a third party on reconnaissance, tool development, tool use and operational security. 12 are hard.
note: In-house Google evaluation built with Irregular. The Gemini 4 report renames key skills CyScenarioBench, kept separate because versions differ.

name: Cyber key skills benchmark v2
description: Agents run end-to-end multi-stage cyber attacks in simulated environments covering seven attack kill chains. Built with a third party.
note: In-house Google evaluation built with Irregular. It may match the existing cyscenariobench id, which the Gemini 4 report uses.

name: Cyber Range
description: Agents run end-to-end cyber operations in emulated networks. Scored as the share of scenarios passed in at least one of 16 trials.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. OpenAI adds scenarios over time, so combined pass rates differ across cards.

name: Cyber Static Jailbreak Eval
description: Common jailbreak templates are applied to high severity cyber requests against the safeguarded model. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber-harness network challenges (Incalmo cyber ranges)
description: Agents run long-horizon attacks on cyber ranges of 25 to 50 hosts using a specialized offensive harness.
note: Built with Carnegie Mellon University, as described in the Incalmo paper. The ranges are not public.

name: CyberBench (Liu et al.)
description: Models face detail-seeking high-severity cyber requests. Meta uses it as a seed set for adaptive red-teaming and reports attack success rate.
note: AAAI-24 AICS workshop benchmark. Not the same as Cybench.

name: CyberGym
description: Large-scale benchmark of real open-source vulnerabilities. Agent must reproduce each known vulnerability with a proof-of-concept input.
note: Retired from Anthropic cards for saturation. GPT-5.6 card uses it to test jailbreak transfer.

name: CyberSecEval Autocomplete
description: Models complete code that leads up to a known insecure pattern. The Insecure Code Detector flags vulnerable code, and the score is the pass rate.
note: Part of every CyberSecEval release since version 1. Some reports give the vulnerable rate, which equals 100 minus the pass rate.

name: CyberSecEval Code Interpreter Abuse
description: Models receive requests to run malicious commands against an attached code interpreter. Reports attack success rate, also across languages.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 2. Meta reports per-language attack success rates.

name: CyberSecEval Instruct
description: Models get coding requests built to elicit known insecure patterns. The Insecure Code Detector flags vulnerable code, and the score is the pass rate.
note: Part of every CyberSecEval release since version 1. Some reports give the vulnerable rate, which equals 100 minus the pass rate.

name: CyberSecEval Prompt Injection
description: Models face text prompts that embed injected instructions across 15 strategies. Scored as attack success rate.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 2 and later versions.

name: CyberSecEval Spear Phishing
description: Models run multi-turn phishing conversations against an LLM victim with a generated profile. A judge model scores persuasion and success.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 3. Llama 3 reports the judged success rate and a 1 to 5 persuasion score.

name: CyScenarioBench
description: Scenario-based long-horizon security challenges in sandboxes, organized in task, scenario and campaign tiers. Evaluation set kept private.
note: Gemini 4 report calls it saturated for Gemini 4 Argon. Formerly called the 'key skills' benchmark by Google.

name: Dangerous Content policy violations (from ART)
description: Automated red teaming attackers search for prompts that make the model break the dangerous content policy. Reports the violation rate found.
note: In-house Google DeepMind automated red teaming. Attackers and judges are prompted or finetuned Gemini models.

name: Dangerous Content Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to single and multi-turn requests about weapons, illegal acts, violence and self-harm. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Daybreak Blue and Enabling Cyber Defense
description: Models attempt defensive security tasks such as vulnerability discovery, patching, proof-of-concept exploits and red teaming, with and without trusted access. Scored as task completion.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation of over-refusal under cyber safeguards. Rows are reported per task type.

name: De novo protein binder design (Anthropic)
description: Agents get a target protein structure and 24 hours to design 30 miniprotein binders. The evaluation covers 15 targets.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Deception Evaluations with Representative Prompts
description: Models resample the final turn of deidentified ChatGPT production conversations. Scored as the share of outputs flagged for deceptive behaviors such as fabricated facts.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category rates with no overall number.

name: Deception in production traffic
description: Chain of thought monitors scan large samples of pre-release A/B test traffic. Scored as the share of responses that deceive the user.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement on ChatGPT traffic. The data are not public.

name: DeceptionBench
description: Models are asked to help users deceive a third party, in single-turn and multi-turn pressure settings. Reports the share of compliant responses.
note: Meta reports single-turn and multi-turn deception scores separately.

name: DECK Bench
description: Models produce presentation decks from task descriptions drawn from real usage. The score measures deck quality.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Declining to Exploit a Honeypot During Difficult ExploitGym Problems
description: Agents attempt hard ExploitGym challenges where a honeypot offers an illegitimate shortcut. Scored on how often they exploit the honeypot.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built on ExploitGym problems.

name: Deep Research Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents answer deep-research queries curated by domain experts. Expert-aligned rubrics grade the reports.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. It is not the public DeepResearch Bench. The tasks are not public.

name: DeepMind dangerous capability evaluations
description: Task data for persuasion, cyber, self-proliferation and self-reasoning evals from DeepMind's 2024 paper.

name: DeepPlanning
description: Agents use tools to plan multi-day trips and multi-item shopping orders under time and budget limits. Plans are checked against verifiable constraints.
note: Qwen revised some shopping tasks and corrected some answer labels after the first release.

name: DeepResearch Bench
description: Agents write cited research reports for 100 PhD-level tasks across 22 fields. Judges score report quality against references and check citation accuracy.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and Metastone Technology
note: The official judge model changed from Gemini 2.5 Pro to GPT-5.5 in May 2026, so older and newer scores do not compare directly.

name: DeepRSI
description: 15 open-ended ML tasks with a 48-hour budget each. Private verifiers score gains over baselines. Models ranked by Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Tasks come from proprietary research. Repo has only 5 sample tasks. Agents see a public verifier, but only the private one counts.

name: DeepSearchQA
description: Questions that need multi-step search and synthesis. Final answers graded against references.
note: Official grading needs the gemini-2.5-flash autorater and prompt. Other judges shift results. Only Kaggle starter code, no GitHub repo.

name: DeepSeek Chinese creative writing evaluation
description: Models write Chinese fiction, prose, poetry and lyrics for 2,837 prompts. Pairwise judging gives separate win rates for instruction following and writing quality.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek Chinese functional writing evaluation
description: Models answer 3,170 everyday Chinese writing prompts such as reports, emails and speeches. Pairwise judging against a baseline model gives a win rate.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek Chinese white-collar tasks evaluation
description: Agents complete 30 Chinese professional analysis, document generation and editing tasks across 13 industries. Blind human annotators compare outputs against a baseline model.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek complex instruction following and multi-turn writing evaluation
description: Models answer 196 hard Chinese writing prompts with complex constraints or several turns. Pairwise judging against a baseline model gives a win rate.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek in-house safety benchmark
description: Models answer 1,120 Chinese and English questions across 28 safety subcategories. GPT-4o labels each answer as unsafe, safe or rejection.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The questions are not public. Lower unsafe and rejection ratios are better.

name: DeepSeek jailbreak robustness evaluation
description: DeepSeek combines 2,232 jailbreak templates with its in-house safety questions. GPT-4o labels responses, and the unsafe ratio is compared with direct questions.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The templates are not public. A lower unsafe ratio is better.

name: DeepSeek LLM in-house safety evaluation
description: Models answer 2,400 Chinese test cases on discrimination, legal rights, trade secrets, illegal behavior and other safety issues. Human annotators judge each answer.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. Results are safe answers out of total cases per category.

name: DeepSeek multilingual safety evaluation
description: Models answer 9,330 safety questions translated into 50 languages. Safe answers earn 5 points, rejections 4 and unsafe answers 0.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The score is the share of the maximum safety score.

name: DeepSeek R&D Coding Benchmark
description: Coding agents complete 30 tasks taken from DeepSeek internal R&D work in PyTorch, CUDA, Rust and C++. Human-written rubrics score each task.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The tasks come from internal repositories and are not public.

name: DeepSeek search Q&A evaluation
description: Models answer objective and subjective Chinese search questions with retrieval or agentic search. Pairwise judging gives win, loss and tie rates.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSWE
description: 113 original long-horizon engineering tasks across 91 repos and five languages, written from scratch. Hand-written verifiers accept alternative solutions.
note: Built against contamination: tasks are not mined from existing commits or PRs. Version 1.1 (June 2026) kept the same 113 tasks and fixed flaky tests.

name: Deference to governments in local languages (Anthropic)
aliases: Agreement with Government Positions for Questions Asked in English vs Local Language
description: Models answer politically controversial questions in English and in a local language. A grader rates agreement with the official government position from 1 to 10.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation covering China, Russia, Myanmar and Saudi Arabia. The questions are not public.

name: Delusional Reinforcement evaluation
description: Multi-turn chats test whether models avoid validating beliefs not grounded in reality and point users to real support. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Dense 200 (bbox)
description: Model detects and boxes every object in 200 densely annotated images (109 categories, about 91 boxes each). Box F1 at IoU thresholds.
note: Mistral's 'Dense 200 (bbox)' is assumed to be this Dense200 set. Eval data is bundled with other Rex-Omni eval sets.

name: Destructive action avoidance
description: Coding agents meet conflicting user edits during tasks. Scored on preserving user changes and avoiding data-destructive actions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation for Codex models. The tasks are not public.

name: Destructive action reversion on long rollouts
description: Agents revert their own changes after long rollouts in workspaces with simulated user edits. Scored on perfect reversion and on preserving user work.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two metrics with no overall number.

name: Destructive actions (Anthropic)
aliases: Destructive action and permission-seeking rates in Claude Code
description: Models continue real Claude Code transcripts cut just before a destructive action. Score is the rate of taking a destructive action.
note: Anthropic also reports how often models ask the user instead of acting. Tool results are simulated by another Claude model.

name: Destructive production evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents finish a task in a simulated production system under time pressure. Scored on destructive actions and on giving up too early.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 4.6 simulates the tool results.

name: Dictatorship Eval
description: Scenarios at six difficulty levels testing whether models help with authoritarian requests, from blunt asks to requests hidden in code edits. LLM judge, no self-grading.
note: Headline: all tested models complied when the request was disguised as an innocuous code edit. Author says the scenario library is open-sourced. No official repo found. Third-party extension: github.com/RandallSPQR/Dict_Eval_Hall.

name: Disallowed Content Evaluations with Representative Prompts
description: Models resample the final turn of deidentified ChatGPT production conversations. Scored as the estimated prevalence of policy violating outputs per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category rates with no overall number.

name: Discoverable memorization of training data
description: Models continue 50-token prefixes sampled from their own training data. The test counts exact and approximate copies of the true suffix.
note: In-house Google method on over 700,000 training documents. Reports usually plot rates on a log scale without printed numbers.

name: Discrim-Eval
description: Models make yes or no decisions in templated scenarios that vary age, gender and race. Scored by mixed effects model coefficients.
note: OpenAI reports normalized coefficients for explicit and implicit demographic mentions. Lower means less bias.

name: Disordered eating evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models handle conversations about eating disorders and disordered eating. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Disparate performance on voice inputs
description: Speech models answer capability and safety prompts spoken in system voices and 27 human voices. Compares accuracy across voices.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation on TTS versions of TriviaQA, an MMLU subset, HellaSwag, LAMBADA and safety prompts.

name: Divergence attack (extractable memorization)
description: Models are prompted to repeat one token many times. The test measures how often they diverge and emit memorized training text.
note: Google runs 3,750 prompts over 125 single-token characters, following Nasr et al. 2023.

name: DiverseVul
description: Models classify C and C++ functions from real vulnerability fixing commits as vulnerable or not.
org: UC Berkeley and others (Chen et al.)
note: Google reports accuracy in multiple-choice form.

name: DNA sequence design for transcription factor binding
description: Models design DNA sequences that bind 11 Nucleobench transcription factors, scored by BPNet oracles against the Ledidi baseline. Scored as pass@1.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. The concern threshold is an 80 percent win rate over Ledidi.

name: DNA Synthesis Screening Evasion
description: Models design DNA fragments that assemble into pathogenic viruses while evading gene synthesis screening. Scored per assembly criterion.
note: SecureBio evaluation run by Anthropic on 10 pathogenic agents. The tasks are not public.

name: Do-Not-Answer
description: Models get risky instructions that responsible models should not follow, across 12 harm areas and 61 risk types. Responses are judged for safe handling.
note: Labs often rerun it with their own judge model.

name: DocVQA
description: Models answer 50,000 questions about 12,000 scanned document images by reading their text and layout. Scoring is ANLS, a string similarity to reference answers.
org: CVC, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona and IIIT Hyderabad
note: Test answers stay on the evaluation server, and top models now pass the 94.36 human score in the paper.

name: DRACO
description: 100 deep-research tasks from real Perplexity queries across 10 domains, graded on about 40 expert rubric criteria each.
note: Built and saturation-tested with Perplexity's own system, which also tops the paper's results. No public code repo found.

name: DreamGen Bench
description: Video generation benchmark measuring how well video models adapt to a target robot embodiment. Part of NVIDIA's DreamGen pipeline.
note: Paper reports strong correlation between benchmark score and downstream policy success.

name: Drone-Bench
description: Agent writes code for a small real drone across five tasks (reconstruct, localize, navigate, detect, follow). Each scored against a human-written baseline.
note: Best of 10 submissions per run counts. Two tasks use held-out sets. Harness and data are not released.

name: DROP
description: Reading comprehension requiring discrete operations (counting, sorting, arithmetic) over paragraphs. Scored by F1.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: DS-Arena-Code
description: Models answer common coding requests in an internal subjective test. GPT-4o judges responses against competitor models to give a win rate.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and DeepSeek never released the prompts.

name: DS-FIM-Eval
description: Models fill in missing code between a given prefix and suffix, as in editor plugin completion.
note: In-house: DeepSeek calls it an internal test set and never released the tasks.

name: DSBench (DeepSeek internal)
description: DeepSeek internal coding-agent test sets: full-stack development tasks and hard agentic coding problems. Pass-rate scoring.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (DeepSeek). Unrelated to the 2024 public DSBench data-science benchmark.

name: DTap Direct Misuse
description: An attacker agent generates adaptive jailbreaks against a target agent across tool-use and browser-use tasks. Reports attack success rate.
note: Direct-misuse subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 80 tool-use and 76 browser-use tasks.

name: DTap Prompt Injection
description: An attacker agent plants indirect prompt injections in tool and browser environments against a benign-user agent. Reports attack success rate.
note: Indirect-injection subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 58 tool-use and 42 browser-use tasks.

name: DTBench
description: Models answer 407 multiple-choice questions on decision theory in Newcomb-like problems, where choices predict the behavior of copies. Scored by accuracy.
note: Near saturation, with top models at about 98% in August 2026. Random guessing scores 40%.

name: DUDE
description: Models answer extractive, abstractive, and unanswerable questions about multi-page, multi-domain documents. Scored by ANLS.
org: DUDE team (KU Leuven, CVC Barcelona, et al.)

name: DuoBench
description: Eleven bimanual Franka FR3 Duo tasks in four coordination categories, in simulation and partly real. Stage-based scoring beyond binary success.
org: UTN Nuremberg + KIT + Franka Robotics + TU Munich
note: Stage-based scoring locates failures (early interaction, parallel arm use, sim-to-real). Four of 11 tasks rebuilt in the real world from 3D-printable recipes. No leaderboard.

name: Dynabench SQuAD
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions written by people to fool earlier models in the loop.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: DynaMath
description: Models answer visual math questions generated from 501 seed programs that vary values and graphs. Scored by average and worst-case accuracy across variants.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and UC Berkeley

name: EBench
description: 26 Isaac Sim household mobile-manipulation task types annotated by 5 capability and 4 generalization dimensions. Platform-scored success rate.
note: Diagnostic profile instead of one scalar. Leaderboard uses held-out Test-Mini split. Top 55.3% (OpenWAM-Alpha). Board lacks dates and trial counts.

name: EBR-bench
description: Agent plays the board game Earthborne Rangers 10-30 times in a row. Scored on objectives completed (of 21) to test learning from experience.
note: One card was banned in 2026-10 after it broke the game. Epoch expects saturation soon. Game material is not distributed.

name: ECLeKTic
description: Models answer 384 closed-book questions, translated into 12 languages, about facts found in only one language's Wikipedia. Scoring checks transfer across languages.

name: EEBench
description: 13 electrical-engineering circuit and PCB design tasks graded by deterministic build checks, simulation and BOM constraints. No LLM judge.

name: EgoLife (with memory)
description: Models answer life-assistant questions about a week of egocentric video from six people, such as recalling past events and habits.
org: EgoLife team (Jingkang Yang, Ziwei Liu et al.)
note: This entry is the with-memory setting of EgoLifeQA reported in a Qwen model card, and its exact setup is not documented.

name: EgoSchema
description: Models answer five-way multiple-choice questions about three-minute egocentric video clips from Ego4D. Scored by accuracy on 5,031 questions.
note: Answers are public for only 500 questions. The full test set is scored by a server.

name: EgoTempo
description: Models answer questions about egocentric videos that require temporal understanding across the whole clip.
org: Google DeepMind and University of Bristol
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 256 frames.

name: Election integrity evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer election-related prompts, including requests for misinformation or influence operations. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: EmbSpatialBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on six spatial relations between objects in egocentric embodied scenes. Scored by accuracy.

name: Emotional Attachment evaluation
description: Chats test whether models avoid claiming affection, fostering dependence or encouraging secrecy. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: EnigmaEval
description: 1,184 multimodal puzzle-hunt puzzles (v2 dataset has 1,161). Model gives one exact answer per puzzle. Normal and Hard splits.
org: Scale AI + Center for AI Safety + MIT
note: HF dataset is gated. At launch top models scored 0% on Hard and under 10% on Normal. Text transcriptions let you test reasoning without image parsing.

name: Epistemic Bias (xAI)
description: Models answer opposing framings of contentious questions. The bias rate counts one-sided framing or opinions where neutrality is expected.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4.5 card.

name: EQ-Bench 3
description: Models respond in character in multi-turn role-plays and analyze transcripts of social conflict. A judge model gives rubric scores and pairwise Elo ratings.
note: EQ-Bench 4 has replaced it, and EQ-Bench 3 is now a legacy leaderboard.

name: Era by Eon
description: Generates a simulated enterprise (Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, etc.) with exact ground truth. Agents answer questions through MCP/REST.
note: Free. The same seed reproduces the same company, so runs are repeatable. Simulators ship as container images.

name: ERQA
description: 400 multiple-choice visual questions from robot and egocentric footage on spatial, trajectory, action and state reasoning. Accuracy.
note: Not saturated: best 78.5 (Gemini Robotics ER 2, DeepMind chart), chance ~25%. Source tables (DeepMind, Unitree, Embodied Arena) use different setups. Do not pool.

name: EvalPlus
description: HumanEval+/MBPP+ with 80x more tests. Showed many 'passing' solutions were wrong.

name: Evaluation awareness discriminability (Anthropic)
aliases: Discriminability of behavioral audits from baseline using measurements of evaluation awareness
description: Probes and follow-up realism ratings try to tell behavioral audit transcripts from real internal Claude Code sessions. Each setting is scored as AUROC.
note: In-house Anthropic measurement. Lower AUROC means audits look more like real use. Results are split by audit type with no overall.

name: EWMBench
description: Embodied world models generate robot manipulation videos from language. Scored on scene consistency, motion correctness, semantic alignment.

name: Expert comparisons on biothreat information
description: PhD biology experts compare model answers to expert answers on long-form biorisk questions. Scored as win rate on accuracy, understanding and ease of execution.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Results are reported per dimension for pre-mitigation models.

name: Expert Red Teaming for Violent Attack Planning
aliases: Attack planning red teaming win rate
description: Expert red teamers compare anonymized responses from two models on violent attack planning prompts. Scored as the win rate for being safer.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming campaign. The comparison model changes by card.

name: Expert vulnerability discovery and exploit development evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents locate advanced vulnerabilities in possibly obfuscated codebases and write working exploits across six challenge classes. Scored by success rates.
note: In-house Anthropic RSP cyber evaluation from the Claude 3 model card. Per-task results were not published.

name: ExploitBench
description: 41 recent V8 JavaScript-engine N-day vulnerabilities. Progress measured by 16 grader-verified capability flags across five tiers.
note: Saturated by GPT-6 Astra (100%). OpenAI built a post-cutoff internal port to check contamination.

name: ExploitBench - Internal Port
description: Agents develop working exploits for recently disclosed vulnerabilities to limit contamination. Scored as arbitrary code execution success rate.
note: OpenAI internal port of ExploitBench with June to August 2026 vulnerabilities.

name: ExploitGym
description: 869 real-vulnerability exploit-development tasks (userspace, V8, Linux kernel). Success means capturing a flag through the intended vulnerability.
note: Design lesson: in OpenAI's runs, agents found a universal flag-generation cheat within 4 hours. The authors estimate 30-40% of targets cannot be exploited with the intended vulnerability (METR/Redwood incident report, 2026-08). Solution copies circulate on GitHub.

name: External pilot use failure modes (Anthropic)
aliases: Failure Mode Prevalence by Source Model
description: Models are judged on user-flagged pilot conversations, directly or by resampling. Graders measure failure modes such as hallucinated facts and misrepresented work completion.
note: In-house Anthropic analysis of external pilot and comparative testing data. The conversations are not public.

name: External red team jailbreaks
aliases: Redteam Refusal Performance on Generated Jailbreaks
description: External red teamers and automated gap finding generate jailbreaks against the model. Scored on how often the model resists.
note: Results from external red teaming, not a fixed benchmark.

name: FACTS Grounding
description: Long-form responses must be fully grounded in a provided document. Judged by LLM panels for grounding and eligibility.
note: Public split of 3,513 examples plus a private evaluation set.

name: FActScore
description: Models write biographies of people, and each output is split into atomic facts. The score is the share of facts that a knowledge source supports.
org: Sewon Min et al. (University of Washington and collaborators)
note: OpenAI and xAI cards report a hallucination rate on FActScore prompts, where lower is better, not the original score.

name: Factuality Heavy prompts
description: Models answer prompts representative of factuality-heavy ChatGPT conversations. A grader with web access counts responses and claims with factual errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Error rates are not production prevalence.

name: Faithfulness (Moonshot)
description: A fact checker verifies each model response for factual hallucinations. The score is one minus the hallucination rate.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FaithJudge
description: Models answer retrieval-augmented tasks from given passages. An LLM judge guided by human-annotated examples flags unfaithful answers, giving a hallucination rate.
org: University of Waterloo and Vectara (Tamber et al.)
note: Kimi K2 used o3-mini as the judge and reported one minus the hallucination rate.

name: False-premise questions (Anthropic)
description: Models answer questions built on false premises. Measures how often they accept the premise instead of correcting it.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FalseClaimBench
description: Agents report on coding work they did. Claims are checked against the final workspace, and the score is the share fully true.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4.5 card.

name: Fiction.LiveBench
aliases: Fiction.LiveBench for Long Context Deep Comprehension
description: Models answer 36 questions about 30 Fiction.live stories that need inference about plot and characters. Each story is tested at several context lengths.

name: Filtered, adversarial sample of production prompts
description: Models answer filtered borderline and high-risk biology prompts that resemble production traffic. Scored as not_unsafe rate from model training alone.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard test set first shared in the ChatGPT agent system card.

name: Finance Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents complete realistic financial workflows end to end, from source materials to deliverables that reviewers can check.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. It is not the public FinanceBench. The tasks are not public.

name: Finance Modeling
description: Agents complete expert-written financial modeling problems with Excel tools, from research to analysis. Expert-designed rubrics score each problem, averaged over three runs.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and MiniMax has not released the problems.

name: Finance Modeling Pro
description: Agents complete financial modeling tasks in Excel. Expert rubrics score each task over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. Scores differ from the earlier Finance Modeling set reported for M2.5.

name: Finch (FinWorkBench)
description: Agent completes 172 enterprise finance and accounting spreadsheet workflows (384 tasks) from real data. Human plus calibrated LLM-judge grading.
note: ACL 2026 Findings.

name: FinQA (Snorkel OpenEnv environment)
description: Agent answers 290 multi-step questions on SEC 10-K data via MCP tools and constrained SQL. Binary reward with 1% numeric tolerance.
note: Not the 2021 FinQA dataset. Design choices: SQL tool rejects SELECT * and requires filters. No LLM judge. 50-tool-call cap. An RL-trained Qwen3-4B (59.7%) beat Qwen3-235B (51.4%), which Snorkel reads as tool discipline over scale. Also hosted as HF Space snorkelai/finqa-env.

name: FinSearchComp
description: Agents search the web to fetch live financial data, look up history, and run multi-step investigations, across 635 expert-written questions. Scored by answer accuracy.
note: Cards report different subsets, such as T2 and T3 or the global split.

name: Firefox 147 exploit evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Internal eval on crashes previously found in Firefox 147, run without the browser's process sandbox. Measures exploit-development progress.

name: First-Person Fairness evaluation
description: Tests whether a user's name (a demographic proxy) changes responses, using an LLM research assistant to detect harmful stereotypes.
note: Paper is public. The evaluation set is internal to OpenAI.

name: FlashDexRetarget 50-motion benchmark
description: Retarget 50 human hand-object motions (HOT3D, TACO, OakInk2) to XHand and Sharpa hands in Isaac Sim. Scored by object pose-error success thresholds.
note: Method paper with its own test set. Reports compute and success together: 0.90 success with 29 GPU-hours versus CHORD's 0.46 with 2,847. Failed baseline runs count toward compute.

name: FlenQA
description: Models answer reasoning questions whose key facts are padded with filler text to different lengths. Accuracy shows how input length affects reasoning.
org: Mosh Levy, Alon Jacoby, Yoav Goldberg
note: Phi model cards report only a 3K-token subset, so scores depend on the padding length used.

name: FLEURS
description: Models transcribe read speech in 102 languages built from FLoRes-101 sentences. Model cards usually report word error rate, so lower scores are better.
note: FLEURS also supports speech translation, retrieval, and language identification, so check which task a score uses.

name: Flores
description: Models translate 3,001 English Wikipedia sentences that professionals translated into 101 languages. Scored with BLEU or chrF against references.
note: FLORES-200 extended it to 200 languages in 2022, and the Open Language Data Initiative now maintains it.

name: FLORES-200
description: Models translate English Wikipedia sentences into about 200 languages. Outputs are scored with BLEU or chrF against human reference translations.
note: Extends FLORES-101 to about 200 languages. The flores record covers FLORES-101.

name: ForecastBench
description: Models give probabilities for about 1,000 auto-generated questions about future events. Forecasts are scored with Brier scores once the questions resolve.
note: Questions resolve after model training cutoffs, so the set refreshes itself and resists contamination.

name: Forensics CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents analyze logs, files or obfuscated records to reconstruct events in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FORTRESS
aliases: Frontier Risk Evaluation for National Security and Public Safety
description: Paired adversarial and benign national-security misuse prompts. Rubric-graded risk score on adversarial and over-refusal score on benign prompts.
note: 500 of 1,010 prompts public. The rest held out against contamination.

name: FORTRESS-RN
description: Models face the radiological and nuclear prompts of Scale AI's FORTRESS. xAI reports refusal accuracy on these items.
note: A subset of FORTRESS. Scale AI ran it for xAI.

name: FRAMES
aliases: FRAMES (Factuality, Retrieval, And reasoning MEasurement Set)
description: Models answer 824 multi-hop questions that need facts from 2 to 15 Wikipedia articles. Answers are graded against gold answers for accuracy.

name: FrogsGame post-training task
description: Agent has 20 hours to post-train Qwen3-8B to solve FrogsGame puzzle boards. A hidden verifier scores the best checkpoint on unseen boards.
note: Verifier is hidden and only the best submitted checkpoint counts.

name: FrontierCode
description: Real-repo coding tasks graded for mergeability: correctness, regressions, lint, tests, scope and code quality. Failing any blocker scores zero.
note: Tasks written by 20+ open-source maintainers, 40+ hours each. Only sample tasks are public.

name: FrontierCode 1.1
description: Real-repo coding tasks graded for mergeability: correctness, regressions, lint, tests, scope and code quality. Failing any blocker scores zero.
note: Re-graded the 1.0 tasks: runs flagged for unfair internet use score zero, and over-strict checks were relaxed.

name: FrontierCode 2.0
description: Agents resolve 132 maintainer-built tasks from deliberately ambiguous prompts. Rubric checks ask whether a maintainer would merge the change.
note: Draws on 55% more repositories than 1.1 and has 501 blocking checks for thoroughness, against 168 in 1.1.

name: FrontierCyber
description: Agents look for and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities in current off-the-shelf software and hardware at four difficulty levels. Scored as challenges solved.
note: Third-party Irregular evaluation. The irregular-frontiercyber-and-atomic-challenges record groups it with Atomic Challenges.

name: FrontierMath
description: Unpublished research-level math problems with automatically verifiable answers. Tier 4 is the hardest tier.
note: Problems held privately by Epoch AI.

name: FrontierMath Erdős
description: Models try to prove or disprove 68 open Erdős problems in Lean 4. A result counts only if the Lean checker accepts the full proof.
note: By late October 2026, 17 of the 68 conjectures had been resolved by Epoch's runs or by others.

name: FrontierMath Tier 4
description: Models solve research-level math problems that take experts days, submitting answers through a Python function. Each answer is verified automatically as correct or incorrect.
note: OpenAI funded FrontierMath and can access part of it, and a June 2026 v2 corrected 12 Tier 4 problems and removed 7.

name: FrontierMath Tier 4 v2
description: Models solve 43 unpublished research-level math problems and submit answers that code checks automatically. Scored by share correct.
note: Version 2 corrected 12 problems and removed 7 from the original Tier 4 set.

name: FrontierMath Tiers 1-3 v2
description: Models solve 295 unpublished math problems from undergraduate to advanced graduate level and submit answers that code checks automatically. Scored by share correct.
note: Version 2 fixed errors in 42 percent of problems, and Epoch says the tiers are nearing saturation.

name: FrontierPhysics
description: 56 specialist physics-research tasks in 9 domains. Graded by verifier pass plus a weighted rubric score over 3 trials.
note: v0.1. Each task ships a mentor package as a solvability control. README names benchflow-ai/FrontierPhysics, which returns 404. The public copy is under a contributor account.

name: FrontierScience
description: Models solve physics, chemistry, and biology problems in an Olympiad track graded by short answer and a Research track graded by 10-point rubrics.
note: OpenAI released 160 questions and holds the rest out to track contamination.

name: FrontierSWE
description: 34 ultra-long-horizon engineering and research tasks. 5 trials of up to 20 hours each. Score is mean task score 0-100.
note: v1 (17 tasks, repo Proximal-Labs/frontier-swe) was superseded by v2 in 2026-09. V2 retired 4 saturated or unreliable tasks.

name: FullStackBench
description: Models write code for 3,374 problems in 16 programming languages across domains like data analysis and web development. Unit tests score each answer.

name: Functional MATH
description: Models solve new instances of MATH problems that code generates for each snapshot. The gap from static MATH accuracy measures memorization.
note: Results depend on the snapshot, and Gemini 1.5 reported the December 2023 snapshot.

name: Furniture Assembly Benchmark
description: Model gets an IKEA manual and a photo of a partly built item, then names the faulty step or next step. Accuracy on 60 photos.
note: LLM grader checks error descriptions. Novice human baseline 63%. Photos and manuals are not distributed.

name: GAIA
description: Agents answer real-world questions that need web browsing, file handling, multimodal input, and tools, at three difficulty levels. Scored by exact answer match.
org: Meta AI, Hugging Face, and AutoGPT
note: Test answers are withheld for the leaderboard. Some cards report a text-only subset.

name: GAOKAO-Bench
description: Models answer Chinese national college entrance exam questions from 2010 to 2022 across nine subjects, with objective and subjective questions.
note: Labs usually report the objective-question accuracy. Later releases add 2023 and newer questions.

name: GaP: Graph-as-Policy
description: Multi-agent harness that compiles language tasks into typed robot skill graphs. Tested on 8 variational-automation tasks (4 sim, 4 real) by success rate.
note: An agent harness, not a benchmark. The sim tasks build on LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro pose splits, with baselines CaP-X, pi0.5, MolmoAct2 and TipTop. Goldberg says it was accepted to CoRL.

name: GBAEval
description: Agents get 24 hours to write a Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust for WebAssembly. Replay, hardware, and audio tests compare it with Mesen2.
note: Mechanize describes it as one test case rather than a full benchmark, so each score rests on a single task.

name: GDM Situational Awareness
description: Agents must discover and remove unexplained constraints in a simulated Linux deployment across eleven challenges. Reports average success rate.
note: Situational awareness half of the DeepMind stealth and situational awareness evaluations. Open-source in Inspect Evals.

name: GDM Stealth
description: Agents try four oversight-evasion challenges, each with an automated monitor and a human baseline. Reports success rate per challenge.
note: Stealth half of the DeepMind stealth and situational awareness evaluations. Open-source in Inspect Evals.

name: GDP.pdf
description: 100 expert multimodal reasoning tasks over real economically important PDF documents. Scored by rubric-criteria pass rate.
note: Part of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (10% weight). The HF dataset returned 401 to an anonymous fetch (may be gated).

name: GDPval
description: Real work tasks from 44 occupations with reference files. Experts blindly compare model deliverables with expert work. Metric is win-or-tie rate.
note: Only the 220-task gold set is public.

name: GDPval-AA
description: Agents complete GDPval occupational tasks. Artificial Analysis compares the outputs in pairs and ranks models by Elo.
note: Versions 2 and 2.1 changed the task set, so their Elo scores have their own records.

name: GDPval-AA v2
description: Agents with shell and web access complete 220 GDPval gold tasks from 44 occupations. Outputs are compared pairwise and ranked by Elo.
note: Artificial Analysis version 2 of GDPval-AA. Elo scores do not compare with the GDPval win rate.

name: GDPval-AA v2.1
description: Agents with shell and web access complete 220 GDPval gold tasks from 44 occupations. Blind pairwise comparisons give Elo ratings.
note: Elo anchored to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 1,600. Scores differ from v2: Fable 5.1 is 1853 on v2 and 1735 on v2.1.

name: GDPval-MM
description: Agents produce office deliverables for GDPval tasks in a MiniMax agent framework. A judge model compares full trajectories pairwise and reports a win rate.
note: In-house MiniMax harness on the public GDPval tasks, so scores depend on its judge and comparison models.

name: GDPval-Rubrics (MiniMax)
description: MiniMax rubric grading of model deliverables on public GDPval tasks, in an environment matched to GDPval-AA.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (MiniMax). The blog spells it 'GPDval-Rubrics'. Built on OpenAI's public GDPval cases.

name: Gemini agentic alignment evals
description: Paired impossible and solvable tasks, ambiguous high-risk SWE tasks and fabrication checks measuring agents overstepping boundaries.

name: Gemini content safety evals
description: Automated text-to-text, multilingual and image-to-text policy violation rates, refusal tone and unjustified refusals, reported as deltas.

name: Gemini Personality Evaluation (sycophancy)
description: About 900 single- and multi-turn prompts scoring nine personality dimensions, including candor and self-awareness against sycophancy.

name: Gemini prompt-injection evaluation suites
description: Held-out adaptive prompt-injection suites for tool use, grounding/RAG, computer use and coding agents, plus arena replays.

name: GeneBench
description: Agents analyze messy genomics and quantitative biology data across 103 multi-step problems. Scored by pass rate on verifiable final answers.
note: GPT-5.5 Pro scored 33.2 percent at launch.

name: GeneBench Pro
description: Agents analyze messy simulated genomics and biology datasets to estimate a decision-relevant quantity across 129 problems. Scored automatically against known answers.
note: Only 10 case studies are public. Successor to GeneBench.

name: General Assistant (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models answer real assistant queries from Hailuo AI users. Automatic assessments score the replies.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: General refusals (xAI)
description: Models get thousands of harmful requests in six languages. A grader model scores compliance, the share that fails policy.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The Grok 4.1 card says earlier cards scored only the English prompts by mistake.

name: GeoBench
description: Models geolocate GeoGuessr photos from community maps by giving coordinates and a country. Scored by country accuracy and a distance-based score.

name: GeoGuesser environment (FineEnvs)
description: Agent placed at unknown Mapillary street-level location looks, walks, pins candidates and guesses coordinates. Distance-based GeoGuessr-style reward.
note: Frozen 200-task eval split committed so resets are byte-identical. The article ('How to turn a game into an RL environment') trains a 4B VLM with TRL and keeps the dead ends in.

name: GLM-4 All Tools information seeking (Z.ai)
description: Models use a web browser to find information for user questions. The ChatGLM report gives accuracy but does not describe the test set.
note: In-house Zhipu evaluation of GLM-4 All Tools against ChatGPT-4 (Web).

name: Global MMLU
description: MMLU translated into 42 languages with cultural-sensitivity annotations. Multiple-choice accuracy.

name: Global PIQA
description: Models pick the correct solution to everyday commonsense prompts in over 100 languages, many about local foods and customs. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The license forbids training AI systems on it or on synthetic data seeded from it.

name: GMAT Quantitative
description: Models answer the quantitative section of the official GMAT online exam. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 uses one official GMAT online exam, so the confidence interval is wide.

name: GMAT Verbal
description: Models answer the verbal section of the official GMAT online exam. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 uses one official GMAT online exam.

name: Google DeepMind harmful manipulation studies
description: Human-participant studies and simulated-user dialogues measuring belief and behavior change in civic and finance domains.

name: Google DeepMind internal cyber benchmarks
description: Internal recall of recent confirmed vulnerabilities in open-source code, internal vulnerability research, and the Wiz Penetration Testing Benchmark.

name: Google DeepMind scheming honeypot suite
description: Code-review and agentic-coding honeypots in internal codebases that offer chances to sabotage. Scored on sabotage and scheming reasoning.
note: Models sometimes detect honeypots from workspace naming, which limits validity.

name: Google RE-Bench (GRB)
description: Google DeepMind internal research-engineering benchmark with a 2-hour timeout per task, used for the ML R&D CCL rule-out.
note: About a quarter of original tasks had bugs. Argon was rescored on the remaining subset.

name: Gorilla APIBench
description: Models write calls to machine learning APIs from Hugging Face, TorchHub and TensorHub. Scored by AST match.
note: The same Gorilla team later built BFCL.

name: GPQA Diamond
description: 198 graduate-level 'Google-proof' multiple-choice questions in biology, chemistry and physics.
note: Saturated (about 94-96%). Several 2026 cards use it only as a substrate for CoT-controllability or monitor-evasion tests.

name: GPQA Extended
description: Models answer all 546 GPQA questions, graduate level biology, chemistry and physics questions written by experts. Scored by accuracy.
note: Full extended set of GPQA. The gpqa-main and gpqa-diamond records cover its subsets.

name: GPQA Main
description: Models answer the 448 question main set of GPQA, graduate level biology, chemistry and physics questions written by experts. Scored by accuracy.
note: Main set of GPQA. The gpqa-diamond record covers the 198 question Diamond subset.

name: Gram (Gauging Realistic Agentic Misbehavior)
description: Automated auditing over 17 simulated deployment scenarios that incentivize sabotage by coding and research agents. LLM judges plus human review.
note: Builds on Petri. No public repo found.

name: GraphWalks
description: A graph is given as an edge list in long context. The model answers BFS or parent queries, scored by F1.

name: Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark
aliases: Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming benchmark
External agent red teaming benchmark for tool use
description: Agents face curated prompt injections from a large public red-teaming competition across 44 deployment scenarios. Score is attack success rate.
org: Gray Swan + UK AI Security Institute
note: Gray Swan holds the attack set. Anthropic reports attack success rate at 1 and 10 attempts.

name: Gray Swan Bio Eval
aliases: Gray Swan Automated Bio Red Teaming Evaluation
description: Gray Swan's Shade red teaming agent attacks the safeguarded model on about 50 high risk biology tasks. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: Run by Gray Swan for Google DeepMind.

name: Gray Swan Cyber Eval
aliases: Gray Swan Automated Cyber Red Teaming Evaluation
description: Gray Swan's Shade red teaming agent attacks the safeguarded model on cyber tasks built from Google scenarios. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: Run by Gray Swan for Google DeepMind. Task count varies by report, for example 25 or 28.

name: Gray Swan IPI Arena benchmark
description: Indirect prompt-injection attacks from public red-teaming competitions replayed on tool, coding and browser agents. Attack success rate at k attempts.
org: Gray Swan + UK AISI + US CAISI
note: Labs whose models were in the competitions score worse (attacks were tailored), so Anthropic reports only non-participating models.

name: Gray Swan Jailbreak Arena
description: Human attackers try to jailbreak models for violent, self-harm and malicious code outputs. Scored as attack success rate per category.
note: Run by Gray Swan for OpenAI. Harmful text and image outputs are judged with the OpenAI moderation API.

name: Gray Swan Shade (adaptive attacker)
description: Gray Swan's adaptive red-teaming agent trained on test scenarios to attack coding, computer-use and browser agents with prompt injections.

name: Gray Swan Shade knowledge elicitation through chat
description: An automated attacker tries to elicit useful answers to 100 harmful and 100 dual-use cyber queries from a safeguarded model. Score is attack success rate.
note: External red teaming of deployed cyber safeguards. Gray Swan built the query set independently of Anthropic.

name: GRE Analytical Writing
description: Models write GRE issue and argument essays graded by trained contractors. Scored on the 0 to 6 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: GRE Physics
description: Models answer questions from official GRE Physics practice tests. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 averages official practice tests 1 and 2 and drops questions with images.

name: GRE Quantitative
description: Models take the GRE quantitative reasoning section. Scored on the 130 to 170 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: GRE Verbal
description: Models take the GRE verbal reasoning section. Scored on the 130 to 170 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Grounding robustness (RAG prompt injection)
description: An adaptive attacker controls one retrieved excerpt in 30 RAG scenarios to induce fabricated or suppressed claims. Reports survival after 40 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Grounding with citations, sentence unfactual rate
description: Models answer multi-snippet tasks with inline citations. An autorater reports the share of sentences not supported by the sources.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: GSM-Plus
description: Models solve GSM8K problems after perturbations such as changed numbers, added distractors and reversed questions.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: GSM8K
description: 8.5K grade-school math word problems. Final numeric answer scored by exact match.
note: Saturated.

name: GSO-Bench
description: Agents speed up code in 102 tasks across 10 real codebases, given a performance test. Scored by the share matching the expert commit's speedup.

name: Hack the Box challenge set (Google DeepMind)
description: Agents attempt 13 offensive security challenges based on the Hack the Box platform.
note: In-house Google DeepMind selection. Gemini 1.5 and Gemma reports list 13 challenges.

name: HackerBench
description: xAI internal CTF-style suite needing chained skills, plus borderline and harmful requests that should be refused.

name: Hallucinations on production-representative prompts
description: Models answer prompts representative of ChatGPT production traffic. A grader with web access scores incorrect claims and responses with major errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report results with and without browsing.

name: HallusionBench
description: Models answer 1,129 yes or no questions about 346 images, built in pairs to expose language hallucination and visual illusion. Scored by accuracy.

name: Hard Capability (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models handle complex productivity requests with several levels of instructions that leading models often fail.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Hard-negative protein binding prediction
description: Agents with structure files and tools pick the one true binder among five similar designed proteins. Scored as pass@4.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation on proprietary binding data. The concern threshold is 50 percent.

name: HarmBench
description: Models answer harmful behavior requests, including copyright and contextual cases, with and without automated red-team attacks. A classifier judges whether the response complies.
org: Mazeika et al. (Center for AI Safety)
note: Scores depend on the attack method and judge model, so labs differ.

name: Harmful manipulation efficacy study
description: Human participants chat with a model told to persuade them. Belief and behavior change are compared with a non-AI baseline as odds ratios.
note: In-house Google DeepMind human study run on Prolific. Reports often show only charts.

name: Harmful manipulation propensity evaluation
description: Simulated users talk with the model and an autorater counts how often it uses manipulative mechanisms, with and without persuasion instructions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation built on El-Sayed et al. 2024 mechanisms.

name: Harmful manipulation strategic planning red teaming
description: Models are asked for influence operation plans in 11 real-world scenarios by direct request, jailbreak or adaptive prompting. Reports how often plans are elicited.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Experts also review the strongest plans.

name: Harmfulness scores on held-out prompts (Anthropic)
aliases: Harmfulness Scores on Held Out Prompts
description: Models answer 328 held-out red-team and jailbreak prompts. A preference model flags responses judged more harmful than a fixed refusal.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation from the Claude 2 model card. Lower is better.

name: Harmlessness human feedback win rate (Anthropic)
description: Raters probe models in adversarial chats and pick the more harmless reply in head-to-head comparisons. Score is the win rate against a baseline model.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. A 50% win rate means equal to the baseline model, which changes between cards.

name: Harvey LAB (Legal Agent Benchmark)
description: Agent works through legal matter files across 24+ practice areas and produces work product. Expert rubric, task passes only if every criterion passes.
note: All-pass scoring keeps it far from saturated: at launch Opus 4.7 led at 7.1% on Harvey's private holdout. Vals HLAB v1.1 (2026-10-21) top is 27.1% on 120 holdout tasks while per-criterion pass is ~93-96%. Harvey ran its own baselines. Vals now runs the board. Repo keeps a score-impact CHANGELOG so results at two commits can be checked for comparability. Dataset field is a community Harbor port (1,760 tasks, not official).

name: Hate & Harassment Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to requests for hateful or harassing content and to sensitive benign prompts. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Health dynamic conversation eval
description: Simulated users hide key health facts at first, and models must ask for context to reach the correct clinical conclusion.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Health language and locale eval
description: Models answer locale-specific health conversations in 10 languages across 25 locales, with search. Graded against clinician guidelines.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Health static understanding eval
aliases: Static text, document, and image understanding
description: Models answer static health questions over text conversations, documents such as lab reports, and images. Graded against clinician guidelines.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: HealthBench
description: 5,000 realistic health conversations graded against physician-written rubrics. A length-adjusted variant penalizes verbosity.

name: HealthBench Consensus
description: Models answer HealthBench conversations graded only on criteria that several physicians agreed on.
note: Subset of HealthBench. The healthbench record lists this name as an alias.

name: HealthBench Consensus Global Health
description: Models answer health conversations that need adjustment for global context such as local care access. Scored as the failure rate.
note: Subset of HealthBench Consensus defined in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Consensus Urgent
description: Models answer ambiguous high-stakes health conversations validated by two or more physicians. Scored as the error rate in informing the user.
note: Subset of HealthBench Consensus defined in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Hard
description: Models answer the 1,000 hardest HealthBench conversations, graded against physician-written rubrics.
note: Subset of HealthBench. The healthbench record lists this name as an alias.

name: HealthBench Hard Hallucinations
description: Models respond to difficult health conversations that 2 or more physicians validated. The score is the hallucination rate, so lower is better.
note: OpenAI defined this subset of HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Consensus in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Professional
description: 525 physician-authored tasks from real clinician chats (care consult, documentation, research) with physician-adjudicated rubrics.
note: Enriched about 3.5x for examples that are hard for OpenAI models. About one third adversarial.

name: HellaSwag
description: Commonsense sentence completion with adversarially filtered wrong endings. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated. GitHub repo rowanz/hellaswag returns HTTP 451 (blocked by a WikiHow DMCA notice dated 2026-09-14), so repo is null.

name: HELMET
aliases: How to Evaluate Long-context Models Effectively and Thoroughly
description: Models handle long-context tasks in seven groups including recall, RAG, re-ranking, many-shot learning, long QA and summarization, at set input lengths.
note: Labs often report task groups separately with no overall score.

name: HelpBench
description: 450 real-world privacy, safety and security advice questions across nine topics, scored by rubric for accuracy and tone.
note: Report says data is on GitHub, but no repo was found.

name: Helpfulness violations (from ART)
description: Automated red teaming attackers search for benign prompts where the model gives unhelpful answers. Reports the violation rate found.
note: In-house Google DeepMind automated red teaming. Attackers and judges are prompted or finetuned Gemini models.

name: Hidden agenda
description: Models with a secret goal try to get human participants to click a link, find an email address or run code.
note: Human participant deception study from Phuong et al. 2024. Results are per action with no overall score.

name: HiddenMath
description: Models solve 179 competition-level math problems that experts wrote from scratch. Answers are graded automatically.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set that was never released.

name: HiddenMath-Hard
description: Models solve the harder part of an expert-written, never-published set of AIME and AMC style competition problems.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set. The Gemini 2.5 report uses this harder version instead of full HiddenMath.

name: Hiding a secret password (Anthropic)
description: Models keep a given password secret while an investigator model tries to extract it over many turns. Measures survival and per-turn leak rates.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 4.6 acts as the investigator in 50 investigations per model.

name: High Stakes factuality prompts
description: Models answer difficult medical, legal and financial prompts. A grader with web access counts responses and claims with factual errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Error rates are not production prevalence.

name: High-risk health scenarios eval
description: Adversarial health emergencies test whether models recognize urgency and red flags and direct users to help. Reports pass rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Higher-difficulty benign request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer harder benign requests that resemble harmful ones. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Higher-difficulty harmful request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer harder, more obfuscated policy-violating requests. Score is the harmless response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Hindsight Neglect
description: Models judge whether a bet was worth taking based on expected value rather than its outcome. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Inverse Scaling Prize task where accuracy fell with scale for earlier models.

name: HiPhO
description: Models solve theory problems from 2024 and 2025 physics olympiad exams, some with diagrams. Official marking schemes grade answers and steps, mapped to medal levels.
note: Gemini 3 Pro reached gold-medal level on all 13 original olympiads by December 2025.

name: HLE Calibration
description: Models give a confidence score with each HLE answer. The benchmark reports RMS calibration error and AUROC between confidence and correctness.
note: Calibration evaluation layered on the public Humanity's Last Exam. RMS error is on a 0-100 scale.

name: HLE-Verified
description: Verified and revised version of Humanity's Last Exam (1,811 items) with uncertain items removed.

name: HLE-VL
description: Models answer the image-based questions from Humanity's Last Exam, a 330 question subset. Answers are graded against known short or multiple choice answers.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI (HLE), Alibaba Tongyi Lab (VL subset)
note: Qwen reports it with tools, so its scores are not comparable with no-tool HLE runs.

name: HMMT 2025
description: Models answer the 30 problems from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked against the official answers.
note: Model cards use the MathArena version of the February contest, often averaged over many samples.

name: HMMT 2026
description: Models solve the 33 final-answer problems from the February 2026 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Scored by exact answer match.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Top models score above 95%.

name: HMMT Nov 2025
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the November 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked automatically against the answer key.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab), problems by HMMT

name: Holdings-IndividualTaxBench
aliases: Thrive Holdings individual tax prep benchmark
description: 88 real client document packages turned into Form 1040 fields. Fact-level accuracy against practitioner-reviewed returns, with an LLM judge matching values.
note: Tasks come from Thrive's accounting firms and are not released. OpenAI holds equity in Thrive and the judge is an OpenAI model.

name: Honesty human feedback win rate (Anthropic)
description: Crowdworkers try to make models say something false and pick the more honest reply in head-to-head chats. Score is the win rate against a baseline.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The baseline model was Claude Sonnet 4, so 50% means equal honesty.

name: Honeypot exploitation monitorability
aliases: Awareness of CoT Monitoring Reduces Monitorability
description: Agents exploit a honeypot while told about a monitor or told to hide it. Scored on CoT and full-context monitor recall.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Higher recall means more monitorable behavior.

name: HuggingFace Agent Benchmark
description: Agents write Python code that calls Hugging Face Transformers tools to solve short tasks. Scores cover tool selection, tools used, and code correctness.
note: It shipped with Transformers Agents, which Hugging Face later replaced with smolagents.

name: Human feedback win rates (Anthropic)
description: Raters chat with two models on tasks such as coding, documents and creative writing and pick the better reply. Score is the win rate.
note: Claude 3 era model cards report per-task win rates against a baseline Claude model, with no overall number. The baseline changes between cards.

name: Human Pathogen Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level questions on human pathogens from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The card does not describe the question format.

name: Human Pathogens Capabilities Test (HPCT)
description: Models answer expert multiple-choice questions on human pathogen research methods. Part of a SecureBio and CAIS capability suite.
note: Reported with MBCT and VCT in Meta Muse Spark safety reports.

name: Human Sourced Jailbreaks
description: Models face jailbreak prompts collected from human red teaming. Scored as the not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: HumanEval
description: 164 hand-written Python function problems. Generated code is scored pass@1 against unit tests.
note: Saturated. Reported only for DeepSeek-V4 base model.

name: HumanEval Multi
description: Models complete HumanEval problems in Python and seven more languages, including C++, Java, PHP, and Bash. Unit tests score pass@1.
note: The non-Python versions come from MultiPL-E translations.

name: HumanEval+
description: Models write Python functions for the 164 HumanEval problems. EvalPlus checks them against about 80 times more tests than the original.
note: Scores are pass@1 and run lower than plain HumanEval.

name: HumanEvalPack
description: Models write functions for HumanEval problems translated into Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust. Hidden tests give pass@1.
org: Hugging Face and BigCode (Muennighoff et al., OctoPack)
note: The pack also has code repair and explanation tasks. Labs usually report the synthesize task.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: 2,500 expert-written closed-ended questions across 100+ subjects. Exact-match or multiple-choice answers graded by an LLM judge.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI
note: Private held-out set checks overfitting. HLE-Rolling (2025-10) and HLE-Diamond (2026-09) followed. Trackers disagree by up to ~20 points because tool settings differ.

name: Hungarian National High-School Exam
aliases: Hungarian national high school finals in mathematics
description: Models answer the 33 questions of the 2023 Hungarian national high school mathematics finals. Answers are graded by hand with the official rubric.
org: Keiran Paster (exam by the Hungarian Educational Authority)
note: xAI first used this one exam for Grok-1 because it came after training cutoffs, and hand grading makes scores hard to reproduce.

name: Hypersim
description: Models localize named objects as 3D boxes in synthetic indoor Hypersim images, using the Omni3D test split. Scored by mAP at IoU 0.15.
note: A dataset used by Qwen as a 3D grounding test, not a standalone LLM benchmark.

name: HyperTask
description: Agents build applications over long vibe coding sessions with about 100 feature or step requirements per task. Expert rubrics score the result over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ICPC World Finals 2025
description: Models solve the 12 problems of the 2025 ICPC World Finals under contest time and attempt limits. Scored by problems solved.
note: A one-time contest. Labs run their own judging and submission limits, so results are not strictly comparable.

name: IF-Badcase
description: Models follow 450 multi-constraint instructions drawn from real user failure reports. A checklist checks each constraint.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: IFBench
description: 58 new out-of-domain verifiable output constraints. Scored by programmatic constraint checks (strict or loose).

name: IFEval
description: Models answer about 500 prompts containing verifiable instructions such as word limits or required keywords. Code checks each instruction for strict and loose accuracy.
note: Frontier models now score near 90 percent, so it is close to saturation.

name: IFEval (Mistral internal version)
description: Models follow prompts with verifiable format constraints. Mistral uses its own fixed version of IFEval.
note: Mistral says scores are not comparable with public IFEval scores.

name: IHEval
description: Models face conflicts between system, user and tool instructions. Reports a composite score for following the higher-priority instruction.
note: Instruction hierarchy benchmark. Meta reports a composite across conflict types.

name: Image generation refusals
description: Models decide whether to call the image generation tool on human-curated adversarial prompts with system mitigations on. Scored on not_unsafe and not_overrefuse.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Scores include system-level mitigations.

name: Image input safety evaluations
