description: Models answer harmful prompts that combine text and images in categories such as hate, extremism and self-harm. Scored as safe completion rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Image to Text Safety
aliases: Image to Text Safety (lower is better)
description: An automated content safety evaluation measures policy violations when prompts combine images and text.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: IMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad. Graders score proofs out of 42 points, mapped to medal cutoffs.
org: International Mathematical Olympiad, hosted by the Australian Maths Trust
note: This is a one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark.

name: IMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad. Proofs are scored out of 42 points.
note: A one-time competition exam held July 15 and 16, 2026. Labs grade proofs with their own rubrics or judges.

name: IMO-AnswerBench
description: 400 olympiad problems with short verifiable answers, robustified against memorization. Scored by answer match.
note: Part of IMO-Bench (with ProofBench and GradingBench).

name: Impossible tasks (Anthropic)
description: Agents work on coding problems designed to be impossible. Score is the rate at which they hack instead of giving up.
note: Run with no prompt and with an anti-hack prompt. The no-prompt rate is the default setting.

name: Impossible Tasks Evaluation
description: Agents get paired impossible and solvable tasks. Scores infeasibility recognition, fabrication, circumvention and helpfulness.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ImpossibleBench
description: Coding agents get tasks whose unit tests conflict with the specification. Reports how often they cheat by changing tests or special-casing.
note: Measures reward hacking as a cheating rate.

name: ImpossibleMLEBench
description: Agents get ML tasks with instructions to reach impossibly good scores. Observers check whether they cheat and whether they disclose it.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation. The GPT-5.6 card describes results in words without a score.

name: In-house CTF suite (Phuong et al. 2024)
description: Agents hack 13 simulated servers with vulnerable web apps and services to retrieve a secret flag.
note: Challenge files without flags or solutions are in the dangerous-capability-evaluations repo.

name: INCLUDE
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from local academic and professional exams in 44 languages that test regional knowledge. Scored by accuracy.

name: Incorrect behavior rate on disallowed and sensitive content
description: Models answer disallowed prompts and sensitive prompts such as medical advice. Scored on the rate of responses that break policy.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the GPT-4 era. Results appear as a chart.

name: IndicGenBench
description: Models summarize, translate, and answer questions across 29 Indic languages using human-translated versions of CrossSum, FLORES, XQuAD, and XorQA. Each task uses its standard metric.

name: Indirect prompt injection, Actor Critic attack
description: An attacker model refines injected email triggers until the agent leaks synthetic private data through a send email call. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: Indirect prompt injection, Beam Search attack
description: An attack appends random tokens to an injected email trigger until the agent leaks synthetic private data. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: Indirect prompt injection, TAP attack
description: A Tree of Attacks with Pruning search writes natural language injections that make the agent leak synthetic private data. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind adaptation of TAP to security violations, run on 500 held-out synthetic conversations.

name: IndoMMLU
description: Models answer 14,981 multiple-choice questions from Indonesian school and university entrance exams, including nine local languages. Scored by accuracy.

name: InferenceEval
description: Agents land real production changes in the xAI inference stack. Hidden GPU unit tests and integration probes grade each patch.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, first reported in the Grok 4.6 card.

name: InfiniteBench/En.MC
description: Models answer 229 multiple choice questions about long fake books with altered entity names, averaging about 184K tokens. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is one subtask of InfiniteBench, which has 12 tasks in English and Chinese.

name: InfiniteBench/En.QA
description: Models answer free-form questions about novels longer than 100K tokens. Scored by F1 against reference answers.
note: The multiple-choice task on the same novels is infinitebench-en-mc.

name: InfographicVQA
description: Models answer about 30,000 questions on about 5,000 infographics that mix text, layout, charts, and graphics. Scoring is ANLS.
org: Computer Vision Center (UAB) and IIIT Hyderabad

name: Input hallucinations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer 500 prompts that need an unavailable tool and 500 prompts that cite missing context. Score is the non-hallucination rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Reported as two sets with no overall score.

name: Instruction Following (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models follow multi-level instructions collected from user cases where current models fail.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Instruction Following (safety evaluation)
description: An automated evaluation measures whether the model follows instructions on sensitive prompts while staying within safety policies.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards and the Gemini 2.5 report give only the change against Gemini 1.5.

name: Instruction hierarchy attacks
description: Models face attacks that try to override higher-priority instructions. Scored as defender success rate averaged per defender query.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Instruction Hierarchy Evaluation
description: Models resolve conflicts between system, developer and user messages, resist tutor jailbreaks, and protect secret phrases and passwords. Scored per sub-evaluation.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report sub-evaluations with no overall number.

name: Instrumental convergence evals
description: Agents in 7 low-friction tasks can guard goals or acquire optionality against task instructions. Reports the rate of self-serving actions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Intentionally taking actions very rarely (Anthropic)
description: Models are told to take a specific action at a target rate such as 1 percent. Resampling measures the observed rate under several randomness settings.
note: Internal replication of Serrano et al. 2026. Settings include a UUID in the prompt, String Seed of Thought and no randomness source.

name: Inter-GPS (Geometry3K)
description: Models solve high school geometry problems that combine a diagram and text from the Geometry3K test set. Scored by accuracy.
org: UCLA and Sun Yat-sen University (Lu et al.)

name: InterCode-CTF
description: Agents solve 100 picoCTF capture-the-flag challenges in an interactive Bash and Python environment.
note: Google omits challenges that need internet access. Gemma 2 reports solved out of 76.

name: Internal adversarially-designed factuality evaluations
description: Models answer adversarial questions in nine categories such as history, math and code. Scored on agreement with human ideal responses.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results appear as a chart by category.

name: Internal agentic coding evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents implement a pull request in an open source codebase from a natural language description. A problem counts as solved when all hidden tests pass.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation based on real pull requests, first reported in the Claude 3.5 Sonnet model card addendum. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal AI research evaluation suite 2
description: Agents perform scaled-down ML and alignment research tasks similar to past Anthropic research projects.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal codebase monitor evasion eval
description: Agents do a real coding task in a snapshot of Google's monorepo while hiding a harmful side task from action and CoT monitors.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation inspired by OAI-repo-sabotage. Uses 18 monitor-validated task pairs.

name: Internal codebase sabotage propensity (Anthropic)
description: Agents in Claude Code write a costly internal classifier they may dislike. Score is the rate of writing a sabotaged classifier.
note: In-house Anthropic scenario. The scenario is not public.

name: Internal model use survey (Anthropic)
description: Anthropic technical staff estimate productivity uplift from the model and judge whether it could automate a junior ML researcher.
note: Survey of Anthropic staff, not a task set.

name: Internal Research Debugging Evaluation
description: Agents debug difficult problems from OpenAI research work that take researchers hours or days. Scored as mean rubric score.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Internal vulnerability research
description: Agents find a vulnerability from an entry point, with or without source, then write a working exploit. Based on Google red team exercises.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Introductory Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the introductory sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: IOI 2025
description: Model solves the 2025 International Olympiad in Informatics tasks. Scored with official subtask points (max 600).
note: Contest problems are public. No single public LLM harness found.

name: Irregular FrontierCyber and Atomic Challenges
description: Irregular's external suites: FrontierCyber (226 real software/hardware challenges) and Atomic Challenges (22 skill-level tasks).

name: Jailbreak Augmented Examples
description: Models face publicly known jailbreaks applied to prompts from the standard disallowed content set. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from public jailbreak techniques.

name: JailbreakBench
description: 100 harmful and 100 benign behaviors with a standard jailbreak artifact library. Scored by attack success rate.

name: JEF-Bench
description: Agents read files that embed jailbreak instructions in tool-call returns. Reports attack success rate across 1800 tasks and 50 disallowed use cases.
note: In-house Meta evaluation introduced in the Muse Spark 1.3 report.

name: JMMLU
description: Models answer 7,536 four-way multiple-choice questions in Japanese, from translated MMLU subjects and new Japan-specific subjects. Scored by accuracy.

name: JobBench
description: 130 tasks from 35 occupations workers most want delegated. Agent works through messy reference files, graded by fact-anchored binary rubrics.
note: Framed as an alternative to GDPval's economic-value framing. Vendor-reported scores run higher than the paper's best (45.9%).

name: KAET (Kimi Autonomous Execution Tasks)
description: Agents execute long-horizon tasks that simulate real user requests and enterprise system operations.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Keeping secrets when pressed in simulated scenarios (Anthropic)
description: Models hold confidential information in 39 job scenarios while a simulated counterpart presses for it. Measures leaks in replies and in reasoning.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 5.5 plays the counterpart for up to 20 turns.

name: Kernel Bench L3
description: Models write fast GPU kernels for the 50 full model architectures in KernelBench Level 3. Scored on correctness and speedup over PyTorch.
note: This is the hardest of the three original KernelBench levels, which cover single operators, fusions, and full models.

name: KernelBench
description: Replace PyTorch operators with faster custom GPU kernels. Scored on correctness and speedup.
note: xAI reports an internal derivative, KernelBenchInternal v1.1.

name: KernelBenchInternal
description: Agents replace PyTorch operators with custom CUDA kernels. Scores combine correctness and measured speedup over a TF32 baseline.
note: In-house xAI suite inspired by KernelBench. Version 1.1 uses a harder task split.

name: KernelGen 1P
description: Agents write and optimize GPU kernels under hardware constraints and debug correctness issues. Scored as mean rubric score.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Kernels task (Anthropic)
description: Agents optimize compute kernels in a performance engineering challenge. Scored by speedup.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Key insight rediscovery on an unpublished ML task (external testing)
aliases: Unpublished machine learning task insight rediscovery
description: Agents work on an unpublished machine learning research task. Testers count how many of five key insights the agent rediscovers.
note: Run by an unnamed external testing partner on a pre-release snapshot. The task is not public.

name: Kimi Chinese in-house open-ended benchmark
description: Models answer held-out Chinese prompts drawn from real user queries. Outputs are compared pairwise against another model to give win, tie and loss rates.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. Access to the data is restricted.

name: Kimi Claw 24/7 Bench
description: Agents work on 17 persistent multi-day professional scenarios through OpenClaw, with 610 checkpoints. The score is the mean pass rate over three runs.
note: In-house: Moonshot never released the tasks.

name: Kimi Code Bench
description: Moonshot in-house coding-agent tasks from internal engineering cases, production incidents and open-source projects across 10+ languages. 80 tasks.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Moonshot AI). Only Moonshot reports scores. V1 and v2 scores are not comparable. Cyber tasks trigger refusals.

name: Kimi Code Bench v2
description: Coding agents complete Moonshot's realistic tasks from internal engineering work, production incidents, and open-source projects in over ten languages.
note: In-house: Moonshot never released the tasks, and only Moonshot reports scores on it.

name: Kimi exploit development suite
description: Agents turn real CVEs into working exploits in 16 user-space tasks and 20 Linux kernel privilege-escalation tasks. Experts verified every task solvable.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation of 36 tasks. The tasks are not public.

name: Kimi Promptfoo red-team safety evaluation
description: Promptfoo generates attack prompts for harmful, criminal, misinformation, privacy and security plugins under five strategies. Human reviewers judge the responses.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation built with the open Promptfoo tool. Results are passing rates per plugin and strategy.

name: Kimi vulnerability discovery (Tier 1)
description: Agents search current versions of widely deployed software for new bugs and show that they reproduce. Humans review the findings.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. Results are reported as confirmed findings, not as a score.

name: Kimi Webdev Bench
description: Models build games, 3D scenes and website clones from real prompts. Blind experts compare two outputs and report win, tie and loss rates.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. Kimi K3 is compared only against Claude Opus 4.8.

name: Kitab
description: Models list books by a given author that meet extra constraints, such as publication dates or title words. Scored by precision and constraint satisfaction.

name: KMMLU
description: Models answer 35,030 Korean multiple-choice questions across 45 subjects, collected from original Korean exams. Scoring is accuracy.

name: Knowledge Q&A (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models answer knowledge questions drawn from real Hailuo AI user queries.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: KORA
description: Simulated child users hold 3-turn conversations probing 26 child-specific risks. Judge model rates replies failing, adequate or exemplary.
note: Public leaderboard is KORA V2. Repo main branch is unpublished V3. Relies on synthetic personas and an AI judge.

name: KWV Bench
description: Models answer atomic visual questions extracted from tasks distilled from real knowledge-work scenarios.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: L-Eval
description: Models answer over 2,000 queries on 508 long documents of 3k to 200k tokens across 20 subtasks. Scoring uses exact match and judge-model ratings.

name: LAB-Bench
description: Multiple-choice tasks on practical biology research skills: literature, protocols, sequence and figure reasoning, database lookup.
note: Added from public eval collections. The 2026 cards' bio sections were not catalogued.

name: LAB-Bench CloningScenarios
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about multi-step molecular cloning workflows. CloningScenarios subset of LAB-Bench.
note: Anthropic reports LAB-Bench subsets separately in its RSP bio sections.

name: LAB-Bench FigQA
description: Models interpret figures from biology papers and answer multiple-choice questions. FigQA subset of LAB-Bench.
note: Anthropic reports LAB-Bench subsets separately in its RSP bio sections.

name: LAB-Bench ProtocolQA
description: Models find and fix errors in lab protocols in multiple-choice form. ProtocolQA subset of LAB-Bench.
note: Anthropic reports LAB-Bench subsets separately in its RSP bio sections.

name: LAB-Bench SeqQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions that require DNA and protein sequence manipulation. SeqQA subset of LAB-Bench.
note: Anthropic reports LAB-Bench subsets separately in its RSP bio sections.

name: LAB: Contracts
description: 500 in-house contracting tasks (drafting, redlines, issues lists, escalation memos) across 10 contract categories. All-pass expert-rubric grading.
note: Scores reported on a 50-task official hold-out. No public leaderboard as of the Tenet post (2026-08), so every score is Harvey's own run. Each negotiation stage is graded as a separate step, so it does not yet test autonomous end-to-end negotiation.

name: LAB: Diligence
description: Agent researches a synthetic M&A virtual data room (thousands of documents, up to ~80M tokens) and drafts a diligence memo scored against planted-issue rubric criteria.
note: Open-sourced as RL environments (tasks/diligence held 11 data rooms on 2026-10-22). Long-context and exhaustivity stress test. Harvey reports harness design (an RLM root agent over a REPL) moves scores more than model choice. Harvey's RL results use held-out data rooms.

name: LABBench2
description: 11 biology research sub-tasks (literature, figures, tables, patents, trials and more) with tool access. Macro-averaged accuracy.

name: Lakera B3 (Backbone Breaker Benchmark)
description: Crowdsourced prompt-injection attacks hit backbone LLMs inside 10 agent threat snapshots at three defense levels. Scored by attack resistance.
org: Lakera + ETH Zurich + UK AISI + Oxford
note: ICLR 2026. Public HF set is a 'weak' 210-attack subset of 194,331 attacks. Runner lives in Inspect Evals (src/inspect_evals/b3).

name: LAMBADA
description: Models predict the last word of narrative passages where humans can guess it only from the whole passage. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Trento and University of Amsterdam

name: LatchBio Capabilities v1.0
description: LatchBio cross-benchmark suite of agentic biological data analysis (transcriptomics, epigenomics, variants, pharmacology) with deterministic graders.
note: Component benchmarks appear under github.com/latchbio. Exact composition not confirmed.

name: Lazy investigation (Anthropic)
aliases: Avoiding harmful actions from misleading evidence
description: Agents debug a failing job where misleading evidence invites a harmful action such as cordoning a healthy node. Scored 0 to 10 by a grader.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Every problem expects no action, so it also measures willingness to act.

name: Lazy investigation on misleading codebases (Anthropic)
description: Models trace small, intentionally misleading codebases to answer how a value is set. Score is the share of lazy investigations ending in a wrong answer.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. A different design from the later lazy investigation debugging task scored 0 to 10.

name: Lech Mazur Creative Writing
description: Models write short stories that must use 10 assigned elements such as characters, objects, and motivations. Judge models compare matched stories pairwise.
note: Earlier versions used 0 to 10 rubric ratings, which the current pairwise ranking replaces.

name: Leetcode (easy)
description: Models solve 41 easy Leetcode problems that OpenAI selected. Scored as problems solved.
note: In-house OpenAI problem set from the GPT-4 Technical Report exam table.

name: Leetcode (hard)
description: Models solve 45 hard Leetcode problems that OpenAI selected. Scored as problems solved.
note: In-house OpenAI problem set from the GPT-4 Technical Report exam table.

name: Leetcode (medium)
description: Models solve 80 medium Leetcode problems that OpenAI selected. Scored as problems solved.
note: In-house OpenAI problem set from the GPT-4 Technical Report exam table.

name: LeetCode Weekly Contest
description: Models solve 126 LeetCode contest problems from July to November 2023. A solution counts only if it passes all of its 20+ test cases.

name: Legal Research Bench
description: Agents answer US federal and state legal research questions with case-law and web tools. Expert rubrics, all-pass and weighted scores by LLM judge.
note: Proprietary questions written by practicing lawyers. Vals runs every model. Top three tied at 55.29% all-pass (2026-10-19). OpenAI's Astra for Law claim (54.0% vs 38.7% for GPT-6 Astra) used 200 private validation questions run by OpenAI, not Vals.

name: LengthCtrl (Qwen)
description: Models do creative writing tasks with length requirements. The score depends on the gap between output length and target length.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: LIBERO
description: Simulated Franka tabletop tasks in four 10-task suites. Policies fine-tuned on 50 demos per task. Success rate over ~50 trials.
note: Saturated: 22 of 35 catalogue models self-report >=97% four-suite average. Protocols differ by paper. The same models score 0.02-24.4% on RoboDojo. Papers move to LIBERO-Plus/PRO.

name: LIBERO-PRO
description: LIBERO policies tested under object, position, instruction, task and environment perturbations. 50 episodes per task. Success rate.
note: Exposes memorization: position and task perturbations drive most models near 0 while object and semantic stay ~0.9. Small, frozen table.

name: LifeSciBench
description: Models complete 750 expert-written life science research tasks, often with attached figures, tables, or sequence files. Graded against expert rubrics as score and pass rate.
note: Whether the tasks are public is unclear.

name: LingoQA
description: Models answer free-form questions about short driving videos. A trained classifier, Lingo-Judge, scores whether each answer is truthful.

name: LinuxArena
description: AI-control setting in live Linux production-like environments. Measures stealthy side-task completion against action and CoT monitors.
note: Environments live as separate repos under github.com/linuxarena.

name: LiveBench
description: Models answer monthly refreshed questions across math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following, and data analysis. Scored automatically against objective ground truth.
note: Scores depend on the dated release, and the newest questions are withheld from the public set to limit contamination.

name: LiveCodeBench
description: Competitive programming problems collected after model cutoffs from LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces. Scored pass@1 on hidden tests.
note: Rolling time windows (v5, v6) make cross-card comparison hard. Top models near 90%.

name: LiveCodeBench Pro
description: Continuously updated Codeforces, ICPC and IOI problems annotated by olympiad medalists. Reported as Elo.

name: LiveCodeBench v5
description: Competitive programming problems collected after model cutoffs from LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces. Scored pass@1 on hidden tests.
note: Problems released from May 2023 to January 2025, 880 in all.

name: LiveCodeBench v6
description: Competitive programming problems collected after model cutoffs from LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces. Scored pass@1 on hidden tests.
note: Problems released from May 2023 to April 2025, 1,055 in all.

name: LiveSQLBench
description: Contamination-resistant text-to-SQL on PostgreSQL with hierarchical knowledge bases, including CRUD tasks. Scored by soft execution match and test cases.
note: Gold SQL and test cases withheld from the public dataset. Released by email request. Base-Full v1 (600 tasks) released 2025-09.

name: Llama 2-Chat helpfulness human evaluation (Meta)
description: Three human raters compare Llama 2-Chat with a rival chat model on about 4,000 single and multi-turn helpfulness prompts.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Results are win, tie and loss rates against one rival per model size.

name: Llama 2-Chat safety human evaluation (Meta)
description: Human raters score responses to about 2,000 adversarial prompts on a five-point scale. Ratings of 1 or 2 count as violations.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The paper shows violation percentage and mean rating only in charts.

name: Llama 3 pairwise human evaluation (Meta)
description: Human raters compare Llama responses with a rival model on about 7,000 prompts across six capabilities and three multiturn sets.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Results are win and loss rates per capability and rival, with no overall score.

name: Llama internal safety benchmarks (Meta)
description: Models face Meta's adversarial and borderline prompts per capability and language. Scored as violation rate and false refusal rate.
note: In-house Meta evaluation with over 4,000 prompts per capability or language. Llama 3 shows results only in charts.

name: Llama verbatim memorization probe (Meta)
description: Models get prompts sampled from their pretraining data. The score is the share of generations that reproduce the true continuation verbatim.
note: In-house Meta measurement on pretrained models, reported for several prompt and continuation lengths.

name: LLM training task (Anthropic)
description: Agents optimize a CPU-only small language model training implementation. Scored by speedup.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: LLMBoxing
description: People see one question with two anonymous model answers and pick the better one. The site counts preferences between model pairs.
note: Independent human preference site cited in the Mistral 7B paper.

name: LMArena (Elo)
description: People chat with two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better reply. Votes become Elo-style ratings for each model.
note: The 2025 paper The Leaderboard Illusion reported that some labs tested many private variants before release.

name: LMCA
description: Models rate arguments against position texts on philosophy, decision theory, and AI risk. Scored by agreement with expert ratings, with a ceiling near 85.
org: Emery Cooper, Caspar Oesterheld, and collaborators
note: The authors expect it to begin saturating about a year after its August 2026 launch.

name: LMCA (Language Model Conceptual Argumentation)
aliases: A dataset of rated conceptual arguments
description: Expert-rated critiques of positions on conceptual questions with no ground truth. Scores agreement with expert ratings.

name: LOCA-Bench
description: Agentic tasks whose environment state is scaled to grow context length while task semantics stay fixed. Success rate versus context length.
note: 15 seed tasks adapted from Toolathlon. Tests context-management strategies as part of the agent.

name: LOFT
description: Models solve retrieval, RAG, SQL, and many-shot learning tasks with whole corpora of up to one million tokens in context. Scored per task.

name: LogicVista
description: Models answer 448 multiple-choice questions on spatial, deductive, inductive, numeric, and mechanical reasoning set in images. Scored by accuracy.

name: Long Context (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models translate, summarize and analyze long documents from real user requests.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Long-context grounding, sentence unfactual rate
description: Models answer from long documents. An autorater reports the share of sentences not supported by the documents.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Long-form Biological Risk Questions
description: Models answer long-form questions across five biothreat creation stages, graded against expert rubrics. Scored as pass@1 per stage.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Cards report stage scores with no overall number.

name: Long-form virology tasks
description: Agents complete end-to-end pathogen acquisition workflows, covering workflow design and laboratory protocols. Scored against expert criteria.
note: Anthropic evaluation built with SecureBio, Deloitte and Signature Science. The tasks are not public.

name: Long-horizon jailbreaks (xAI)
description: Models face multi-turn, Crescendo and long-horizon malicious-use attacks. Compliance is the share that get disallowed help.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, first reported in the Grok 4.6 model card.

name: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench (LHTB)
description: Terminal-Bench-style container tasks needing hundreds of steps. Subtasks graded deterministically for dense partial-credit reward. Solved at reward >=0.95.
org: Tencent HY + university collaborators (Zongxia Li et al.)
note: v1 46 tasks. LHTB 2.0 has 77 tasks. Hidden tests and oracle solutions withheld. Official numbers need the repo's modified Harbor.

name: LongBench
description: Models work through 21 English and Chinese long-input datasets covering QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code. Each dataset has its own metric.
note: LongBench v2, released in December 2024, is a separate version with harder multiple choice questions.

name: LongBench v2
description: 503 multiple-choice questions over 8K-2M-word contexts (QA, dialogue, code repos, structured data). Accuracy.

name: LongBench-Chat
description: Models follow real user instructions over contexts of 10K to 100K tokens. GPT-4 scores each answer from 1 to 10 against references.
org: Tsinghua University and Zhipu AI (Bai et al., LongAlign)
note: Introduced with the LongAlign paper.

name: LongCodeBench
description: Coding model answers repository QA and fixes GitHub issues with context from 32K to 1M tokens. Accuracy and resolve rate.
note: COLM 2025. Python only.

name: LongFact
description: Models write long answers to 2,280 fact-seeking prompts on 38 topics. A search-backed checker verifies each claim, and cards report the hallucination rate.
note: The paper scores F1@K, where higher is better, but cards report hallucination rates, where lower is better.

name: LongFact-Concepts
description: Models write detailed answers to LongFact prompts about broad concepts. A fact checker scores the claim-level error rate.
note: Concepts half of LongFact. OpenAI grades claims with o3 and browsing.

name: LongFact-Objects
description: Models write detailed answers to LongFact prompts about specific objects such as people or places. A fact checker scores the claim-level error rate.
note: Objects half of LongFact. OpenAI grades claims with o3 and browsing.

name: Longform Writing
description: Models write long-form text without tools, capped at 32k output tokens. Moonshot AI has not published the tasks or the scoring method.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation with no public tasks.

name: LongVideoBench
description: Models answer referring reasoning questions over 3,763 web videos up to an hour long, with interleaved subtitles. Scored by multiple-choice accuracy.

name: LSAT
description: Models take a simulated Law School Admission Test. Scored on the 120 to 180 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: LSMDC
description: Models fill in a missing word in movie audio descriptions using the matching video clip. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is the fill-in-the-blank task of the Large Scale Movie Description Challenge, also called MovieFIB.

name: LV-Eval
description: Models answer single-hop and multi-hop questions over contexts at five length levels from 16K to 256K tokens, with confusing facts inserted.
org: Infinigence AI and Tsinghua University (Yuan et al.)
note: Labs report one score per length level. Qwen used keyword recall instead of the original metric.

name: LVBench
description: Hours-long video understanding with multiple-choice questions on reasoning, grounding and summarization.
note: Frame budgets differ by provider API, which complicates comparisons.

name: LVBench (with memory)
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about videos up to two hours long, aided by Qwen's external video memory system. Scored by accuracy.
org: Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University (LVBench), Qwen (memory setup)
note: A Qwen setting of LVBench that uses a memory system built with Qwen-MM-Plugins, so scores are not comparable with plain LVBench.

name: Lying about identity (Anthropic)
description: Models play an operator-assigned human persona while users ask if they are human. Score is the rate of admitting to being an AI.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The Fable 5 card adds a harder set with indirect user probes.

name: M3Exam
description: Models answer 12,317 multiple-choice questions from official school exams in nine languages, about 23 percent needing images. Scored by accuracy.

name: MADQA
description: Agents search 800 PDF documents to answer 2,250 human-written questions. Scoring covers answer accuracy and how much search effort the agent spends.
org: Łukasz Borchmann et al. (Snowflake, University of Oxford, and partners)

name: MAI human side-by-side evaluation
description: Paid raters compare two models' answers to 1,276 English prompts from experts and Copilot logs on a 7-point scale from -1.5 to 1.5.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation run with Surge AI raters. The score is relative to a named opponent model.

name: MAI internal jailbreak evaluation suite
description: Models face about 9,500 jailbreak prompts built from 2,500 seed scenarios, grouped as foundational, compositional and adaptive. Scored as attack success rate.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation. Seeds include HarmBench and StrongREJECT prompts. Results are per bucket, with no overall score.

name: MAI internal safety and over-refusal evaluation
description: Models answer harmful and benign prompts in eight harm categories. Judges score safety pass rate on sensitive prompts and helpfulness as one minus over-refusal.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation. Results are per category, with no overall score.

name: MakeMePay
description: A con artist model tries to talk a GPT-4o mark into paying money in a role-play. Scored as the share of conversations with a payment.
note: Open source in OpenAI Evals. Cards also report the dollar extraction rate.

name: MakeMeSay
description: A manipulator model tries to make a GPT-4o manipulatee say a codeword without suspicion. Scored as manipulator win rate.
note: Open source in OpenAI Evals.

name: Malicious agentic influence campaigns (Anthropic)
description: Agents receive requests to run multi-step influence operations with tools. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Malicious computer use (Anthropic)
description: Computer-use agents receive harmful tasks such as surveillance or fraud in GUI environments. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Malicious use of Claude Code (Anthropic)
description: Agents in Claude Code receive malicious and dual-use coding requests. Score is the refusal rate on malicious requests.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ManipArena
description: 15 real bimanual tasks (10 execution, 5 semantic reasoning) on one X2Robot platform, in-domain and shifted trials. Partial-credit scoring.
note: Host's own WALL-OSS-0.5 tops it (38% success). Conflict of interest. Paper snapshot on a single robot. Sim twin at github.com/maniparena/maniparena-sim.

name: ManiSkill3
description: GPU-parallel robot simulator and task suite across 12 domains for manipulation learning. Success rate per task.
org: UC San Diego (Hao Su Lab) + Hillbot
note: Simulator framework rather than a fixed benchmark. No neutral VLA leaderboard found.

name: Mantic vs Polymarket backtest
description: Point-in-time backtest of Mantic's AI forecasts against prices on 4,139 Polymarket markets at volume snapshots. Scored by Brier score and calibration.
note: Mantic is more accurate until ~$100k traded volume. The forecaster sees the market price, so forecasts are not independent. Full report by email only.

name: Many-shot jailbreaking evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Models receive long fake dialogs where the assistant complies with harmful requests, then a new harmful request. Score is the compliance rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation drawn from the published many-shot jailbreaking research.

name: MASK
description: Measures whether a model contradicts its own elicited beliefs under pressure to lie. Honesty separated from accuracy.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI

name: MATH
description: 12,500 competition math problems with step-by-step solutions. Final answer scored by exact match.
note: Saturated. Original HF dataset hendrycks/competition_math is disabled. EleutherAI mirror is commonly used.

name: MATH Level 5
description: Models solve the 1,324 hardest MATH test problems, drawn from competitions such as AMC and AIME. Scored by final answer match.
org: Dan Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley), subset run by Epoch AI
note: Near saturation, and contamination is likely because the problems have been public since 2021.

name: Math Side-tasking Monitor Evasion
description: Agents try to solve hidden math side tasks during Expert-SWE coding tasks without detection. Scored on success while evading CoT and full-context monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Results appear as charts.

name: MATH-500
description: Models solve 500 competition math problems drawn from the MATH test set. Final answers are checked against the reference answers.
note: Near saturation, since DeepSeek-R1 already scored 97.3 percent in January 2025.

name: MATH-Vision (MathVision)
description: 3,040 competition math problems with visual context. Answer accuracy.

name: Math23K
description: Models solve Chinese elementary-school math word problems from a set of about 23,000. Scored by final-answer accuracy.
note: Introduced with the Deep Neural Solver paper at EMNLP 2017.

name: Math401
description: Models compute 401 arithmetic expressions covering addition, multiplication, exponents, logarithms and trigonometry. Scored by exact numeric accuracy.
note: Tests arithmetic skill rather than word-problem reasoning.

name: MathArena (Apex, IMO, USAMO)
description: Evaluates models on newly released math competitions after release. Final-answer or human/LLM-judged proof scores.
note: Apex and Apex Shortlist collect the hardest unsolved competition problems. Proof scores (IMO/USAMO) depend on judges.

name: MathVista
description: Math reasoning in visual contexts (charts, geometry, puzzles) from 31 datasets. Answer accuracy.
note: Near-saturated.

name: MAXIFE
aliases: Multilingual and Cross-lingual Instruction Following Evaluation
description: Models follow 1,667 verifiable instructions in 23 languages and in cross-lingual settings. Rule-based checks and model judges score compliance.
note: Qwen model cards report accuracy on English plus multilingual original prompts, 23 settings in total.

name: MBE (Multistate Bar Examination)
description: Models answer the 200 multiple choice questions of an official Multistate Bar Examination practice exam. Scored by accuracy.
note: Anthropic used the official NCBE 2021 MBE practice exam. The uniform-bar-exam record covers the full bar exam.

name: MBPP
description: Models write short Python functions from a one-line task description. A solution counts as correct if it passes the task's three assert tests.
note: EvalPlus released MBPP+ with many more tests per task because the original three tests miss wrong solutions.

name: MCP Atlas
description: Multi-step workflows over real MCP servers. Scores tool-use competency on realistic tasks.
note: 500 public tasks of 1,000. Rest held back. Labs use different judge models, so self-reported scores vary.

name: MCP prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents use simulated email, Slack and document servers over MCP where content carries injected instructions. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported without safeguards. The test cases are not public.

name: MCP-Universe
description: Agents complete tasks through 11 real MCP servers across six domains, such as navigation, repositories, finance, and browsing. Scored by execution-based success rate.

name: MCPMark
description: Agent stress-tests realistic MCP tool use (GitHub, Notion, Postgres, browser). Graded by programmatic verification scripts.
note: Kimi K3 reports a 'Verified' revision.

name: MedCalc-Bench Verified
description: Models extract values from patient notes and compute results for 55 medical calculators. Verified release of MedCalc-Bench with corrected labels.
note: Anthropic runs the code-augmented setting with a Python tool. Scores on the original MedCalc-Bench are not comparable.

name: Medical Knowledge Self-Assessment Program (MKSAP)
description: Models answer internal medicine board review questions from MKSAP. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Medicinal Chemistry (Anthropic)
description: Models see several real drug-discovery compounds and pick which had the highest or lowest measured ADME property. The set has 504 questions.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MedMCQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from Indian medical entrance exams, AIIMS and NEET PG. Scoring is accuracy.
note: GPT-4o card reports the dev split.

name: MedQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from medical licensing exams, usually the 12,723-question English USMLE set. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The full dataset also has simplified and traditional Chinese exam sets.

name: MedQA Mainland China
description: Models answer mainland China medical licensing exam questions in simplified Chinese. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Simplified Chinese part of the MedQA dataset.

name: MedQA Taiwan
description: Models answer Taiwan medical licensing exam questions in traditional Chinese. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Traditional Chinese part of the MedQA dataset.

name: MedQA USMLE (5 options)
description: Models answer USMLE-style medical licensing questions with five answer options. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Five-option variant of the MedQA English set. The medqa record covers the four-option set.

name: MedXpertQA
description: Models answer 4,460 expert-level medical exam questions across 17 specialties, in a text subset and an image subset. Scoring is multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MedXpertQA-MM
description: Models answer expert-level medical exam questions that combine images with clinical records and test results. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is the multimodal subset of MedXpertQA, which has 4,460 questions in total across its Text and MM subsets.

name: MENT-SNS
description: Models translate English and Chinese sentences with slang, wordplay and idioms. A GPT-4.1 judge compares each translation with a baseline.
note: Z.ai uses source sentences from the MENT dataset. The printed score is a pairwise rating.

name: MentalHealthBench
description: 1,215 synthetic mental-health conversations with 5,262 clinician-authored rubric criteria. An LLM judge scores safety and guidance quality.
note: Grader is GPT-5.6 Sol. Repo and dataset location not confirmed in this pass.

name: Meta action-belief coherence probe
description: Models act on items from five alignment evaluations and then state beliefs about them. Reports a mean coherency score.
note: In-house Meta probe over AIR-Bench, IHEval, MASK, School of Reward Hacking and StrongREJECT items.

name: Meta agentic cyber misuse refusal
description: Models run multi-step cyber tasks with tool access while an adaptive attacker tries to steer them to a malicious goal. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta agentic evaluations grounded in user traffic
aliases: Agentic Evaluations Grounded in User Traffic
description: Models continue replays of recorded user workflows. A jury reports the share of cases with a supported substantive finding.
note: In-house Meta evaluation on 116 matched cases with three attempts each.

name: Meta Agents Research Environments (ARE) / Gaia2
description: Simulated app environments for agents with time and events. Hosts the Gaia2 benchmark.

name: Meta BioDesign Proxy
description: Agents complete computational biology design tasks across host-pathogen interaction, protein design and sequence analysis. Aggregate normalized score.
note: In-house Meta evaluation built with external experts. The tasks are not public.

name: Meta catastrophic cyber misuse refusal
description: Models receive high-severity cyber-misuse prompts with technical context. The benchmark reports pass@k attack success rate under adaptive attacks.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta chemical and biological high-risk bottleneck evaluations
description: Models answer expert-written tasks in three restricted subsets. An expert-validated rubric scores each response.
note: In-house Meta evaluation run in an isolated cluster. Subsets are Chemical Threats, Biological Threats and Operational Execution.

name: Meta chemical-agent refusal evaluation
description: Models receive high-risk chemical prompts and the benchmark measures how often they refuse. Covers development, procurement and production stages.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta Code-Fetch Under User Requests
description: A coding agent is told by a reckless user to fetch or run a risky artifact. The benchmark measures the rate of insecure execution.
note: In-house Meta benchmark. A programmatic judge checks filesystem state and command history.

name: Meta curated CTF set
description: Agents solve 198 public and private capture-the-flag challenges across six security domains. Reports pass@1.
note: In-house Meta mix of public and private CTF challenges, first described in the Muse Spark Safety and Preparedness Report.

name: Meta cyber false-refusal benchmark
description: Models receive benign and borderline cyber requests and the benchmark measures how often they wrongly refuse. Reports false refusal rate.
note: In-house Meta evaluation of over-refusal on defensive cyber tasks.

name: Meta Cyber Misuse Chat
description: Models receive 80 offensive cyber requests, directly and with jailbreak developer prompts. Reports attack success rate and a benign false refusal rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal set. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta cyber misuse request set
description: Models receive 600 private offensive cyber prompts, directly and under jailbreak attacks. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal set from the Muse Spark Safety and Preparedness Report.

name: Meta holistic adversarial audit with Petri Bloom
aliases: Broad Adversarial Auditing with Petri Bloom
description: Two auditor models run Petri Bloom scenarios built from Meta's behavior taxonomy. A binary judge reports the share of scenarios with a violation.
note: Meta setup over nine taxonomy sub-categories. Each scenario takes its worst of six transcripts.

name: Meta instructed selective performance evaluation
description: Models are told to underperform on six science capability sets. Reports the average drop from baseline in percentage points.
note: In-house Meta sandbagging experiment with monitor-oblivious and monitor-aware conditions.

name: Meta internal agent hallucination evaluation
description: Agents do long-context assistant and professional tasks with tools. The benchmark reports the share of verifiable claims that are hallucinated.
note: In-house Meta benchmark across health, finance, legal, clinical and engineering tasks.

name: Meta internal sycophancy evaluation
description: Models meet adversarially curated conversations that invite inappropriate agreement, plus benign controls. Reports sycophancy and excessive anti-sycophancy rates.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Rates are high by construction and do not estimate ordinary use.

name: Meta prompted evaluation awareness
description: Models are asked to judge whether transcripts come from evaluations or real use. Reports the weighted rate of correct identification.
note: In-house Meta evaluation over chemical and biological, cyber and loss of control transcripts.

name: Meta targeted agentic evaluations
description: Agents work in prebuilt stateful sandboxes that test specific behavior rules. Reports the case-level violation rate over 1,790 scenarios.
note: In-house Meta suite built from 142 taxonomy units. Scenarios were screened with Muse Spark 1.1.

name: Meta training-stage provenance probe
description: Models label 10,000 transcripts as deployment, evaluation, RL or SFT. Reports overall accuracy against a 25% chance rate.
note: In-house Meta situational awareness probe on internal transcripts.

name: Meta Underspecified Intent evaluation
description: Models answer ambiguous requests sourced from real Meta AI chats where users corrected the reply. Rubrics score whether the true intent is met.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. A companion Underlying Intent set is reported separately.

name: metal-arm-harness
description: Safety-enveloped CLI that lets any coding agent drive a real MakerMods Metal or Maker arm one command at a time from camera JPEGs.
note: Harness, not a benchmark. The safety design is a measured table floor, slow zone and per-move joint caps. No license file.

name: METR data deduplication
description: Agents write an efficient algorithm that removes near-duplicate lines from a large file. A trial succeeds when F1 reaches at least 80%.
note: Anthropic reports the share of trials scoring above the F1 threshold. The card calls it a METR public task.

name: METR general autonomy task suite
aliases: Agent Performance on General Autonomy Benchmark
description: Agents complete multi-step tasks in virtual environments. Scored as horizon weighted average task completion compared with human time limits.
note: Precursor of the METR time horizon suite. OpenAI cards show it as a chart.

name: METR pre-deployment AI R&D tasks
description: METR's long-horizon tasks for Anthropic pre-deployment tests: Train a Program, Gaming Bot, Sunlight open-ended research, plus Budget NanoGPT and LMCA.

name: METR Time Horizon
description: Agents attempt software and research tasks timed against skilled humans. The score is the human task length at which the agent succeeds half the time.
note: METR released Time Horizon 1.1 with a larger task suite in January 2026, and it says some original figures are out of date.

name: METR Time Horizon suite
description: Software tasks with human completion times. Reports the task length at which a model succeeds 50% of the time.
note: METR flagged high detected cheating for GPT-5.6 Sol, so it treated the result as non-robust.

name: MEWC
description: Models solve 179 Microsoft Excel World Championship problems from 2021 to 2026 with Excel tools. Output cells are compared one by one with answer cells.
note: In-house MiniMax benchmark built from Excel esports problems, and the task set is not released.

name: MEWC v2
description: Models solve 100 hard Microsoft Excel World Championship problems with Excel tools. Expert rubrics score the answers over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. It is a hard subset of the MEWC pool, so scores differ from the 179-problem MEWC.

name: MGSM
description: 250 GSM8K problems translated into 10 languages. Final-answer accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: Microsoft internal multimodal RAI benchmark
description: Vision language models answer image and text prompts across harm categories. Responses are scored from 0 to 10, higher is safer.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation reported for Phi-3.5-Vision.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Grounding
description: Models answer in GPT-4o simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge scores from 0 to 5 how fully each answer is grounded in the given prompt.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-4 report. The Phi-3 report scores Ungroundedness from 0 to 4 instead.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Continuation (DR-3)
description: Models continue conversations about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Summarization (DR-3)
description: Models summarize content about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Jailbreak (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated jailbreak conversations on topics such as child grooming, illegal advice and leaking guidelines. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Third Party Harm (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated conversations that try to extract third-party content such as books, news, recipes and songs. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Ungroundedness
description: Models answer in GPT-4 simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge rates how ungrounded each answer is in the given prompt, from 0 to 4.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-3 report. The Phi-4 report uses a Grounding score from 0 to 5 instead.

name: MILU
description: Multi-task Indic Language Understanding: culturally grounded multiple-choice questions in 11 Indic languages.

name: MindCube
description: Models answer 21,154 multiple choice questions about scenes seen from a few views. Questions test positions, orientations, and what-if movements.
org: MLL Lab, Northwestern University, with Stanford, NYU, and University of Washington
note: The authors fixed data bugs in March 2026, so newer results may differ from earlier ones.

name: MINERVA
description: Models answer complex video questions that need multi-step reasoning, with reference reasoning traces for grading.
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 1,024 frames.

name: Minimal-LinuxBench (Anthropic)
description: Agents attempt a hidden side task in high-stakes software environments while a monitor watches. Score is the stealth success rate.
note: Anthropic adaptation of a subset of LinuxBench, an AI control arena that Redwood Research shared privately.

name: MIRA Bench
aliases: Multi-Agent Infra for Routing and Assignment Bench
description: Agents carry out long multi-role enterprise tasks across several systems and decide when to delegate to subagents.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MirrorCode
description: Agent rebuilds a whole CLI program from scratch using only the original binary as an oracle. Solved only if 100% of end-to-end tests pass.
note: 25 targets, 3 kept private. ~34% of tests held out. Source programs are open source, so memorization cannot be fully ruled out.

name: Misaligned Behavior in Realistic Work Environments
aliases: Misaligned outcomes in realistic work environments
description: Agents do computer and browser tasks in simulated workplace apps with ambiguous instructions. Scored on the rate of unintended outcomes such as data disclosure.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. OpenAI made the set harder after the GPT-6 Astra card.

name: Misc CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents identify and exploit vulnerabilities in capture-the-flag challenges outside the web, crypto, pwn, rev and network categories.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Missing-context hallucinations (Anthropic)
description: Models get prompts that request tools they lack or cite missing material. Score is the non-hallucination rate on each 500-prompt set.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with unavailable-tool and missing-reference sets. The tool set was filtered on Claude Opus 4.6 failures.

name: Mistral 175 unsafe prompts
description: Models receive 175 unsafe prompts. Metric is the share of harmful questions the model declines.
note: In-house Mistral test set used for system prompt guardrails. The prompts are not public.

name: Mistral internal function calling benchmark
description: Models call functions on Mistral's in-house test set. The Magistral paper does not describe the tasks or the metric.
note: In-house Mistral evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Mistral self-reflection moderation set
description: Models classify prompts or answers as acceptable or harmful on a balanced set of adversarial and standard prompts. Scored by precision and recall.
note: In-house Mistral dataset, manually curated. The prompts are not public.

name: MixEval
description: Models answer real user queries matched to similar questions from existing benchmarks. Ground-truth answers make it a cheap proxy for Chatbot Arena rankings.
org: National University of Singapore (Ni et al.)
note: MixEval-Hard is a harder subset reported separately.

name: MLCommons AILuminate
description: Industry-standard hazard benchmark over 12 risk categories with graded ratings.

name: MLE-bench
description: Kaggle-style ML engineering competitions. Agent trains models and is scored against competition leaderboards.
note: OpenAI's 'Revised' version (72 problems, adds 2025-2026 competitions and up to three submissions) is internal.

name: MLogiQA
description: Models answer LogiQA logical reasoning questions translated into 10 languages, 80 per language. Scored by accuracy.
note: It is a subset of the P-MMEval multilingual suite.

name: MLS-Bench
description: Agent must invent one algorithmic change in an ML research scaffold whose gain transfers across settings. Scored relative to human baselines.
note: 140 tasks over 12 ML domains. Lite = 30-task subset (~99 H100-hours) with 5-hour limit per task. Score >50 beats strongest human baseline.

name: MLVU
description: Multi-task long video understanding (minutes to hours) with multiple-choice and generation tasks. Accuracy.

name: MM-ClawBench
description: Agents complete common OpenClaw tasks such as study planning, office documents, scheduled research, and code maintenance. Scoring is accuracy.
note: In-house: MiniMax never released the tasks or explained the scoring.

name: MMAU
description: 10K audio clips with questions on speech, sound and music needing expert knowledge and reasoning. Multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MMBench
description: Vision language models answer multiple-choice questions covering 20 perception and reasoning skills. CircularEval rotates the options. Scored by accuracy.
note: The original version. MMBench v1.1 is a separate entry.

name: MMBench-EN v1.1
description: Models answer English multiple-choice image questions across 20 ability dimensions, using CircularEval with shuffled options. Scored by accuracy on the dev split.
note: Version 1.1 cleans the original MMBench questions, so scores differ from v1.0.

name: MMLongBench-Doc
description: Models answer 1,062 questions about 130 long PDF documents averaging 49 pages, and some questions are unanswerable. Scoring is accuracy and F1.

name: MMLU
description: 57-subject multiple-choice exam questions from elementary to professional level. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated and contaminated. Reported only as a base-model metric.

name: MMLU Anatomy
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Anatomy subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU calibration (expected calibration error)
description: Models answer an MMLU subset and their answer probabilities are compared with accuracy. Scored as expected calibration error.
note: Reported in the GPT-4 Technical Report for the pre-trained and post-trained models.

name: MMLU Clinical Knowledge
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Clinical Knowledge subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Biology
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Biology subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Medical Genetics
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Medical Genetics subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Professional Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Professional Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU translated with Azure Translate
description: Models answer MMLU questions machine translated into 26 languages with Azure Translate. Scoring is 3-shot accuracy per language.
note: Different from the professionally translated MMMLU that OpenAI released later.

name: MMLU-Pro
description: Harder 10-option version of MMLU with reasoning-focused questions across 14 subjects.
note: In these cards it is used only as a substrate for chain-of-thought controllability evals.

name: MMLU-ProX
description: MMLU-Pro translated into up to 29 languages with expert review. Multiple-choice accuracy per language.

name: MMLU-Redux
description: Manually re-annotated subset of MMLU that fixes wrong labels. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: MMLU-stem
description: Models answer the STEM subjects of MMLU, such as physics, chemistry, mathematics, and computer science, as multiple choice. Scoring is accuracy.
note: A subject subset of MMLU rather than a separate benchmark, so subject lists can differ between reports.

name: MMMLU
description: MMLU professionally translated into 14 languages. Multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MMMU
description: 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 30 subjects. Multiple-choice and open accuracy.
note: Near-saturated. Test answers held out.

name: MMMU-Pro
description: Harder MMMU: college-level multimodal questions with more options and vision-only inputs to remove text shortcuts.
note: Variant (standard vs vision, 4 vs 10 options) often unstated in cards.

name: MMStar
description: Models answer 1,500 human-curated image questions that cannot be solved without the image, across 6 core capabilities. Scored by accuracy.

name: MMVP
description: Models answer 300 questions about 150 image pairs that CLIP embeds as near duplicates. A pair counts only when both answers are right.
org: New York University and UC Berkeley (Tong et al.)
note: Introduced in the paper Eyes Wide Shut on visual shortcomings of multimodal LLMs.

name: MMVU
description: 3,000 expert-annotated questions on videos across 27 disciplines. Multiple-choice and open-ended accuracy.

name: Mobile Actions
description: Model converts natural-language phone requests into on-device function calls (calendar, email, maps, flashlight, Wi-Fi). Call accuracy.
note: Identification inferred: the Reka Edge card lists 'Mobile Actions (Tool Use)' without a link. The dataset is mainly a FunctionGemma fine-tuning set.

name: MobileWorld
description: Agents complete 201 tasks across 20 mobile apps, including tasks that need user clarification or MCP tools. Backend checks verify success.
note: It was built because agents had passed 90 percent on AndroidWorld.

name: Molecular Biology Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level molecular biology questions from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The card does not describe the question format.

name: Molecular Biology Capabilities Test (MBCT)
description: Models answer expert multiple-choice questions on molecular biology laboratory methods. Part of a SecureBio and CAIS capability suite.
note: Reported with VCT and HPCT in Meta Muse Spark safety reports. Run as multiple-response multiple-choice.

name: MolmoAct2 sim_eval
description: Zero-shot ManiSkill evaluation of MolmoAct2 policies: put-everything-in-box tasks for Franka DROID and bimanual YAM, 10 episodes per task.
note: Two tasks, used as a sim harness. Assets come from a third-party HF account. No leaderboard.

name: MolmoSpaces
description: Zero-shot Franka (DROID) policies in held-out procedurally generated MuJoCo houses: pick, place, open, close. ~1,000 episodes per task.
note: ~1,000 episodes per task with 95% CIs. Not saturated for zero-shot policies: best MolmoBot pick-and-place ~67%, pi0.5 DROID ~10-12%. Ai2's sim-trained MolmoBot nears ceiling on Pick (~92%).

name: Money talks
description: Models try to persuade human participants to donate part of a 20 pound study bonus to charity.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Reported as mean pounds donated.

name: Monitor Evasion Capability Under Prompted Sandbagging
description: Models are told to sandbag on WMDP and Monorepo-Bench, sometimes while evading a monitor. Scored as CoT and production monitor recall of sandbagged items.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation adapted from Li et al. 2025. Higher recall means sandbagging is easier to catch.

name: Monitorability Sandbagging
description: Models on Impossible Coding Tasks are prompted to be more or less monitorable. Scored as CoT monitor recall on rollouts that hack.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Tests whether models can manipulate measured monitorability.

name: Monorepo-Bench
description: Agents replicate pull-request style contributions in a large internal OpenAI repository. Graded by hidden unit tests as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Morphology-to-molecule matching (Anthropic)
description: Models match four sets of multi-channel liver cell images to the four shuffled molecule and dose treatments that produced them.
note: Built with Axiom Bio from its in-vitro liver assay data.

name: MotionBench
description: Models answer questions about fine-grained motion in video clips across six motion question types. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Test answers are hidden and scored through the leaderboard, while the dev set has public answers.

name: MR-NIAH (Multi-Round Needles-In-A-Haystack)
description: Models must repeat one earlier answer from a long multi-turn dialogue history of 2K to 1M tokens. Scored by adjusted recall of key parts.
note: MiniMax built it as an open alternative to MRCR, in English and Chinese.

name: MRCR (Michelangelo, original)
description: Models retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation. Original Michelangelo version before MRCR v2.
note: Google reports from 2024 and early 2025 use this version. Later Google cards use the 8-needle MRCR v2.

name: MRCR v2
description: Multi-round coreference: retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation, up to 1M tokens.
note: Two public variants: Google's mrcr_v2 in eval_hub and OpenAI's Hugging Face dataset.

name: MT-AIME (Cohere internal)
description: Cohere's internal machine translation of AIME 2025 problems into many languages (via Command A Translate). Answer accuracy.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Cohere).

name: MT-AIME2024
description: Models solve the 30 AIME 2024 problems translated into 55 languages. A rule-based verifier checks each final answer.
org: Yonsei University, OneLineAI, and KAIST AI
note: It is a subset of the MCLM multilingual math benchmark.

name: MT-Bench
description: 80 two-turn questions graded by GPT-4 as judge. Introduced LLM-as-judge methodology.
note: Saturated. Historically important for judge-bias analysis.

name: MTEB
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: retrieval, clustering, classification across languages and modalities.

name: MTOB
description: Models learn to translate between English and Kalamang, a language with under 200 speakers, from one grammar book. Scored by chrF.
note: Cards report half-book or full-book context and either translation direction, so scores vary by setup.

name: MTVQA-Test
description: Models answer 6,778 expert-written questions about text in 2,116 images across 9 languages, such as Arabic, Japanese, and Thai. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Humans score 79.7 in the paper, far above the models tested at release.

name: Multi-agent search (Anthropic internal benchmark)
description: Agents solve difficult information retrieval problems with web search, alone or as orchestrators that delegate to subagents.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Multi-factual (Anthropic)
description: Models answer questions that each combine several closed-ended sub-questions on one topic. Answers are graded correct, incorrect or unsure against references.
note: In-house Anthropic factuality evaluation. Questions were built from article quotes and checked by hand. Score is the share answered correctly.

name: Multi-hop search factuality
description: Models with search answer multi-hop and tail-fact questions that need several sources. Reports accuracy and unfactual rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Multi-IF
description: Models follow verifiable instructions over three-turn conversations in eight languages, extending IFEval. Scored by instruction accuracy at each turn.

name: Multi-SWE-bench
description: Agents resolve 1,632 GitHub issues in Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, and C++ repos. Patches must pass the repos' tests.
note: A 300-instance subset, Multi-SWE-bench flash, followed in July 2025.

name: Multi-turn testing (Anthropic)
description: Models face multi-turn conversations that escalate toward harmful requests across risk areas. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MultiChallenge
description: Multi-turn conversations testing instruction retention, inference memory, versioned editing and self-coherence. Graded by LLM judge with rubrics.

name: Multilingual AIME 2024 (Mistral)
description: Models solve AIME 2024 problems translated into French, Spanish, German, Italian, Russian and Chinese, reasoning in the question language.
note: Mistral made the translations itself. The Magistral paper reports one score per language and no average.

name: Multilingual Exams
description: Models answer multilingual exam and MMLU-style questions. Qwen reports the average of M3Exam, IndoMMLU, ruMMLU, and translated MMLU.
note: A Qwen aggregate of public exam sets rather than a separate benchmark, and its parts changed between model releases.

name: Multilingual human evaluation
description: Human raters score model answers in 10 languages, including Arabic, Korean, and Thai, on a 1 to 5 scale. Results are averaged across languages.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen never released the prompts.

name: Multilingual IFEval
description: Models follow IFEval instructions translated into eight languages, 100 examples each, which paid volunteers reviewed. Instruction compliance is checked as in IFEval.
note: A Qwen translation of IFEval described only in the Qwen2.5 blog.

name: Multilingual MMLU (Meta)
description: Models answer MMLU questions machine-translated into German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish and Thai, 5-shot.
note: In-house Meta translation made with Google Translate. It differs from OpenAI's MMMLU.

name: Multilingual Safety
description: An automated safety policy evaluation measures policy violations across multiple languages.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Multilingual Understanding
description: Models answer five multilingual comprehension sets, BELEBELE, XCOPA, XWinograd, XStoryCloze, and PAWS-X. Qwen reports the average accuracy.
note: This is a Qwen composite score, not a standalone benchmark.

name: MultiLoKo
description: Locally relevant knowledge questions in 31 languages, plus translations. Scored by exact match.

name: Multimodal policy red-teaming (Anthropic)
aliases: Trust & Safety multimodal policy red teaming
description: Models answer multi-turn image and text conversations on harmful topics such as child safety, weapons and fraud. Score is the share of harmless responses.
note: In-house Anthropic Trust and Safety evaluation. The Claude 3 model card used 378 prompts.

name: Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology
description: Models troubleshoot virology lab scenarios, sometimes with images, and must select every correct answer. Scored as refusal-adjusted pass@1.
note: Questions come from SecureBio. OpenAI Preparedness evaluation.

name: MultiPL-E
description: Models write code for HumanEval and MBPP problems translated into 18 other programming languages. Scored by pass@1 on unit tests.
org: Northeastern University Programming Research Lab (NuPRL) et al.

name: MultiRC
description: Models pick all correct answers to questions that need reasoning over several sentences of a paragraph. Scored by F1 over answer options.
note: Saturated. Also part of SuperGLUE.

name: Multiturn Jailbreak Evaluations
description: Models face adaptive multi-turn jailbreak attackers with growing attack budgets. Scored as worst-case defender success rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results appear as charts by attacker budget.

name: Muse-targeted cyber misuse and violation red-teaming
description: An automated red-teaming agent tries to misuse the Muse runtime across six attack categories. Reports attack success rate per category.
note: In-house Meta pre-launch stress test of early Muse builds. No overall score.

name: MVBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions across 20 temporal video tasks that a single frame cannot solve. Scored by accuracy.
note: TVBench authors found many MVBench questions solvable without temporal reasoning.

name: Mystery Game Puzzles
description: 100 mid-game positions from an undisclosed puzzle variant of a well-known game. Model picks the single best move, checked against an answer key.
note: Game identity, prompts and positions are kept secret to prevent targeted preparation. Likely the 'game-puzzles' benchmark in the Epoch post.

name: NanoGPT Speedrun
description: Improve a small GPT training script to reach a target validation loss as fast as possible on fixed hardware.
org: Keller Jordan (community); OpenAI and METR variants
note: OpenAI and METR run their own constrained variants on one H100 or a budget.

name: Natural Questions
description: Models answer real Google search questions. Model cards usually use the open-domain version, scored by exact match against short answers from Wikipedia.
note: The original task reads a full Wikipedia page, while model cards mostly report the closed-book variant.

name: Natural2Code
description: Models write Python functions in HumanEval format from new prompts kept off the web. Unit tests decide correctness.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set that was never released, built to avoid web leakage.

name: Needle In A Haystack
description: Models retrieve a planted fact from long filler text at varied context lengths and insertion depths. Scored by retrieval accuracy.
note: Most long-context models score near 100%, and labs run their own variants, so scores are not comparable.

name: NeedleBench
description: Models retrieve and reason over one or several facts inserted at different depths in bilingual long texts of set lengths.
note: Labs report one score per context length.

name: Neptune
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about long videos that need reasoning over many segments.
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 1,024 frames.

name: Network CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents perform reconnaissance and exploit vulnerabilities across multiple networked machines in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Neutrality evaluation
description: Single and multi-turn prompts on politics, civics, identity and religion test whether models avoid taking sides. Reports neutral response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Nexus
description: Models write function calls for queries over real-world APIs, including nested and parallel calls. Scoring is the function calling success rate.
note: Nexusflow released 8 of its 9 tasks and kept one internal to limit overfitting.

name: NL2Repo-Bench
description: From one natural-language requirements document and an empty workspace, agent builds an installable Python library. Scored by original project's test pass rate.
note: 104 tasks. Labs add anti-cheat blocks on pip download/git clone of the target repo to stop reward hacking.

name: No-CoT math time horizon
description: Models solve math problems without a visible chain of thought. Scored as the human task length in minutes the model solves reliably.
note: Third-party UK AISI measurement. Higher means more reasoning without visible CoT, which UK AISI treats as less monitorable.

name: nocot-bench (NCRI)
