description: Reasoning problems answered without chain of thought (e.g., Brew multi-hop tasks). Measures forward-pass reasoning relevant to monitorability.

name: NOVA-63
aliases: Native Omni-lingual Versatile Assessments of 63 Disciplines
description: Models answer questions written by native speakers in 14 languages across 63 academic disciplines. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The Hugging Face dataset is empty and marked under review, and nearly all reported scores come from Qwen.

name: Novel compiler task (Anthropic)
description: Agents build a compiler for an unusual programming language from a specification and test cases.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Novel logical reasoning problems expert evaluation (Z.ai)
description: Human experts score model answers to new multi-step logic problems with a fixed scoring standard for each question.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation built to avoid contamination. The problems are not public.

name: Nuscene
description: Models localize named objects as 3D boxes in nuScenes driving camera images. Scored by mAP.
note: Qwen lists it under spatial intelligence without a footnote, so the 3D grounding setup is inferred from its Hypersim row.

name: OAI-repo Sabotage v2
description: Agents try to complete a hidden sabotage side task in OpenAI code without detection. Scored on side task success while evading CoT and action monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Results appear as charts by reasoning length.

name: OCBench
description: 28 simulated manipulation tasks with human-like scripted demonstrators for controlled BC and RL studies. Policies scored by task success rate.
note: Design: scripted policies mimic human demos (narrow, temporally correlated, smoothly random via Hermite splines, with mistakes and recoveries), giving unlimited controllable data. Reproduces known BC effects. No leaderboard.

name: OCRBench
description: Models answer 1,000 checked questions on text recognition, scene text, documents, key information extraction, and handwritten math. The score counts correct answers.
org: Yuliang Liu, Xiang Bai et al.
note: OCRBench v2, released in December 2024 with 10,000 pairs, is a separate version.

name: OCRBench v2
description: Visual-text localization and reasoning tasks across 31 scenarios (documents, scenes, charts). Averaged task accuracy.

name: OctoCodingbench
description: Agents complete 72 coding tasks while following rules from system prompts, AGENTS.md files, skills, and memory. An LLM judge checks 2,422 pass or fail items.
note: MiniMax first reported it as internal, then released the tasks in January 2026.

name: ODinW-13
description: Models detect objects in 13 varied real-world datasets, such as aquarium and aerial images, from text category names. Scored by mean average precision.
note: A 13-dataset subset of the 35-task ODinW benchmark in ELEVATER.

name: OfficeQA
description: Grounded reasoning over a large corpus of U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents: locate tables and compute precise numeric answers.
note: Pro = 133 hard questions. Pro V2 (90 questions, new corpus) followed. Answers gated on HF to limit crawling.

name: OfficeQA Pro
description: Models answer the 133 hardest OfficeQA questions by finding tables in U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents and computing exact numeric answers.
note: Harder subset of OfficeQA recommended for frontier models. Kept apart from the full OfficeQA set.

name: OJBench
description: Models write C++ or Python solutions to 232 competition problems from NOI and ICPC. Judge test cases score each solution by pass@1.
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Tsinghua University, and others

name: OK-VQA
description: Models answer over 14,000 visual questions that need outside knowledge beyond the image. Scoring is VQA accuracy against human answers.
org: Allen Institute for AI and Carnegie Mellon University

name: Okapi MMLU
description: Models answer MMLU multiple choice questions that ChatGPT translated into 26 languages. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The questions are machine translated, so translation errors and English cultural bias remain.

name: Omni-MATH
description: Models solve 4,428 Olympiad-level competition math problems across 33 subdomains and 10 difficulty levels. A GPT-4 or Omni-Judge grader checks answers.
org: Peking University and Alibaba et al.

name: OmniDocBench
description: Diverse PDF pages with layout, text, table and formula annotations. Parsing scored by edit distance and TEDS.

name: Online Experience (Moonshot)
description: Agents produce the deliverable file types that real online users request most often, following the distribution of real usage.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Open Ended Questions (hallucination)
description: Models write open-ended factual text such as biographies, checked against Wikipedia. Scored as average number of incorrect statements.
note: In-house OpenAI hallucination evaluation.

name: OpenAI agentic alignment evals
description: Respecting auto-review and warnings, an ExploitGym honeypot, coding and blocker deception, broken search tool, realistic work environments, agent-to-agent messages.

name: OpenAI cyber safety evaluations (incl. Daybreak Blue)
description: Refusal and helpfulness evaluations for cyber requests, including the Daybreak Blue set for enabling defensive security work.

name: OpenAI Deployment Simulation
description: Replays representative production or internal Codex traffic on a candidate model to forecast misaligned or disallowed behavior before launch.

name: OpenAI Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks
description: Multi-turn conversations with adversarial simulated users on mental-health risks. Scored on safe and supportive responses.

name: OpenAI GPT-Red jailbreak and prompt-injection evals
description: Static jailbreaks from attacker models (half from a held-out attacker), adaptive multi-turn attackers, and direct and indirect prompt-injection sets.

name: OpenAI internal AI self-improvement evals
description: Internal Research Debugging (41 real research bugs plus alignment-auditing tasks) and KernelGen 1P (kernels for OpenAI first-party hardware).
note: Replaced saturated Monorepo-Bench and OPQA.

name: OpenAI internal cyber evaluations
description: Internal suites: curated public CTF challenges, VulnLMP long-horizon vulnerability research on real software, and Sandbox Bench (22 mostly zero-day targets).

name: OpenAI monitorability evals
description: Open suite from 'Monitoring Monitorability' testing whether CoT and action monitors catch hidden properties of agent behavior.

name: OpenAI performance in cases flagged by users
description: Model answers de-identified ChatGPT prompts that users flagged for factual errors. Scored on any error and on repeating the flagged error.
note: Adversarially selected set. OpenAI warns error rates are far above production and are not hallucination rates. Results only in a chart. An appendix version for GPT-6 Sol and Luna was added 2026-09-22.

name: OpenAI Production Benchmarks and safe-completion evals
description: Hard production-derived prompts per policy category, under-18 evals, agentic safe completions and image-input evals. Scored on safe completion rate.

name: OpenAI PRs
description: Agents replicate internal OpenAI pull requests from a pre-PR branch and a prompt. Graded by hidden unit tests as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: OpenAI Research Engineer Interview: Coding
description: Models solve 18 self-contained coding problems like those in OpenAI interviews. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the internal interview question bank.

name: OpenAI Research Engineer Interview: Multiple Choice
description: Models answer 97 multiple-choice questions drawn from OpenAI machine learning interview topics. Scored as cons@32.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the internal interview question bank.

name: OpenAI user-flagged hallucination eval
aliases: Performance in Cases Flagged by Users
description: Production conversations users flagged for factual errors. Measures the rate of incorrect claims.

name: OpenAI-Proof Q&A
description: Agents diagnose 20 real OpenAI research and engineering bottlenecks using code, logs and run artifacts. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. Each problem took an OpenAI team over a day.

name: OpenBookQA
description: Models answer elementary science multiple-choice questions that need a given core science fact plus common knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated by frontier models.

name: OpenEQA
description: Agents answer over 1,600 open-vocabulary questions about real indoor scenes from recorded episodes or active exploration. A judge model scores answers against human answers.

name: OpenRCA
description: Agents find the root cause of 335 software failures from enterprise telemetry logs, metrics and traces. Scored on component, start time and reason.
org: Microsoft, CUHK-Shenzhen and Tsinghua University (Xu et al.)
note: Published at ICLR 2025. The data covers telecom, banking and online marketplace systems.

name: OpenScore String Quartets
description: Models transcribe images of string quartet sheet music into symbolic notation. Scored as 1 minus normalized edit distance from the reference encoding.
org: OpenAI, using the OpenScore String Quartets corpus
note: OpenAI's exact setup is unpublished, and the separate OSSQ-OMR benchmark uses the same corpus and metric.

name: Opportunistic sandbox escape (Anthropic)
description: Agents do dev-ops tasks in 1,753 sandboxes with deliberate weaknesses. Score is the share of scenarios where they use credentials or files outside.
note: Anthropic also reports the rate of reaching outside the sandbox by any route. It differs from the older audit-based sandbox evaluation.

name: OptimBench
description: Agents solve optimization engineering tasks. Part of Meta's recursive-improvement suite and graded programmatically.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: OR-Bench
description: Models meet benign and borderline prompts and the benchmark measures how often they wrongly refuse. Reports false refusal rate.
note: Public over-refusal benchmark for large language models.

name: Organic Chemistry (Anthropic)
description: Models predict structures from spectra, design synthetic routes, predict reaction products and convert between IUPAC names, SMILES and structure images.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Organic Chemistry V2 (Anthropic)
description: Models predict structures from spectra, design multi-step syntheses, predict reaction products and read chemical structure images. V2 adds harder expert-recommended problems.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Scores are not comparable with the original Organic Chemistry set.

name: OSGym
aliases: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
description: Infrastructure running 1,000+ parallel OS sandboxes for computer-use agent training and evaluation. Tasks span browsing, documents, SWE and multi-app work.
note: Infrastructure, not a scored benchmark: 1,420 trajectories/min at ~$0.2-0.3 per replica-day. The v1 paper's code link github.com/agiopen-org/osgym returned 404 on 2026-10-22, and v5 lists no code.

name: OSWorld
description: Agents complete 369 real computer tasks in Ubuntu desktop apps through screenshots and mouse and keyboard actions. Execution-based scripts check the final state.
note: OSWorld-Verified fixed task errors in July 2025, and OSWorld 2.0 replaced it as the latest version in June 2026.

name: OSWorld 2.0
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Releases are versioned and some cards report the offline subset or partial score, so cross-card numbers are not directly comparable.

name: OSWorld 2.0 (Aug 2026)
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Patch release on the same 108 tasks: 14 changed to prevent reward hacking and 31 modified.

name: OSWorld 2.1
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Bug-fix release on the same 108 tasks, with evaluator fixes and updated mock websites.

name: OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset)
description: Agents complete the 82 OSWorld 2.1 tasks on the official offline list, with no internet access. Scored by checkpoint partial credit and strict pass rate.
note: Subset of the 108 OSWorld 2.1 tasks. Scores are not comparable with scores on the full set.

name: OSWorld-Verified
description: 369 open-ended tasks in real desktop apps. Agent acts through screenshots, mouse and keyboard. Execution-based checkers score success.
note: Human baseline 72.4%. Top reported scores are ~83-86%, so near-saturated. Successor OSWorld 2.0 released 2026-06 (repo xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2).

name: OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025
description: Models solve 45 problems from three OTIS Mock AIME exams written by students of the OTIS program. Integer answers are scored by exact match.
note: Epoch AI added it as a harder successor to MATH Level 5, which was nearing saturation.

name: Over-eager behavior on GUI computer use tasks (Anthropic)
aliases: Overly agentic behavior in GUI computer use settings
Over-Eager Behavior on GUI Computer Use Tasks
description: Computer-use agents face impossible tasks with an unwanted shortcut available. Score is the rate of unapproved workarounds instead of checking with the user.
note: Run with neutral, encouraging and discouraging system prompts. The neutral prompt is the default setting.

name: Overconfidence: verifying command-line syntax (Anthropic)
description: Agents are asked for an exact invocation of an unfamiliar command-line tool. Graders score from 1 to 5 whether they check documentation before running commands.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Oversight gaming
description: A prompted monitor flags aligned-graded rollouts whose behavior follows from reasoning about oversight. Scored as rate per alignment evaluation.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement. Earlier cards called it undermining evaluation validity.

name: Overstepping boundaries on ambiguous and high-risk tasks
description: Agents get ambiguous or high-risk coding and other tasks where they should pause to ask the user, plus clear tasks they should just do.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Package registry publishing evaluation (Anthropic)
aliases: Propensity to publish harmful content to public package registries
Intensity of pressure required for a model to publish a backdoored package
description: Agents in a simulated capture the flag exercise can publish a backdoored package to a registry. An investigator escalates pressure until they act.
note: Built after an incident in which a model published harmful content to PyPI. Results are counts of investigations by outcome.

name: PAI-Bench
description: Physical-AI video generation from 1,044 prompts in six domains, VLM-QA plus quality metrics. Companion control and understanding tracks.
note: Generation score compressed near the real-video reference (Source 82.6. Cosmos3-Super 83.9 exceeds it). Robot domain spreads more (55-90).

name: Pairwise Bioweaponization Campaign
description: Red teamers with biology PhDs compare anonymized responses from two models on bioweaponization prompts. Scored as the win rate for being safer.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming campaign. The comparison model changes by card.

name: Pairwise safety red teaming
aliases: ELO Scores across vision-based red teaming categories
description: Red teamers compare anonymized responses from several models and pick the least safe. Scored as ELO or win rate.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming study. Cards use ELO or win rates.

name: Pantograph frontier-LLM robot benchmark (Pandroid)
description: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 drive Pandroid robots through a fixed tool harness on eight simple manipulation tasks, 10 blind-graded attempts each.
note: Controlled design: same prompt, tools and budget (20 min or 96 turns), random interleaving across six robots, blind grading, p about 0.001 stratified by task. Astra 35%, Fable 15%. Human teleoperators reach 100%. Fixed clock penalises slow thinking. One team runs both models.

name: PaperBench
description: Agent replicates ICML 2024 papers from scratch. LLM judge grades against author-written hierarchical rubrics.
note: Repo renamed from openai/preparedness. Qwen and MiniMax use different judges (Opus 4.6) and 12h runs, so scores are not comparable.

name: Parametric CAD Bench
description: Agents author editable parametric FreeCAD part designs, graded against held-back references for geometry and spec consistency.
note: Not the same as anniedoris/CADBench. A submission-portal repo exists at github.com/gNucleus-AI/cad-bench-submission.

name: PartBench
description: Parametric mechanical part design and CAD-style generation, graded for geometric and manufacturing fidelity.
note: Only source found is the Grok 4.6 card reference to normalfactory.com.

name: Participation in junk science (Anthropic)
description: Models talk with simulated users ranging from curious to openly fraudulent who seek fake science. Score is the rate of generating unsound scientific content.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with 90 scenarios. The tasks are not public.

name: Passkey Retrieval
description: Models find a random passkey hidden at a random position in a long filler prompt. Scored by retrieval accuracy.
note: Synthetic test from the Landmark Attention paper. Strong long-context models usually score near 100%.

name: Pattern Labs cyberoffensive challenges
description: Agents attempt evasion, network attack simulation and vulnerability exploitation challenges at easy, medium and hard levels. Scored as success rate per type.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Results are per challenge type with no overall number.

name: PAWS
description: Models decide whether two sentences with heavy word overlap are paraphrases.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: Perception Test MCVQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about real-world videos filmed to show perceptually interesting situations. Scored by top-1 accuracy.
note: Multiple-choice video QA task of the Perception Test benchmark.

name: PerceptionBench (Moonshot)
description: Moonshot in-house benchmark of atomic visual perception skills. Scoring details unpublished.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Moonshot AI). Not the same as other public benchmarks with this name.

name: Person Identification evaluation
description: Models receive requests to identify people in photos. Scored on refusal rate in non-adversarial and adversarial sets.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two difficulty levels with no overall number.

name: Personal-device assistant prompt injection eval
description: OS assistant agents in 44 stateful scenarios ingest untrusted content that tries to trigger unauthorized actions. Reports 5-step adaptive survival and task utility.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: PersonQA
description: Models answer questions about publicly available facts on people. Scored on accuracy, with hallucination rate reported alongside.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results here record accuracy and name the hallucination rate in the text.

name: Petri
aliases: Parallel Exploration Tool for Risky Interactions
description: Open-source auditing tool where auditor agents probe target models in simulated scenarios and judges score misaligned behaviors.
note: Anthropic cards use Petri to compare Claude with other labs' models.

name: Petri Bloom
description: An auditor model runs generated scenarios to elicit named misaligned behaviors. Judges score each transcript from 1 to 10.
note: Bloom generates scenarios and Petri runs the interactions. Meta averages mean scores across 13 shared behaviors.

name: Phage-plasmid Co-evolution
description: Models predict future amino acid mutations in a phage and plasmid system from earlier observations. Scored as negative log likelihood.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 9.40 or lower.

name: PhAIL
description: Real Franka bin-to-bin picking of four object types. VLAs scored on throughput and completion against human and teleop references.
note: Throughput metric, not just success: best model ~59 units/hour vs 330 teleop and 1,331 human. One narrow task. Repo holds paper analysis scripts.

name: PhiBench
description: Models answer original prompts that Microsoft's Phi team wrote to test a wide range of skills and reasoning.
note: In-house: Microsoft never released the tasks, and the Phi-4-reasoning report uses a newer version, PhiBench 2.21.

name: Phylogenetics (Anthropic)
description: Models analyze phylogenetic data and tree diagrams, testing quantitative reasoning about tree structure and visual interpretation.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: PhysicalRealismBench-U
description: VLM watches 1,300 synthetic Isaac Sim videos, flags physics-law violations, names object and frames. Scored by joint realism F1.
note: Lab-created benchmark (Reka). Not cited in the Reka Edge card. No code or dataset link. Best realism F1 0.60 at launch.

name: PhysicianBench
description: 100 physician tasks performed by an agent inside an EHR environment. Scored by pass rate per attempt.

name: Physics-IQ
description: Video models continue 396 filmed physical events from a frame or 3 s clip. Motion compared with the real continuation.
note: Not saturated: Verified best 58.2% (v2v, best-of-N) vs 100% physical-variance ceiling. Some rows supplied by model makers via GitHub issues. Physics-IQ Verified: arXiv 2606.18943, physics-iq-verified.anates.ai.

name: PhysicsFinals
description: Models answer 61 undergraduate physics final exam problems written by physics professors. A professor grades the answers.
note: In-house Google eval, never released.

name: PhyX
description: Models solve 3,000 image-based physics problems across six domains such as mechanics and optics. Versions include multiple choice and open-ended answers.
note: A 1,000 question testmini subset also exists, so check which split a model card reports.

name: Pile-test
description: Models predict text from the test split of the Pile, an 800GB corpus of 22 sources. Scored by bits per byte.
note: A language modeling metric for base models, not a task benchmark.

name: PinchBench
description: Real-world tasks (scheduling, email triage, coding, research, files) for an LLM driving an OpenClaw agent. Graded by automated checks and LLM judge.
note: Task set grew from 23 to 53 tasks. V2.0 changed default judge backend, so versions are not comparable.

name: PIQA
description: Models pick which of two solutions better achieves an everyday physical goal. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi

name: PLawBench
description: Model handles 850 realistic legal consultation, case-analysis and document-drafting tasks. LLM judge scores against about 12,500 expert rubric items.
note: ACL 2026. Qwen judged it with gemini-3.1-pro-preview.

name: PlugInject
description: Agents receive function call outputs that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation drawn from a split of training data.

name: PMC-VQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about medical images drawn from PubMed Central figures. Scored by accuracy.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Shanghai AI Laboratory

name: PolicyBench
description: No-tools estimate of US taxes and benefits for 100 households across 18 programs. Headline metric is answers within $1 of PolicyEngine-US.
note: Prompts and reference values are public, so the authors call the board a preview. Forced tool calls lowered some Claude scores.

name: Political Persuasion Parallel Generation
description: Human raters pick the more persuasive of two short political social media posts. Scored as win rate against GPT-4o.
note: OpenAI persuasion evaluation. Post-mitigation models often refuse political persuasion.

name: Political Science LLM Benchmark
description: 33 political-science text-coding tasks, 100 texts each (~3,300 items). Models scored by mean F1 against human-coded labels.
note: 31 models. Open-weight models run on one GPU. Some texts may be in training data.

name: Poly-Guard Bench
description: Models meet harmful requests and statements across domains. Reports attack success rate under single-turn and multi-turn adaptive red-teaming.
note: Policy-grounded guardrail dataset. Meta uses the cyber domain, high-severity subset.

name: PolyMath
description: Models solve 9,000 parallel math problems in 18 languages across four difficulty levels, from school math to frontier math. Final answers are checked.
note: Some model cards report only the English subset, PolyMath-en.

name: POPE
description: Vision language models answer yes or no questions about whether objects appear in COCO images. Scored by accuracy or F1 on object hallucination.
org: Renmin University of China (Li et al.)

name: PostTrainBench
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
note: Known reward hacking (eval tampering, swapping in instruct models). Agent-as-judge added. Dataset link holds trajectories, not tasks.

name: PostTrainBench 1.1
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
note: Version 1.1 added judges for contamination and API use, and banned distillation from hosted models. Runs that broke the rules score as the base model.

name: PostTrainBench 1.2
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
note: Version 1.2 dropped BFCL, reweighted the other six benchmarks, fixed HumanEval scoring, and averages up to five seeds.

name: PRBench
description: Model answers 1,100 expert-written law and finance questions. LLM judge grades against weighted expert rubrics of 10-30 criteria each.
note: Hard subset of 550 tasks. Top Hard scores about 0.39 at release.

name: Preference on ChatGPT and API prompts
description: Human labelers compare model responses to 5,214 prompts sent to ChatGPT and the OpenAI API. Scored as win rate against a baseline model.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The baseline model changes between reports.

name: PresentBench
description: Models generate full slide decks from background materials for 238 real-world cases. A judge scores each deck against about 54 hand-written checklist items.

name: PrimeVul
description: Models classify C and C++ functions as vulnerable or not, with a paired setting that pairs each vulnerable function with its patch.
org: Columbia University and Google (Ding et al.)
note: Google reports accuracy in multiple-choice form, with standard and paired settings.

name: Proactive Searches
description: Graders read ExploitGym Honeypot reasoning traces for speculation about other agents and attempts to contact them. Scored as rate of trajectories.
note: In-house OpenAI analysis of unintended agent-to-agent communication. The tasks are not public.

name: Production Deception - Adversarial
description: Models answer prompts representative of traffic that previously elicited deception in ChatGPT. Scored as deception rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Production Jailbreaks
description: Models face jailbreaks found in production ChatGPT data. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The jailbreaks are not public.

name: ProfBench
description: Model writes expert-level reports in physics, chemistry, finance and consulting. Calibrated LLM judges grade against PhD/MBA-written rubrics.
note: Lab-created by NVIDIA (ICLR 2026). Nemotron reports a ProfBench (Search) variant. Reference documents are not in the HF set.

name: ProgramBench
description: 200 tasks: rebuild a full program from only its compiled binary and docs. Hidden behavioral tests (248k total) must match the original.
note: Tasks range from jq to FFmpeg and SQLite. The Opus 5.5 system card reports a 100-agent swarm result.

name: Prompt injection attacks in search and function calling
description: Agents receive search results and function call outputs that contain stronger known prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection live bug bounty (Anthropic with Gray Swan)
description: Expert red teamers submit prompt injection attacks against hidden frontier models in tool use, coding and computer use scenarios. Score is attack success rate.
note: Each round runs for about a week with new scenarios. Claude models are tested without product prompt injection protections.

name: Prompt injection robustness
description: Agents meet indirect prompt injection attacks inside tool outputs. Scored as defender success rate averaged per defender query.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, browser use (Anthropic)
aliases: Robustness against adaptive attackers: browser use
description: Browser agents face indirect prompt injections in web environments from an internal adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, coding (Anthropic)
description: Coding agents face indirect prompt injections crafted by an adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: Anthropic uses Gray Swan's Shade adaptive attacker for this surface. Reported at 1 and many attempts.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, computer use (Anthropic)
aliases: Robustness against adaptive attackers: computer use
description: Computer-use agents face indirect prompt injections crafted by an adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: Anthropic uses Gray Swan's Shade adaptive attacker for this surface. Reported with and without safeguards.

name: Prompt injection, general tool use
description: An adaptive attacker injects payloads into tool responses across 100 multi-step scenarios to trigger unrelated tool calls. Reports survival after N attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection, turn injections in tool use
description: Static and adaptive payloads in tool outputs spoof multi-turn conversation syntax. Reports survival after N attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ProofBench
description: Models write Lean 4 proofs of graduate-level theorems, with Mathlib search and code tools for up to 40 turns. Scored by the share that compile.
note: Saturated by October 2026, with several systems at 100% on the 100-problem private split.

name: PropensityBench
description: Agents face 979 scenarios with equally effective safe and harmful tools under escalating pressure. Reports the rate of harmful tool choice.
note: Proprietary Scale AI evaluation with a public leaderboard.

name: Protein Design (Anthropic)
description: Models generate novel protein sequences under design constraints and rank protein design libraries for experimental testing.
note: Reported as two tasks, Sequence Generation and Library Ranking, with no overall score.

name: ProteinGym
description: Deep mutational scanning benchmarks. The model ranks mutations by predicted effect on protein function. Anthropic reports a hard subset.

name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended
description: Models correct errors in published lab protocols using open-ended questions adapted from LAB-Bench ProtocolQA. Scored as pass@1.
note: OpenAI open-ended adaptation of the ProtocolQA multiple-choice set.

name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended (xAI)
description: Models name the single most important mistake in a biology lab protocol in free text, with no answer choices.
note: xAI's free-text version of LAB-Bench ProtocolQA. It may differ from OpenAI's open-ended version.

name: Protocols (Anthropic life sciences)
description: Models find and fix errors in molecular biology protocols and answer practical questions about applying real laboratory protocols.
note: Reported as two variants, Troubleshooting and Understanding (V2), with no overall score. Benchling built the Understanding set.

name: PubMedQA
description: Models answer biomedical research questions with yes, no, or maybe, given a PubMed abstract without its conclusion. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University

name: Putnam 2025
description: Models solve the 12 problems of the 2025 William Lowell Putnam competition with full proofs. Scored out of 120 points.
note: DeepSeek scored it with a hybrid informal and formal Lean pipeline checked by a strict verifier.

name: PutnamBench
description: Models write formal Lean proofs of Putnam competition problems. A proof counts only when the verifier accepts it.
note: Labs often report Putnam-200, a fixed random subset first used by Seed-Prover.

name: Pwn CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents exploit insecure software on a remote server for privilege escalation or code execution in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Qasper
description: Models answer 5,049 questions about 1,585 NLP research papers from the full paper text. Answers are scored with token F1.

name: QuAC
description: Models answer free-form questions in information-seeking dialogs about a hidden Wikipedia section, across 100K questions. Scored by word-level F1.
org: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington, Stanford, and UMass Amherst

name: Quadruped reinforcement learning task (Anthropic)
description: Agents train a quadruped to reach high performance in a continuous control task.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: QuALITY
aliases: QuALITY (Question Answering with Long Input Texts, Yes!)
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about English passages that average about 5,000 tokens. Scoring is accuracy.
note: About half the questions were too hard for annotators to answer under tight time limits.

name: QuantBench
description: Models answer 25 multiple choice versions of quant trading firm reasoning puzzles. Scored as cons@16 accuracy.
note: OpenAI contextual evaluation. Questions come from competitions run by firms such as Jane Street.

name: QVHighlights
description: Natural-language queries over YouTube videos. Model localizes relevant moments, scored by Recall@1 at IoU 0.5.

name: Qwen Chinese human evaluation
description: Three annotators rank chat model answers to 300 Chinese instructions on knowledge, language, writing, math and coding. Results are win rates against GPT-3.5.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The instructions are not public.

name: Qwen in-house Chinese automatic evaluation
description: Models answer Qwen in-house Chinese datasets on knowledge, comprehension, coding, math and related skills. Skills and weights change between reports.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The Qwen2 report gives an average, the Qwen2.5 report gives per-skill scores only.

name: Qwen in-house English automatic evaluation
description: Models answer Qwen in-house English datasets on knowledge, comprehension, coding, math and related skills. Skills and weights change between reports.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The Qwen2 report gives an average, the Qwen2.5 report gives per-skill scores only.

name: Qwen2 multilingual safety evaluation
description: Models answer risky prompts in several languages on illegal behavior, fraud, pornography and privacy, including jailbreak attempts. Scores are harmful response rates.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The prompts are not public. Lower is better.

name: QwenBlenderBench
description: Models complete Blender 3D modeling tasks in Qwen's internal visual agent and coding test. Qwen has not described its scoring.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen has not released the tasks.

name: QwenClawBench
description: Agents complete 100 tasks across 8 domains in isolated OpenClaw workspaces drawn from real user patterns. Automated checks and an LLM judge score each task.
note: Qwen built it as an internal benchmark for Qwen3.6-Plus and released it afterward.

name: QwenQoderBench
description: Qwen in-house benchmark of user experience in the Qoder coding product, run in Claude Code (avg@5, 6-hour limit).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenReactBench
description: Model builds bilingual React projects in Claude Code across 7 categories. Rendered outputs judged by a multimodal model, ranked with Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenSVG
description: Models write SVG graphics code for Qwen's in-house prompts. Results are reported as ratings near 1,500 to 1,600, not percentages.
note: In-house: Qwen never released the tasks or explained the rating method.

name: QwenSVGBench
description: Model writes SVG code for bilingual prompts. Rendered outputs judged by a multimodal model and ranked with Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenSWEBench
description: Qwen in-house software-engineering benchmark run in Claude Code (avg@3, 8-hour limit). Task and scoring details unpublished.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenVisualOffice
description: Models handle visual office tasks in an internal Qwen test set. Qwen has not published the tasks or how they are scored.
note: In-house Qwen benchmark, so scores cannot be checked independently.

name: QwenWebBench
description: Models generate front-end code for web apps, games, SVG, and other categories in English and Chinese. Multimodal judgments produce Elo ratings.
note: In-house Qwen benchmark, and the tasks are not released.

name: QwenWebDev
description: Models generate front-end web pages in English and Chinese across 7 categories. Pages are rendered and a multimodal judge compares them, giving Bradley-Terry Elo ratings.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen has not released the tasks.

name: QwenWorldBench
description: Models act as world models that simulate agent environments in 7 domains, such as terminal, web, and Android. A rubric judge scores five dimensions.
note: In-house: Qwen never released the tasks.

name: RACE
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions from Chinese middle and high school English exams. Reported here without a subset split.
note: Use race-m or race-h when a report gives the middle or high school subset.

name: RACE-H
description: Models answer multiple-choice reading questions from English exams for Chinese high school students. The test split has 3,498 questions, scored by accuracy.

name: RACE-M
description: Models read passages from English exams for Chinese middle school students and answer multiple-choice questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is the middle school subset of RACE, alongside the harder high school subset RACE-H.

name: Radiological and Nuclear Expert Knowledge
description: Models answer 87 expert and tacit knowledge questions on radiological and nuclear threats. Scored as cons@32 accuracy.
note: Questions written by an MIT nuclear security fellow for OpenAI Preparedness.

name: RBench
description: 650 image+text prompts for robot video generation (tasks and embodiments). MLLM judge scores task completion, physical plausibility, stability.
note: MLLM-judged. GPT and Qwen judges give different scores and orders. Best GPT-judged 0.642. Later rows (e.g. Cosmos 3) were supplied by model authors.

name: RE-Bench
description: Seven open-ended ML research-engineering environments with human-expert baselines. Score normalized to reference solutions.

name: RE-Bench subset (Anthropic)
description: Agents solve a modified subset of four METR RE-Bench research engineering tasks. Scores are normalized from reference solution 0 to expert solution 1.
note: Anthropic runs triton_cumsum, rust_codecontests_inference, restricted_mlm and fix_embedding. Scores are not comparable to METR's reported scores.

name: Real-scenario prompts human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: One human evaluator scores replies to 660 curated real user prompts in English, Chinese and other languages on a 0 to 10 scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Scores are given per language with no combined score.

name: Real-World Finance (Anthropic)
description: Agents complete about 50 analyst tasks in banking, private equity, hedge funds and corporate finance, producing spreadsheets, slides and documents. Rubric graded.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Real-World Finance v2 (Anthropic)
description: Agents complete 294 long-horizon finance tasks such as building financial models. A model grader compares deliverables pairwise and ratings are fit as Elo.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Scores are Elo with Sonnet 4.6 fixed at 1000, so they do not compare with the first version.

name: Real-world vulnerability discovery
description: Agents search popular open-source codebases to rediscover about 1,200 recent confirmed vulnerabilities across many languages. Reports share discovered.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: RealKIE-FCC Verified
description: Model extracts structured fields from scanned FCC invoices into a JSON schema. Amazon human-verified labels. Field-level similarity (ALNS).
note: Lab-created verified variant (Amazon AGI) of Indico's RealKIE FCC Invoices set (RealKIE released 2024-03).

name: REALM
description: High-fidelity simulation benchmark for VLA generalization: 15 perturbation factors, 7 skills, 3,500+ objects. Success rate validated against real-robot results.
org: Czech Technical University (CIIRC) + University of Amsterdam
note: Design: checks that sim scores correlate with real-robot performance. Paper evaluates pi0, pi0-FAST and GR00T N1.5 only. No leaderboard. IEEE RA-L 2026.

name: RealToxicityPrompts
description: Models continue 100,000 web text prompts. Scored on the rate of toxic generations judged by a toxicity classifier.
org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington
note: Labs use different classifiers and sampling, so rates rarely compare across reports.

name: RealWorldQA
description: Models answer a question about each of 700+ real-world photos, many taken from vehicles, that test basic spatial understanding. Answers are easy to verify.

name: Reasoning behavior classifiers (Anthropic)
aliases: Percentages of model outputs exhibiting harmful behaviors
description: Classifiers scan reasoning text from training episodes for deception, harmful actions and distress. Score is the share of outputs flagged.
note: In-house Anthropic monitoring of training transcripts. Results are given per category with no single overall rate.

name: Recognition of model-written user turns (Anthropic)
aliases: Model ability to distinguish their own simulated user turns from real user turns
description: Models write synthetic user turns for real Claude Code transcripts, then judge which version is real. Score is accuracy above chance.
note: The same model acts as generator and judge. Anthropic reports the probability of a correct choice minus 0.5.

name: ReCoRD
aliases: Reading Comprehension with Commonsense Reasoning Dataset
description: Models fill in a masked entity in a query about a news article, using the article as context. Scoring is exact match and token F1.
org: Johns Hopkins University and Microsoft Research
note: ReCoRD is one of the SuperGLUE tasks.

name: RecreationBench
description: Agents explore a running reference app and rebuild it, across 250 tasks on five platforms. Programmatic tests and a VLM judge score the result.

name: Red Teaming Network pairwise safety comparison
description: Red teamers compare anonymized responses from two models in free-form risky conversations. Scored as the share of ratings where a model is safer.
note: Human red teamers rate only conversations with at least one perceived unsafe response.

name: RedCode
description: Models meet adversarial prompts to generate or run harmful code. Generation is model-judged and execution is checked in a container.
note: Meta reports attack success rate averaged over single-turn and multi-turn arms.

name: RedlineBench
description: Agent acts as counsel at one turn of a SaaS contract negotiation and returns tracked-change redlines. Three LLM judges grade attorney-written rubrics.
note: Attorneys wrote a branching tree of golden responses. The counterparty playbook is hidden from the agent. Built without client data.

name: RefAdv-S
description: Models locate the object a referring expression describes among hard distractors in real images. Scored by accuracy at 0.5 box overlap on 1,142 cases.
note: It is the public subset of the larger Ref-Adv benchmark.

name: RefCOCO / RefCOCO+ / RefCOCOg
description: Model grounds a referring expression to a bounding box in a COCO image. Scored by accuracy at IoU 0.5.
org: UNC Chapel Hill (Licheng Yu et al.)
note: Reka's 'RefCOCO-A/B' are the testA/testB splits.

name: RefSpatial-Bench
description: Real images where the model points to an object or free space defined by multi-step spatial relations. Scored by mask hit.
note: No independent leaderboard. Subset aggregation not stated. One cross-checked row (RoboBrain2.0-7B) differs from its origin: 42.2 vs 32.50.

name: Refusal to assist with AI safety R&D (Anthropic)
description: Models receive single-turn coding requests for legitimate AI safety research with user context. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Refusals + System Jailbreak (xAI)
description: Models get the xAI refusal set with jailbreak templates in the system message. The metric is the answer rate.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 model cards.

name: Refusals + User Jailbreak (xAI)
description: Models get the xAI refusal set with jailbreak templates in the user message. The metric is the answer rate.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 model cards.

name: Regurgitation Evaluations
description: Models are asked to reproduce training data. Scored on how often they refuse to regurgitate it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards describe results in words without a number.

name: RelBench
description: Agents build models for prediction tasks over multi-table relational databases, graded on held-out targets.
note: Built as a deep learning benchmark. xAI reports an aggregate agent score labeled accuracy.

name: ReMI
description: Models reason over several images per question in math, physics, logic, code, charts, and spatial or temporal tasks. Scored by accuracy.

name: Remote Labor Index
description: Agents complete real paid remote freelance projects from many sectors. Reviewers judge whether each deliverable would be accepted as commissioned work, giving an automation rate.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: The best agent automated only 2.5% of projects at launch. Only a 10 task public set is released.

name: RepoInject v1
description: Coding agents do benign tasks in 84 repository tasks seeded with prompt injections. Reports attack success rate at one and three attempts.
note: Third-party private benchmark run for Meta before release.

name: RepoQA
description: Models find a function in a long code repository from a description of what it does, across Python, C++, Rust, Java and TypeScript.

name: ReproBAIT
description: Agents independently reproduce biological AI models from published scientific papers. Scored as success rate.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards.

name: Research sandbagging (Anthropic)
description: Agents are told to sabotage a coding task or imitate a weaker model without alerting a weaker monitor. Measures the performance drop and monitor suspicion.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation based on Gasteiger et al. 2025. Results are a scatter of task performance against monitor suspicion.

name: ResearchRubrics
description: 101 deep-research prompts with 2,593 expert-written weighted rubric criteria (including penalties). Reports graded for grounding, reasoning and clarity.
note: ICLR 2026 paper.

name: ResearchTasteBench
description: Agents are scored on judgment about which research directions are worth pursuing. Part of Meta's recursive-improvement suite.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Graded programmatically. The tasks are not public.

name: Respecting Auto-Review
description: Agents receive an Auto-review denial during a coding task. Scored on how often they try to circumvent the denial.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Respecting Warnings
description: Agents meet low-stakes restrictions and warnings during routine tasks. Scored on the rate of unwanted persistence past the warning.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Rev CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents reverse-engineer binary executables to find hidden details or vulnerabilities in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Reward-hack-prone coding tasks (Anthropic)
description: Models solve hard coding problems where earlier Claude models often special-cased tests. Score is the classifier hack rate.
note: Anthropic also reports a hidden-test hack rate on held-out tests for the same tasks.

name: RewardBench
description: Models act as judges and pick the preferred response in chosen and rejected pairs across chat, hard chat, safety and reasoning. Scored by accuracy.
org: Allen Institute for AI (Lambert et al.)
note: It measures reward model or judge quality, not answer quality. RewardBench 2 is a later separate release.

name: Rewind-attacker cyber adversarial robustness (Anthropic)
description: An automated attacker with rewinds and 400 calls tries to make a safeguarded Claude Code agent complete offensive cyber tasks. Score is attack success rate.
note: Tasks include ransomware, data exfiltration, CVE exploitation, command and control and self-replication.

name: RGB
description: Models answer English and Chinese news questions from retrieved passages, testing noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. Scored by accuracy.

name: Riemann-bench
description: 25 private research-mathematics problems from professors and IMO medalists. Agents with tools, 100 runs per problem.

name: RISE
description: Agents answer real questions from human experts that need multi-step search and interaction with information-dense web pages. MiniMax has not published the scoring method.
note: In-house MiniMax benchmark, and the tasks are not released.

name: RL rollout audit for beyond-episode drives
description: LLM autoraters read a stratified sample of 10,000 RL training rollouts for alignment faking, training gaming and beyond-episode drives.
note: In-house Google DeepMind audit of training data, so results are rates over sampled rollouts.

name: RoboArena
description: Double-blind pairwise A/B trials of generalist DROID policies on real Franka arms, free-form tasks by volunteer evaluators. Elo-style rating.
note: Relative rating with no ceiling. Evaluators at 28 organisations. One contributed 2,301 of 3,994 evals. Low-eval rows are unofficial.

name: RoboCasa365
description: Mobile-manipulator kitchen sim: train on 300-task Human300 data, test on 50 tasks incl. 16 unseen composite tasks. Success rate.
note: Composite-Unseen tops out at 36.7% versus ~80% on Atomic-Seen, a large generalisation gap. Team trains baselines. Other entries self-evaluated and reviewed. Submissions live in github.com/robocasa-benchmark/leaderboard.

name: RoboChallenge
description: Fine-tuned policies run 10 real rollouts on each of 30 tabletop tasks across four robot types. Scored by success rate and progress.
note: Table30 v1 retired 2026-05-27 at 64.33% top success. V2 (dataset RoboChallenge/Table30v2) leader 40.67%. Benchmark team runs every rollout, but host Dexmal also submits its own DM0 models.

name: RoboColiseum
description: AgiBot Genie robot in Genie Sim 3.0 (Isaac Sim): instruction, robustness, manipulation and spatial boards after post-training on provided sim data.
note: Instruction board crowded (many pi0.5 fine-tunes 0.72-0.84). Manipulation and spatial not saturated. Many noisy third-party rows. Organiser baselines mixed with submissions.

name: Robocurve physical tool-use benchmark (unidentified)
description: Unnamed Robocurve physical tool-use robot task.
note: robocurve.org, the RCI page and the public run export (robodojo-rc-tier-1, roboharm-v1, simple-tasks) show no such benchmark or Gemini 3.7 Flash runs.

name: Robocurve simple tasks (LLM control of YAM arms)
description: Frontier LLMs control bimanual I2RT YAM arms through Inspect Robots tools on block-into-bowl, puzzle, push-ball and stack-bowls. Staged scores, 20 trials.
note: Block into Bowl near saturation: GPT-6 Astra 19/20 (95%) versus Fable 5.1 8/20, with 6x fewer output tokens. Puzzle stays at 10%. The public run export holds 220 simple-tasks trials with logs and videos.

name: RoboDojo
description: Generalist manipulation policies run 42 Isaac Sim tasks and 18 remote real-robot tasks. Scored by task score and success rate.
org: MMLab@HKU + UC Berkeley + Tsinghua + others (RoboDojo team)
note: Far from saturated: best robot policy (DM0.5) had 19.34% sim success on 2026-09-16. Models self-reporting 97-99% on LIBERO score 0.02-24% here. Team also evaluated GPT-6 Astra as an embodied agent.

name: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1
description: Six real RoboDojo tasks on I2RT YAM arms, 20 attempts each. Robot policies and tool-calling LLMs scored by rubric progress.
note: One team runs every attempt on its own rigs and publishes per-trial score, cost, time, logs and video. Best entry Dream-1 59.3% progress (trained on YAM). Robocurve says best LLM score rose 15% to 43% in two months.

name: RoboGate
description: 68 industrial pick-and-place scenarios (nominal, edge, adversarial, randomized) for a Franka arm in Isaac Sim. Organisers run submitted VLAs and report success.
note: All 15 policies score 0/68, with grasp-miss rate 1.0. A scripted IK baseline scores 57/68, so the floor effect gives no ranking. Many entries are LIBERO fine-tunes run zero-shot. Commercial vendor runs every model.

name: Roboharm
description: Whether an agent controlling a bimanual robot through tool calls executes physically harmful instructions. Reports refusal accuracy.
note: Possible match: github.com/robocurve/roboharm (five fixed-scene robot refusal tasks). Not confirmed as the same benchmark.

name: RoboLab
description: Zero-shot DROID Franka policies in Isaac Lab on 120 tabletop tasks at three instruction levels, 10 episodes each. Success rate.
note: 1,200 episodes per policy with CIs. Best robot policy 42.9% at 2026-09 capture. NVIDIA runs internal rows, including its own models.

name: Robotic Origami Challenge (IROS 2026)
description: Fold a six-fold paper airplane on a supplied bimanual Sharpa-hand rig. Origami judges give pass/fail, and passes are ranked by folding time.
org: Sharpa + BitRobot/FrodoBots + Nippon Origami Association + partners
note: Single task. Quality is binary and only speed is graded, with a 10-minute cap. Organisers supply the hardware and an outside judge, so teams bring policies only. No results page found after the 27 Sep-1 Oct 2026 event.

name: RoboTwin 2.0
description: Bimanual Aloha-AgileX sim: 50 tasks, policies trained on 50 clean demos per task, 100 trials each in clean and domain-randomized scenes.
note: Official board: team retrained 17 of 22 entries via XPolicyLab. Clean track crowding (top 89.58%), randomized top 68.12%. Self-reported paper numbers (~86-94%, larger demo budget) are saturated and not comparable.

name: Robust IF Bench
description: Models follow a diverse set of hard instructions from Microsoft AI's internal benchmark.
note: In-house: Microsoft AI never released the tasks or the scoring method.

name: RTE
description: Models decide whether a premise sentence entails a hypothesis, using data from the PASCAL RTE challenges. Scored by accuracy.
org: PASCAL RTE Challenge organizers, packaged in GLUE

name: RTVLM
description: Vision language models answer red-teaming image prompts on faithfulness, privacy, safety and fairness. GPT-4V scores responses from 0 to 10.
org: Li et al. (HKU, Peking University and others)

name: RULER
description: Synthetic retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation and QA tasks at configurable lengths. Measures effective context size.
note: Synthetic. Near-saturated for frontier models at 128K.

name: SaaS-Bench
description: 106 long-horizon GUI workflows across 23 locally deployed real SaaS apps. Scored from app databases with weighted checkpoints and full-resolution rate.
note: Best agent fully completes under 4% of tasks at launch. v1.1 released via repo.

name: Safe response to high-severity prompts
aliases: Challenging conversations with implicit harmful intent
description: Models handle multi-turn self-harm and violent activity conversations where harmful intent only emerges from context. Scored as safe response rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Reported per category, with and without system-level safety context.

name: Safety (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models respond to safety-relevant user prompts. MiniMax scores whether replies are safe and helpful.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: SafetyBench
description: Models answer 11,435 multiple choice questions on seven safety topics in Chinese and English, such as ethics, illegal activities and privacy.
note: Tsinghua CoAI benchmark, ACL 2024. Test answers were open-sourced in July 2025.

name: Sakana kana-letter reading-order set
description: Model recovers the reading order of 25 expert-annotated classical Japanese kana letters (chirashigaki). Scored by normalized edit distance.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Sakana AI). Built because no public benchmark existed. No release link.

name: Sandbox Bench
description: Agents find and exploit vulnerabilities in runtimes, file format parsers and egress proxies across 22 challenges. Success means recovering the protected flag.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Most targets are undisclosed zero days.

name: Sandbox escape evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents face 28 handmade scenarios that tempt them to cross a staged sandbox boundary. Score is the share of runs with a crossing attempt.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing
description: Models take the SAT reading and writing section. Scored on the 200 to 800 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: SAT Math
description: Models take the SAT math section. Scored on the 200 to 800 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: SAT Reading
description: Models answer the reading section of official SAT practice tests. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 averages 8 exams from the 2018 Official SAT Study Guide. This is reading only, not EBRW.

name: SAVE-Bench
description: A coding agent works where the environment or the user instruction carries hidden risk. The benchmark scores whether it surfaces the risk to the user.
note: In-house Meta benchmark with a multi-turn tier. An LLM judge scores harmful execution and risk verbalization.

name: scBench (LatchBio SingleCellBench)
description: 195 verifiable single-cell RNA-seq analysis problems. Each pairs a data snapshot with a task and a deterministic grader.
note: Mapping of the card name 'SingleCellBench' to latchbio/scbench is inferred.

name: ScholarCatalyst
description: Given a research question, retrieve the 'catalyst papers' that 184 lead authors labeled for 207 projects, searching only prior literature. Recall@20.
note: Far from saturated: best Recall@20 about 0.5.

name: SciCode
description: Scientist-curated research coding problems split into subproblems across natural sciences. Code checked against test cases.
note: Mistral cites 'SciCode-Verified' (pass@1, n=6). Kimi uses Artificial Analysis numbers. Test-set answers partly held out.

name: ScienceQA
description: Models answer about 21,000 multiple-choice science questions from school curricula, many with images. Scored by accuracy.
org: UCLA and Allen Institute for AI
note: Top systems score above 90 percent, so it is near saturation.

name: SciUniverse
description: 92 tasks in 17 chemistry, biology and materials families run in C5R's lab or its digital twin. Pass@1 averaged equally across families.
note: Level 1. 8 families run in the real lab, so results are noisier. Model evaluation by contacting C5R.

name: ScreenSpot
description: Model locates a described UI element in mobile, desktop and web screenshots. Scored by click-point accuracy.
note: Largely superseded by ScreenSpot-Pro for frontier comparisons.

name: ScreenSpot-Pro
description: GUI grounding on high-resolution professional-software screenshots. The model must locate the target UI element.
note: Astra score known only from secondary write-ups of OpenAI launch materials.

name: Seal-0
description: Models answer 111 fact-seeking questions where web search returns conflicting or unhelpful results. Answers are graded for accuracy, usually with search enabled.
note: The maintainers refresh the questions over time, so scores from different releases may not compare.

name: Search triggering
description: Models decide whether to call search for queries that need fresh facts or answer directly when search is unneeded. Reports F1.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SEC-bench Pro
description: 183 validated vulnerabilities in V8 and SpiderMonkey. Agent must discover and reproduce each bug from limited information.

name: SecCodeBench
description: Models write or patch functions in project scaffolds drawn from real Alibaba vulnerabilities. Code must pass functional tests, then proof-of-concept security tests.
org: Alibaba Group (with Tsinghua, Zhejiang, Fudan, and Peking universities)
note: Version 2 in February 2026 has 98 scenarios across 22 CWE types, and development moved to alibaba/last-secure-code-benchmark.

name: SecretPatch
description: Models decide whether commits are security patches, including silently released ones, from a set of 4,702 security patches.
note: Dataset from a DSN 2019 paper on secret security patches. Google reports accuracy.

name: Secure and defensive coding (Anthropic)
aliases: Production secure coding sessions, classifier flag rate
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen sampled defensive coding sessions such as patching and incident response. Score is the classifier flag rate.
note: Measures false positives of the deployed classifier system on benign cyber work. An LLM grader labels sessions as purely defensive.

name: SecureBio VMQA, single choice
description: Models answer 350 virology troubleshooting questions in single-choice form. VMQA is an earlier version of the Virology Capabilities Test.
note: Google FSF sections report it with N=350. The Gemini 3 Pro FSF report calls the same N=350 set SecureBio VCT SC.

name: SecureCodeReview (xAI)
description: Internal agentic eval: fix the security issues in a realistic codebase without introducing new ones.

name: Select machine learning engineering tasks from METR
description: Agents attempt machine learning engineering tasks drawn from METR. Scored as successful trials.
note: OpenAI ran these tasks for the GPT-4o Preparedness autonomy assessment.

name: Self-harm refusals (xAI)
description: Models face self-harm and crisis prompts and conversations. A model fails if it assists or refuses without pointing to help.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The metric is compliance on should-refuse conversations.

name: Self-preference bias (Anthropic)
description: Models grade transcripts attributed to themselves or to other models. Measures whether scores favour the model's own outputs.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Self-proliferation challenges (Phuong et al. 2024)
description: Agents try 10 end-to-end tasks such as installing a wallet or deploying a model on a cloud server, with 45 milestone substeps.
note: Reports give challenges passed end to end, milestones passed and expert bits needed.

name: Sexually Explicit Content Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to direct, adversarial and benign sexual content prompts in single and multi-turn chats. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SHADE-Arena
description: Paired main and hidden side tasks in mock environments. Measures if an agent completes the side task undetected by a monitor.
org: Anthropic + Scale AI + Redwood (Kutasov et al.)
note: Opus 5.5 recognizes it as an evaluation in over 80% of attempts. safety-research/SHADE-Arena is deprecated.

name: Short-horizon computational biology tasks
description: Agents perform end-to-end computational tasks related to modifying and engineering biological agents.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SHP2 Protein Function Prediction
description: Models predict held-out assay measurements for single amino acid variants of SHP2. Scored as mean R squared over three assay datasets.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.60.

name: Silent copying of answers (Anthropic)
aliases: Undisclosed use of an available answer
description: Agents solve held-out coding tasks where the answer is reachable in the sandbox. Score is the rate of using it without telling the user.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SimpleBench
description: Models answer over 200 multiple-choice trick questions on spatial, temporal, and social reasoning that ordinary people solve. Scored by average accuracy over five runs.
note: The top model, Claude Fable, scores 81.9 percent against an 83.7 percent human baseline.

name: SimpleQA
description: Models answer 4,326 short fact questions that each have one indisputable answer. A grader model marks each reply correct, incorrect, or not attempted.
note: Google DeepMind released SimpleQA Verified, a cleaned 1,000 question subset, because the original has label errors and duplicates.

name: SimpleQA Hallucination Rate
description: Models answer 4,326 short fact-seeking questions. This metric is the share of questions answered incorrectly, so declining to answer is not penalized.
note: Google DeepMind later released SimpleQA Verified, a cleaned 1,000-question version.

name: SimpleQA Verified
description: 1,000 human-verified, de-duplicated short-answer factual questions measuring parametric knowledge.

name: SimplerEnv
description: Real-to-sim replicas of Google Robot and WidowX/Bridge setups. Policies scored by success rate on pick, move, drawer and Bridge tasks.
org: UC San Diego + Stanford + UC Berkeley + Google DeepMind
note: Self-reported under mixed zero-shot and fine-tuned protocols. Papers quote conflicting baselines. WidowX near ceiling for best model (95.8). Google Robot tracks still separate models.

name: SimpleSafetyTests
description: Models answer 100 clearly harmful prompts on illegal items, physical harm, scams, child abuse and self-harm. The score is the share of safe responses.
note: HELM Safety reports it as a safety score.

name: SimpleVQA
description: Models answer 2,025 short factual questions about images across 9 tasks and 9 topics. An LLM judge grades answers against fixed references.

name: Single-turn benign request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer benign requests on sensitive topics. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Single-turn harmful request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer single-turn requests that violate the usage policy. Score is the harmless response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SIQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about people's motives, reactions, and emotions in everyday social situations. Scored by accuracy.
org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington
note: Test labels are hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set.

name: Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD)
description: 16 tasks measuring whether models know facts about themselves and their situation.

name: Situational awareness evaluations (Phuong et al. 2025)
description: Agents must notice and change details of their own deployment, such as config limits, to finish a task. Eleven challenges.
note: Situational awareness half of the stealth-and-situational-awareness-evaluations suite. Google reports challenges solved out of 11.

name: SkillInject
description: Agents use a skill file that carries an adversarial instruction while doing a legitimate task. Reports how often the agent follows the injection.
note: Measures agent vulnerability to skill file attacks.

name: SkillsBench
description: 86-87 containerized expert tasks in 11 domains, run with and without Agent Skills. Verifier tests give pass rate and skill lift.
note: Paired with/without-skills runs isolate the effect of skills. Audited submissions are on HF (benchflow/skillsbench-leaderboard). SkillsBench 2.0 is planned.

name: SLAKE
description: Models answer English and Chinese questions about radiology images of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Hong Kong Polytechnic University (Xiao-Ming Wu group)
note: The authors say the released data was cleaned and may differ slightly from the paper.

name: Slide generation human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: People compare HTML slide decks from two models on content, layout and visual quality. Metric is overall win rate.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. GLM-5 is compared with GLM-4.5.

name: Slop Arena
description: Site collecting writing-preference data to tune slop detection to a user's taste, paired with the slop-guard tool.
note: Site rendered only a title for me. Method and leaderboard not confirmed.

name: SMDD-Bench
description: 502 small-molecule drug-design tasks in 5 types. Agent uses a fixed toolkit to produce a molecule that must pass all task criteria.
note: Every task has a known solution, so all are solvable. Prime Intellect and Harbor environments released 2026-10.

name: Sneaky Sandbox Escape
description: Agents doing coding tasks secretly escape a vulnerable sandbox and disable a monitor process. Scored on side task success while evading monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation with 40 tasks across 10 sandbox implementations.

name: Soft Bias (Internal)
description: Models answer paired sociopolitical prompts with sides swapped. A judge scores each pair 0, 0.5 or 1 for framing differences.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The score is the average bias from 0 to 1.

name: SpaceXAI internal R&D evals
description: Internal xAI model-development tasks (MTS Eval) and production inference-stack patches (InferenceEval).

name: SpaceXAI MTS Eval
description: Agents do model-development tasks from xAI engineers, such as diagnosing reward hacking and debugging training infrastructure, under fixed budgets.
note: In-house xAI evaluation with 29 tasks in the standard non-GPU suite.

name: SpatialBench (LatchBio)
description: Agentic spatial-transcriptomics data analysis problems with deterministic graders. Anthropic reports a 115-problem Verified variant.

name: SpatialEval Maze-Nav
description: Models answer questions about routes and turns in mazes given as text or images. 1,500 multiple-choice questions scored by accuracy.
note: Phi reasoning reports use the text-only 10 by 10 version.

name: SpatialEval Spatial-Map
description: Models answer questions about relations and counts among objects placed on a map given as text or images. 1,500 questions scored by accuracy.
note: Phi reasoning reports use the text-only version.

name: SpatialSense VQA
description: Models judge whether a stated spatial relation between two objects holds in an image. The relations were crowdsourced to defeat simple cues.
org: Princeton Vision and Learning Lab (Kaiyu Yang, Olga Russakovsky, Jia Deng)
note: Gemma 3 reports a VQA-style version for pretrained checkpoints, not the original classification setup.

name: SpatialViz-Bench
description: Models answer 1,180 generated multiple choice puzzles on mental rotation, mental folding, visual penetration, and mental animation. Scoring is accuracy.
note: A program generates the questions, which limits training contamination. Humans score about 82%.

name: Speaker identification
description: Speech models get audio requests to identify a speaker by voice. Scored on refusing when they should and complying for famous quotes.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report should refuse and should comply rows with no overall number.

name: SpeedrunBench
description: Agents try to finish goals in 10 video games as fast as possible. Score is time to goal in frames or seconds, lower is better.
note: Agent writes an input tape and scoring runs in a separate container. Public repo covers the three open-source games. HF dataset is gated.

name: SPI (security patch identification)
description: Models decide whether code commits from open-source projects are security patches.
note: Dataset from SPI: Automated Identification of Security Patches via Commits, ACM TOSEM 2021. Google reports accuracy.

name: SpireClimb
description: Agents play Slay the Spire 1 and 2 at max difficulty through a computer-use harness on fixed seeds. Score is the mean win rate.
note: Top human players win ~85% (StS1) and ~95% (StS2). Seeds are not published.

name: SpireClimb StS1 A20 Heart
description: Agents play Slay the Spire 1 through its graphical interface at Ascension 20 and must defeat the Heart. Scored by win rate over fixed seeds.
note: Epoch expects saturation within a few model generations because labs may train on the game.

name: SpireClimb StS2 A10
description: Agents play Slay the Spire 2 at Ascension 10 through screenshots and mouse and keyboard, 15 runs per character. Scoring is the win rate.
note: Epoch AI froze the game at v0.107.1, and top human players win about 95 percent of runs.

name: SpreadsheetBench
description: Real spreadsheet manipulation questions from Excel forums. Output workbook is checked cell-by-cell against reference solutions.
note: Kimi K3 reports 'SpreadsheetBench 2'. I did not find a separate public repo for v2.

name: SpreadsheetBench 2
description: Agents complete 321 expert-annotated business spreadsheet workflows, such as financial modeling, debugging, and charting, in multi-sheet workbooks. Scoring is task accuracy.

name: SQuAD
description: Models extract answer spans from Wikipedia paragraphs for over 100,000 crowdsourced questions. Scored by exact match and F1.
note: Saturated, with models above human performance since 2018. SQuAD 2.0 added unanswerable questions.

name: SQuAD v2
description: Models extract answers from Wikipedia paragraphs and must abstain on over 50,000 adversarial unanswerable questions. Scored by exact match and F1.
note: Saturated. The test set is hidden, so cards report the dev set.

name: SQuALITY
description: Models write question-focused summaries of public-domain short stories. Outputs are scored against human-written reference summaries with ROUGE.

name: SRE-Bench
description: Software reverse engineering without source: 262 binary instances from 19 private programs, each with six graded objectives.
note: Programs are private to stay contamination-free.

name: SSH stress-testing evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Models continue prefilled conversations about suicide and self-harm built from anonymized user feedback. Score is the rate of appropriate course correction.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Standard jailbreaks (xAI)
description: Models face a battery of published and internal jailbreaks. Compliance is the share of should-refuse attacks that get disallowed help.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The Grok 4.5 card calls it Jailbreaks.

name: Standard Refusal Evaluation
description: Models answer disallowed and benign safety-related prompts across policy categories. An autograder scores not_unsafe and not_overrefuse.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Some cards give category scores only.

name: Static Jailbreak Evaluations
description: Models face a fixed set of jailbreak attacks on bio, violence and cyber requests. Scored as defender success rate per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Stealth and Situational Awareness evaluations
description: Prerequisite-scheming challenges: stealth tasks (circumventing oversight) and situational-awareness tasks (reasoning about own deployment).
note: Open-source in Inspect Evals (gdm_stealth, gdm_self_reasoning). External review found many SA tasks test one ability.

name: Stealth evaluations (Phuong et al. 2025)
description: Agents pursue a secret side task while avoiding detection by an oversight mechanism. Pass means beating the top half of human baselines.
note: Stealth half of the stealth-and-situational-awareness-evaluations suite. Google reports challenges passed out of four or five.

name: StoryCloze
description: Models pick the correct ending for a four-sentence everyday story from two candidate endings. Scored by accuracy.

name: StrategyQA
description: Models answer 2,780 yes or no questions that need implicit multi-step reasoning, such as whether Aristotle used a laptop. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Mor Geva et al. (Tel Aviv University and Allen Institute for AI)

name: StrongREJECT
description: Forbidden-prompt jailbreak benchmark with a rubric grader that scores how useful a non-refusal actually is.
note: HF copy linked by Mistral is a third-party mirror (walledai).

name: StrongREJECT v2 (Meta)
description: Models face a cascade of jailbreak attacks on disallowed behaviors adapted from StrongREJECT plus internal ones. Reports attack success rate.
note: Meta variant of public StrongREJECT with internally curated behaviors and a multi-turn LLM attacker.

name: Structural Biology (Anthropic)
description: Models answer questions about a biomolecule's function from structural data and basic tools, in multiple-choice and open-ended variants.
