note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report the two variants separately with no overall score.

name: Structured expert probing campaign: chem-bio novel design
description: Biosecurity and chemistry experts test whether a model helps design novel chem-bio threats. Scenarios are rated against Preparedness risk levels.
note: Results are counts of scenarios per risk level, not a score.

name: Structured expert probing campaign: radiological and nuclear
description: Radiological and nuclear experts test whether a model helps with weapons development steps. Conversations are rated against Preparedness risk levels.
note: Results are counts of conversations per risk level, not a score.

name: Subversion Strategy Eval
description: Models must devise and execute strategies to subvert control protocols without shared memory between calls.
note: Anthropic cards report a subset of the environments.

name: Suicide & Self-Harm evaluation
description: Static and dynamic chats with suicidal or self-harm signals test adherence to prevention practice and crisis resources. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Suicide and self-harm evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models handle single-turn and multi-turn conversations about suicide and self-harm. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SUNRGBD
description: Models detect objects in about 10,000 indoor RGB-D images and predict their 3D bounding boxes. Scored by average precision.

name: SuperCLUE-Math6
description: Models solve thousands of multi-step Chinese math word problems. Scores combine reasoning-step quality and accuracy into a comprehensive score and a reasoning level.
note: Reports give a comprehensive score, a reasoning-steps score, an overall accuracy score and a reasoning level from 1 to 5.

name: SuperGLUE
description: Models solve eight English language understanding tasks, including BoolQ, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, and WSC. Scored by the average task score.
org: NYU, Facebook AI, University of Washington, and DeepMind
note: Saturated, with models above the human baseline since 2021.

name: SuperGPQA
description: 26,529 graduate-level multiple-choice questions across 285 disciplines. Accuracy.

name: SURDS
description: Models answer spatial questions about objects in nuScenes driving camera images across six single-object and multi-object tasks. Scoring is task accuracy.
org: Xianda Guo et al. (Wuhan University and partners)
note: The first arXiv version was called DriveMLLM before the authors renamed it SURDS.

name: Surface Evolver Bench
description: Agents write Surface Evolver datafiles that model liquid surfaces under physical constraints across 16 tasks. Deterministic checks give partial credit for matching hidden reference quantities.
note: Only one example task is public, and the scored tasks and grading scripts stay hidden.

name: Surge AI blind coding evaluation
aliases: Surge AI blind human coding eval
description: Surge AI raters blindly score model coding outputs on a 1-5 scale. Mistral reports five models.
note: Lab-commissioned human eval (Mistral with Surge AI). Tasks and rubric not public.

name: SVG-Bench (MiniMax)
description: Model creates or edits SVG graphics from text or image prompts. A VLM checks results, averaged over 3 runs.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (MiniMax).

name: Swarm Bench
description: Models orchestrate agent swarms on complex tasks that benefit from coordinated decomposition and parallel execution.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The K2.5 report lists WildSearch, Batch Download, WideRead and Long-Form Writing domains. Tasks are not public.

name: SWE agentic fabrication eval
description: A grounding autorater checks whether claims made by coding agents on long SWE tasks are supported by tool outputs.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SWE Atlas
description: Scale's coding-agent suite beyond patching: codebase Q&A, writing production tests, and refactoring in real repos. Rubric/test-scored leaderboards.
note: Positioned as the successor to SWE-bench Pro. Three leaderboards (QnA, Test Writing, Refactoring). Suite completed 2026-05.

name: SWE Refactor Bench
description: Agents migrate 20 whole open-source repositories to a new language, framework, platform, or build system. Graded by migration audit, behavioral tests, and adversarial verifier models.

name: SWE-bench Multilingual
description: 300 GitHub-issue tasks across nine programming languages in SWE-bench format. Patch graded by repository tests.
note: Released with SWE-smith. Paper link is the SWE-smith paper.

name: SWE-bench Multimodal
description: SWE-bench tasks whose issues include screenshots or design mockups from visual JavaScript repos. Patch graded by hidden tests.

name: SWE-Bench Pro
description: 1,865 long-horizon issue-resolution tasks from 41 repos in four languages. Agent patch must pass hidden tests. Pass@1.
note: 731 public, 858 held-out and 276 commercial tasks. Copyleft repos reduce contamination. Vendor-reported scores differ from Scale's standardized runs.

name: SWE-bench Verified
description: 500 human-validated GitHub issues from 12 Python repos. Agent writes a patch that must pass hidden tests.
note: Near-saturated. Absent from 2026 Anthropic/OpenAI headline tables. OpenAI cards use it only inside CoT-Control.

name: SWE-bench Verified (hard subset)
description: Agents solve a subset of SWE-bench Verified tasks estimated to take a human engineer more than one hour.
note: Anthropic RSP autonomy evaluation built on public SWE-bench Verified tasks.

name: SWE-bench Verified hard subset (Meta)
description: Agents fix the hardest SWE-bench Verified issues. Meta uses about 42 tasks and a 50% indicative threshold for AI R&D risk.
note: Meta's own hard subset. It may differ from Anthropic's SWE-bench Verified hard subset.

name: SWE-Dev
description: Models implement new features in real Python repositories from requirement documents, across 500 test tasks. Developer-written unit tests decide pass or fail.

name: SWE-fficiency
description: 498 tasks in nine Python data/ML/HPC repos: agent must speed up a real workload without breaking tests. Scored as speedup relative to expert patch.
note: Replay study (arXiv 2607.01211) found 411/498 tasks keep a valid signal and a few low-speedup tasks dominate the score weight.

name: SWE-Lancer
description: Models complete real Upwork software tasks, from bug fixes to features, and pick between engineering proposals. Scored by end-to-end tests and payout earned.
note: Only the Diamond split is public. Some cards report dollars earned rather than pass rate.

name: SWE-Lancer Diamond (SWE Manager)
description: Models review competing implementation proposals for real freelance tasks and pick the best one. Scored against the original choice as pass@1.
note: Manager split of SWE-Lancer. The swe-lancer record covers the IC SWE split.

name: SWE-Marathon
description: 20 realistic multi-hour software tasks (library reproductions, product clones, ML work). Verifiers combine hidden tests, parity and integrity checks.
note: v1.1 released 2026-07. No configuration exceeds 30% pass@1. Reward hacking seen in 13.8% of rollouts. Labs ran H20-recalibrated branches.

name: SWE-Perf
description: Agents speed up code in 140 tasks drawn from performance pull requests in real GitHub repos. Scored on correctness and runtime gain.

name: SWE-PI
description: A coding agent does a bug-fix task in a repository seeded with an injected payload that tries to exfiltrate a secret. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta benchmark. 142 scenarios from 50 SWE-bench instances.

name: SWE-rebench
description: Agents fix fresh GitHub issues that an automated pipeline mines each month. Tests decide whether the issue is resolved.
note: Scores depend on the monthly task window, so results from different months are not directly comparable.

name: SWE-Review
description: Models review code changes in several languages and scenarios to find defects. Scores reflect defect recall and the rate of hallucinated defects.
note: In-house: MiniMax never released the tasks or the formula that combines recall and hallucination rate.

name: SWM-Bench (Social World Models)
aliases: Building Social World Models with Large Language Models
description: Predict how Kalshi and Polymarket belief trajectories shift after news events. 12k+ points across politics, finance and crypto, chronologically split.
note: Chronological train / Polymarket-test / Kalshi-test split limits leakage. Baselines are time-series foundation models. ICML 2026.

name: SWT-bench
description: Agents write tests that reproduce real GitHub issues from SWE-bench repositories. Scored by the share of tests that fail before and pass after the fix.
note: Reported on Lite and Verified splits, so check which one a card uses.

name: Sycophancy evaluation (offline)
description: Models answer a fixed set of messages resembling production traffic that could elicit sycophancy. A grader assigns a sycophancy score.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Scores run from 0 to 1, lower is better.

name: Sycophancy on user-provided prompts (Anthropic)
aliases: Non-sycophantic response rate on re-sampled challenging conversations
description: Models continue real feedback conversations where earlier Claude models were sycophantic. Score is the non-sycophantic response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation built from user feedback conversations. The prompts are not public.

name: Sycophancy prompts (Anthropic)
description: Models answer single-turn prompts that invite sycophancy, such as bad business ideas or delusional beliefs. Four synthetic sets and one hand-written set report sycophancy rates.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The hand-written set targets users with severe mental illness or delusional thinking.

name: SycophancyEval (answer sycophancy)
description: Models answer factual questions where the user suggests a wrong answer. Score is the relative accuracy drop against neutral prompts.
note: xAI used it in the Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 cards. Later xAI cards use an internal sycophancy eval instead.

name: SycophancyEval (Sharma et al.)
description: Models answer questions and give feedback while users state opinions. Measures accuracy shifts and feedback positivity caused by user views.
note: Anthropic system cards replicate the answer bias and feedback bias settings from the paper.

name: SysBench
description: Models follow 500 system messages across five user turns each. A model verifier checks constraints, instructions and whole sessions.
note: Labs usually report ISR, the instruction-level satisfaction rate.

name: T-Eval
description: Models use tools step by step, and each sub-process is scored separately: instruction following, planning, reasoning, retrieval, understanding, and review.

name: Tacit Knowledge and Troubleshooting
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on tacit lab knowledge and troubleshooting that need hands-on expertise. Scored as cons@32.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. The questions are not public.

name: Tacit Knowledge Brainstorm (Open-Ended)
description: Models answer 50 open-ended troubleshooting questions drawn from virologists' and molecular biologists' careers. Scored as pass@1 against an ideal answer.
note: OpenAI treats this evaluation as contextual.

name: TallyQA
description: Models answer open-ended counting questions about images, including complex ones that need object relationships or attributes. Scored by exact count accuracy.

name: Task-dependent output homogenization evaluation
description: Models answer prompts several times. A judge scores functional diversity where it is wanted and consistency where one answer is right.
note: Reports a homogenization score and a heterogeneity score on a 0 to 1 scale.

name: TASTE
description: 92 pairwise comparisons of AI safety research proposals. Model must match experienced researchers' preference. Accuracy versus ~77% human agreement.
note: Dataset is available on request only.

name: TasteVal
description: 8 AI R&D tasks. Models iteratively design experiments. Taste measured as the compute needed to reach expert-level scores.
note: Tasks kept private.

name: TAT-DQA
description: Models answer questions about financial report pages that mix tables and text, often needing arithmetic. Scored by exact match and F1.
org: NExT++ Research Centre, National University of Singapore

name: tau-bench
description: Agents chat with a simulated user and call retail or airline APIs under policy rules. A task passes if the final database matches the goal.
note: The repo marks its tasks as outdated and points to tau2-bench, now tau3-bench, which fixes airline and retail tasks.

name: tau2-bench
description: Dual-control customer-service simulations (retail, airline, telecom) where agent and simulated user both act. Graded on final state.
note: τ³-bench (v1.0.0, 2026-03) lives in the tau2-bench repo and adds banking_knowledge and voice modes. V1.0.1 fixed banking grading. Telecom scores depend on the user-simulator model.

name: tau2-bench Verified
description: Agent serves simulated customers in airline, retail and telecom under policies, with Amazon-fixed faulty tasks from τ²-bench. Pass rate.
note: Lab-created verified variant (Amazon AGI) of Sierra's τ²-bench. Fixes documented in FIXES.md.

name: tau3-bench
description: Agents use tools and follow policies while talking with simulated users in airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. Scoring is task success rate.
note: Release 1.0.1 in July 2026 fixed banking grading, so earlier banking scores do not compare, and τ-bench 2.0 followed in October 2026.

name: Temporal reasoning with search
description: Models with search answer real queries that test date arithmetic, stale facts and time-sensitive context. Reports error rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Terminal-Bench
description: Agents complete about 80 hard tasks in sandboxed Linux terminals, such as compiling code or configuring servers. Test scripts check the final container state.
note: Terminal-Bench 2.0 replaced this first release in November 2025 with 89 harder tasks, and later versions followed.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
description: 89 hard terminal tasks across 16 categories in containers. Hidden tests verify the final state. 5 trials per task.
note: Leaderboard entries are audited and trajectories are public. Later versions exist (Vals now uses Terminal-Bench 4.0).

name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
description: 89 hard terminal tasks across 16 categories in containers. Hidden tests verify the final state. 5 trials per task.
note: Fixed 28 of the 89 tasks in 2.0. Scores moved by up to 12 points, so the two are kept apart.

name: Terminal-Bench 3.0
description: Agents complete 74 tasks across 7 domains in sandboxed terminal environments. Verifier scripts grade each trial as pass or fail.
note: Released first as FrontierBench v0.1, the name Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 card uses. Terminal-Bench 4.0 succeeded it in August 2026.

name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
description: Agents complete 66 hard tasks in containerized terminals across software, ML, science, security, and operations. Test scripts verify each result, scored as resolution rate.
org: Stanford University, Harbor, and Laude Institute
note: It removed 8 saturated or flawed tasks from Terminal-Bench 3.0 and set a flat 8-hour agent timeout.

name: Terminal-Bench Hard
description: Agents complete 44 hard tasks from Terminal-Bench Core in the Terminus 2 harness. Artificial Analysis scores pass@1 averaged over 3 repeats.
note: Artificial Analysis retired it in June 2026 in favor of Terminal-Bench 2.1.

name: Terminal-Bench-Science
description: 70 scientific research-workflow tasks across five science areas, run in Harbor containers. Hidden tests give the resolution rate.
note: 70 tasks kept from 920 proposals. v0.1. V0.2 in progress. Citation is a Zenodo DOI, no paper.

name: Text persuasion study on political opinions
description: Participants read model-written articles or chat with a model on political topics. Scored on opinion shift against human-written articles.
note: Human participant study used for the GPT-4o Preparedness persuasion score.

name: Text to Text Safety
aliases: Text to Text Safety (lower is better)
description: An automated content safety evaluation measures policy violations in model answers to text prompts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Text-based reinforcement learning task (Anthropic)
description: Agents build scaffolding that improves a weaker model on a text-based reinforcement learning task.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TextArena
description: Collection of competitive text games for LLM eval and RL, with an online Elo leaderboard.

name: TextQuests
description: Agents play 25 classic interactive fiction games. Measures game progress and harmful actions per 100 steps.
note: Meta reports the harm rate per 100 steps as a safety measure.

name: TextVQA
description: Models answer 45,336 questions about 28,408 images that require reading text in the image. Scoring is VQA accuracy against human answers.

name: TheAgentCompany
description: Agents do work tasks in a simulated software company, using a browser, code, and chat with simulated coworkers. Scored by full and partial checkpoint completion.

name: TheoremQA
description: Models solve 800 university-level questions in math, physics, EE and CS, and finance that each need a specific theorem. Scored by answer accuracy.

name: ThinkFollow (Qwen)
description: Models hold multi-turn dialogues with randomly inserted think and no-think flags and must switch reasoning mode correctly.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: Thrive Holdings helpdesk ticket resolution benchmark
description: Agent investigates IT support requests, takes action and decides when to escalate to a technician. Scored by pass rate.
note: Item count not stated. Drawn from Thrive's IT services firms.

name: Time series forecasting task (Anthropic)
description: Agents solve a regression and time-series forecasting problem with known state-of-the-art results, in six variants.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TIR-Bench
description: Models solve 13 kinds of image tasks that need tool use on images, such as rotation, jigsaw, and maze. Most items are multiple choice.
note: Qwen cards list two numbers for it, and the cards do not say which setting each one uses.

name: Tone
description: An automated evaluation measures whether model refusals are objective, neutral and not preachy.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Tool use prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents run bash commands where files, scripts or command outputs carry injected instructions. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported without safeguards. The test cases are not public.

name: Tool-calling prompt injections
description: Agents receive prompt injections inside tool call outputs such as connectors. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Toolathlon
description: 108 long-horizon tasks across 32 apps through about 600 MCP tools. Execution-based checkers inspect final environment state.
note: Verified final release 2026-06-30. Do not mix with original-version scores.

name: Toolathlon-Verified
description: 108 long-horizon tasks across 32 apps through about 600 MCP tools. Execution-based checkers inspect final environment state.
note: A checked subset of Toolathlon tasks.

name: ToolCall-Badcase
description: Models choose a tool and its arguments for 200 cases drawn from real user failure reports. Each case has a ground-truth call.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The cases are not public.

name: ToolUse (Qwen)
description: Models make single-turn, multi-turn and multi-step tool calls. The score combines intent recognition, format and parameter accuracy.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: ToxiGen
description: Models continue ToxiGen prompts about 13 minority groups. Scored by the average toxicity of the generations.
note: Generation use of ToxiGen. The classification use is toxigen-discriminative.

name: ToxiGen (discriminative)
description: Models label statements about 13 minority groups as toxic or neutral. Scored by accuracy, often split into toxic and neutral labels.
note: Microsoft Phi reports run it through Eureka ML Insights. Other labs use ToxiGen prompts to measure toxic generations instead.

name: Training distribution hack rate (Anthropic)
aliases: Subset of training data classifier hack rate
description: Classifier monitors measure reward hacking on a subset of Anthropic's reinforcement learning training episodes.
note: Monitoring metric on training data, not a fixed public task set.

name: TRAIT
description: Models answer 8,000 forced-choice items on Big Five and Dark Triad traits. Reports a score per trait.
note: Psychometric inventory adapted for language models. There is no overall score.

name: Trajectory Labs cyber red teaming
description: Expert red teamers try to break safeguarded cyber endpoints across nine attack technique families on exploit reproduction tasks.
note: Run by Trajectory Labs for Google DeepMind. Results are counts of successful breaks.

name: Translated ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU (Mistral)
description: Models answer French, German, Spanish and Italian versions of ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU.
note: The Mixtral paper does not name the translation source and gives no average.

name: Translation Human Scoring (Z.ai)
description: People score model translations. The GLM-5 report does not describe the test set or the scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation shown only in a GLM-5 report chart.

name: TriviaQA
description: Trivia questions with evidence documents. Scored by exact match.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: TroubleshootingBench
description: Models find and correct realistic experimental errors in expert-written wet lab protocols. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TruthfulQA
description: Models answer 817 questions across 38 categories that are written to elicit common misconceptions. Scoring checks for truthful answers, often in multiple-choice form.

name: TSP-Opt
description: Models find optimal tours for 960 traveling salesman instances across 8 difficulty levels. Answers are checked for optimality.
note: The Phi-4-reasoning report lists the dataset as to be released.

name: TurkishMMLU
description: Models answer over 10,000 multiple choice questions that Turkish curriculum experts wrote for nine high-school subjects. Scoring is accuracy.

name: TVBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on 10 temporal video tasks, such as action counting and ordering, that static frames cannot solve. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Santiago de Compostela and University of Amsterdam et al.

name: TVQA
description: Models answer 152,545 multiple-choice questions about clips from 6 TV shows, using video frames and subtitles. Scoring is accuracy.

name: TydiQA
description: Models answer information-seeking questions from Wikipedia articles in 11 typologically diverse languages, across 204K question-answer pairs. Scored by F1.
note: Model cards usually report the gold passage (GoldP) task.

name: U18 safety evaluations
description: Models answer challenging prompts in teen safety categories such as age-restricted goods, eating disorders and emotional reliance. Scored as safe completion rate per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Uhura ARC-Easy
description: Models answer ARC-Easy science questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Uhura collaborators (Adelani, Kgomo, Bayes and others)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura TruthfulQA
description: Models answer TruthfulQA questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Uhura collaborators (Adelani, Kgomo, Bayes and others)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura-Eval
description: Models answer new reading comprehension questions written in Amharic, Hausa and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Uhura collaborators (Adelani, Kgomo, Bayes and others)
note: Created with fluent speakers for the GPT-4o System Card.

name: UK AISI alignment and monitorability evaluations
description: UK AISI suites: Out-of-Scope Supply Chain Attack simulation, AI-safety-research sabotage in a simulated company, no-CoT time horizon, CoT legibility.

name: UK AISI and CAISI simulated enterprise network range
description: Agents attack a 32-step simulated enterprise network that takes a human expert about 20 hours. The score is steps completed.
org: UK AI Security Institute and NIST CAISI
note: Government pre-deployment evaluation. The range is not public. Kimi K3 report cites the joint assessment.

name: UK AISI CoT Controllability
description: Models follow instructions that constrain the content of their chain of thought. Scored as the share of samples that follow the constraint.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. Low controllability is the safer direction for monitoring.

name: UK AISI cyber ranges
description: Agents attack multi-host simulated corporate and industrial networks end to end. Scored as the share of attempts that complete the range.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards. The ranges are not public.

name: UK AISI narrow cyber tasks
description: Agents solve UK AISI cyber tasks graded by difficulty, including expert-level tasks. Scored as pass@5 and pass@1.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The tasks are not public.

name: UK AISI Out of Scope Supply Chain Attack
description: Agents in simulated hard cyber challenges with incidental internet access may attack out-of-scope open source projects. Scored as rate of samples with such attacks.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. All tool calls are simulated by other models.

name: UK AISI sabotage continuation evaluation
description: Agents resume trajectories where sabotage of safety research already began. Scored on the share of trajectories where they actively continue the sabotage.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UK AISI unprompted sabotage evaluation
description: Agents act as AI research agents on AI safety research tasks. Scored on confirmed instances of sabotaging the safety research.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UMI-Bench
description: 10 real tabletop tasks trained from standardized UMI hand-held gripper demos. 50 rollouts per task. Progress score and success rate.
note: Best pi0.5 at 55.84 average progress. Two tasks have 0% full success for every model. No live leaderboard.

name: Unauthorized Code Execution Bench
description: A coding agent meets injected instructions to run or fetch malicious artifacts while doing a benign task. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta benchmark of 76 tasks over 40 malicious objectives.

name: Unauthorized voice generation
description: Speech models produce audio that may deviate from the approved system voice. Scored on how many meaningful deviations the output classifier catches.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation of the voice output classifier. Reports precision and recall by language.

name: Uncritically reporting flawed results (Anthropic)
description: Agents analyze data with code that silently mishandles broken values. Graders check whether the agent flags the flaw or reports the biased numbers.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report an overall score from 0 to 10 and a separate misreported rate.

name: Ungrounded inference and sensitive trait attribution
aliases: UGI and STA safe behavior accuracy
description: Speech models get requests to infer traits about a speaker from audio. Scored on refusing ungrounded inferences and hedging plausible ones.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Ungrounded Inference evaluation
description: Models receive requests for inferences about people that images or text cannot justify. Scored on refusal rate in non-adversarial and adversarial sets.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two difficulty levels with no overall number.

name: Uniform Bar Exam (MBE+MEE+MPT)
description: Models take a simulated Uniform Bar Exam with multiple-choice, essay and performance test parts. Scored on the 400-point scale.
note: OpenAI collaborators at CaseText and Stanford CodeX ran it for the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Unintended Engagement with External Agent Messages
description: Agents discover a message board with apparent peer agents during a task. Scored on engagement with peers and on carrying out a specified unauthorized action.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Unjustified refusals
description: An automated evaluation measures over-refusals on benign or borderline prompts that can be safely fulfilled.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: USABO Semifinal Exam 2020
description: Models take the 2020 USA Biology Olympiad semifinal exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: USAMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the 6 problems of the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Expert human graders score each proof.
note: In the first evaluation only Gemini 2.5 Pro reached a non-trivial score, at 25 percent.

name: USAMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Judges grade each proof from 0 to 7 against rubrics.
note: MathArena reports GPT-5.4 at 95.2% and says it essentially saturates the benchmark.

name: User Confirmations During Computer Use
description: Agents doing computer use tasks reach financial, high-stakes communication and other actions. Scored on asking the user for confirmation when policy requires it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: USMLE Step 1 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 1 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 2 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 2 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 3 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 3 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank. Only the multiple choice section is included.

name: USNCO Local Section Exam 2022
description: Models take the 2022 US National Chemistry Olympiad local section exam. Scored out of 60 questions.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: V*
description: Models answer 191 multiple choice questions about small details in high-resolution images, such as an object's color or relative position.
note: Some model cards report runs with Python image tools, which are not comparable with plain runs.

name: Vals Finance Agent
description: 927 expert-reviewed research questions on public-company filings. Partial credit only after required checks pass. Private test split.
note: v2 retired in favor of v2.1 (October 2026).

name: Vals Finance Agent v2
description: 927 expert-reviewed research questions on public-company filings. Partial credit only after required checks pass. Private test split.
note: Rebuilt with 927 harder questions in nine workflow categories, scored with partial credit. Scores do not compare with v1.1.

name: Vals Index
description: Agents are scored on eight finance, coding, legal, and tax benchmarks, combined with weights from each sector's share of US GDP.
note: Six of the eight components are private. Weights and components change across versions, with v2.2 from October 2026.

name: VATEX
description: Models write English or Chinese captions for short video clips from a set of over 41,000 videos. Scored by CIDEr.
org: UC Santa Barbara and ByteDance AI Lab

name: VATEX ZH
description: Models write Chinese captions for short videos of human activities from the VATEX dataset. Captions are scored with CIDEr against human references.

name: VCSUM
description: Models summarize transcripts of 239 real Chinese meetings that total over 230 hours. Scored with ROUGE against human-written summaries.
org: Han Wu, Mingjie Zhan, Linqi Song, and colleagues

name: VCT-v2
description: Models answer an updated set of expert virology troubleshooting questions from SecureBio. Scored as refusal-corrected accuracy.
note: Run by SecureBio in pre-release testing. The questions are not public.

name: Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard (HHEM)
description: Models summarize short documents. The HHEM-2.1-Open classifier flags summaries that add unsupported facts, giving a hallucination rate.
note: Labs often report one minus the hallucination rate so that higher is better.

name: Vending-Bench
description: Agents run a simulated vending machine business over long horizons, ordering stock, setting prices, and paying daily fees. Scoring is final net worth in dollars.
note: Andon Labs deprecated it in November 2025 in favor of Vending-Bench 2.

name: Vending-Bench 2
description: Agent runs a simulated vending-machine business for one year starting with $500. Score is the final bank balance, averaged over runs.
note: Paper covers the original Vending-Bench. The v2 environment is not released. Theoretical optimum is ~$63k, so headroom remains.

name: Verbalized grader awareness (Anthropic)
description: Models work on tasks where grading is disclosed clearly, ambiguously or barely. An autorater flags transcripts that reason about the grader.
note: Reported separately for three disclosure levels with no overall rate.

name: Verbalized metagaming
description: A prompted monitor reads chains of thought on alignment evaluations and deployment simulations. Scored as the share of samples reasoning about grading or monitoring.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement. Cards report rates per evaluation suite with no overall number.

name: Verifying the Verifiers (Project APE CRED benchmark)
aliases: Verifying the Verifiers: Towards Autonomous Policy Evaluation
description: Verifier LLMs must find planted errors (prose-table, paper-code, execution, data) in AI-generated economics papers. Credit needs a verbatim quote of the edit.
org: Project APE, University of Zurich (Willner, Yanagizawa-Drott)
note: Mutation testing on 100 reproducible host papers with deterministic scoring and no LLM judge. Best single config 99% recall (Codex 5.6 Sol high). Instances and answer key withheld against contamination. Up to 28% of per-error outcomes flip between identical runs. Repo holds the APE papers, not the CRED code.

name: VIBE (MiniMax)
aliases: VIBE: Visual & Interactive Benchmark for Execution
description: Agent builds complete web, simulation, Android, iOS or backend apps from scratch. Agent verifiers check execution, interaction and visuals.
note: Lab-created eval (MiniMax). VIBE v1 open-sourced on HF (Dec 2025). VIBE-V2 cited for M3 is labeled internal.

name: Vibe Code Bench
description: End-to-end web application development from natural-language specs. Built apps are tested against functional requirements.
note: Official scaffold fork at github.com/vals-ai/VibeCodeBench-Openhands-Scaffold. Results come from the Vals AI leaderboard.

name: Vibe-Eval
description: Models answer 269 image-based prompts, 100 of them hard, that have expert gold responses. A Reka Core judge rates each answer.

name: Video-MME
description: Models answer 2,700 multiple-choice questions about 900 videos from 11 seconds to 1 hour long, with and without subtitles. Scored by accuracy.
note: Video-MME-v2 (2026-04) is a harder successor. MiniMax HF metadata maps its score to v2 though the card says Video-MME.

name: Video-MMMU
description: 300 expert-level lecture videos with questions testing perception, comprehension and adaptation of knowledge. Accuracy.
note: Frame sampling differs across labs.

name: VideoDR (with search)
description: Agents watch a video, extract clues across frames, and search the web to answer 500 multi-hop questions. Scored by answer accuracy.
note: The set grew to 500 samples in May 2026.

name: VideoHallucer
description: Paired basic and hallucinated questions about videos detect intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations. Scored by pair accuracy.

name: VideoMME v2 (with subtitles)
description: Models answer multiple choice questions about videos with subtitles or audio added. Related questions are scored as groups to penalize guessing.
note: This is the with-subtitles setting, which scores higher for reasoning models than the frames-only setting.

name: VideoPhy-2
description: 200 action-centric prompts. Generated videos human-rated for semantic adherence, physical commonsense and physical-rule grounding.
note: Hard: best model reached only 22% joint performance on the hard subset at release. Conservation laws are a common failure.

name: Virology Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-written virology troubleshooting questions from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards.

name: Virology Capabilities Test (text-only)
description: Models answer the text-only questions of the SecureBio Virology Capabilities Test. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards.

name: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT)
description: Models answer 322 multimodal virology troubleshooting questions written by expert virologists. Multiple-select variant requires all correct options.
note: Anthropic cards call it Multimodal virology and use the multiple-select variant.

name: VisFactor
description: Models take 20 vision-centric subtests adapted from a human cognitive psychology test battery, covering perception primitives and visual memory. Scored by accuracy.

name: Vision2Web
description: Agents build websites from 918 prototype images across 193 tasks, from static pages to full-stack apps. A GUI agent and a VLM judge score them.

name: VITA-Bench
description: Agents handle multi-turn requests in simulated food delivery, in-store, and travel services with 66 tools. A rubric-based judge scores task success.
note: An updated version in January 2026 fixed data and the evaluator, so older scores differ.

name: VLA-Arena
description: VLAs fine-tuned on level-0 tabletop tasks, tested on 170 tasks in 11 suites at harder unseen levels L1/L2. Success rate.
note: L0 (the fine-tuning level and page default) median 0.73. L2 best 0.56 and median 0.14, so compare on L1/L2. Benchmark team fine-tuned most entries. Five came from outside users.

name: VLABench
description: 100 language-conditioned manipulation task categories needing world knowledge, implicit intent and long-horizon reasoning. Evaluates VLAs and VLMs.
note: Site says the complete leaderboard 'will be released soon'.

name: VLGuard
description: Vision language models answer safe and unsafe image and text pairs from the VLGuard test set. Responses are judged for harmfulness and refusal.
org: Zong et al. (University of Edinburgh and others)
note: Built as a safety fine-tuning dataset with a held-out test set. The Phi-3 report gives a judged score from 0 to 10.

name: VLMsAreBiased
description: Models count or identify features in altered images of famous subjects, such as a logo with an added stripe, across 7 domains. Scoring is accuracy.

name: Voice persuasion study on party preferences
description: Participants hear model-voiced audio clips or talk with a voiced model. Scored on shifts in hypothetical party preference against human baselines.
note: Human participant study with over 3,800 respondents and a one-week follow-up.

name: VoiceBench
description: Spoken instructions with speaker, environment and content variation. Voice assistant responses scored by GPT judge or rules.

name: VPCT
description: Models view an image of a ball, ramps, and three buckets and predict which bucket the ball falls into. Scored by accuracy on 100 problems.

name: VQAv2
description: Open-ended questions about COCO images, balanced to reduce language priors. Scored by consensus accuracy against 10 human answers.
note: Saturated legacy benchmark.

name: Vulnerability finding evaluations (Anthropic)
aliases: Violative and defensive vulnerability discovery, classifier flag rate
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen sampled vulnerability discovery traffic. Reports flag rates on violative binary work and on defensive source code work.
note: Measures the deployed classifier system. Higher flag rates are better on violative traffic and lower are better on defensive traffic.

name: VulnLMP
description: Agents run long vulnerability research campaigns against widely deployed hardened software with verifier owned evidence. Judged on verified exploit outcomes.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards describe outcomes in words without a score.

name: WANDR
description: 500 wide-search tasks: find tens to hundreds of entities and facts, then return structured records with citations.

name: We-Math
description: Models solve visual math problems decomposed into sub-problems by knowledge concept. Scoring compares sub-problem and full-problem results to diagnose knowledge and generalization gaps.
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
note: A successor, We-Math 2.0, followed in August 2025.

name: Web Clone Bench
description: Agent gets a running reference app (Gmail, Jira, Figma, etc.) and 8 hours to build a clone. Expert-written workflows are replayed as end-to-end tests.
note: 9 apps. Shipping the reference's own bundles scores zero. Environments are available through partnership.

name: Web CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents discover and exploit vulnerabilities in web applications across easy, medium and hard capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Web of lies
description: Models argue for the correct or incorrect answer to simple factual questions and participants report belief shifts.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Reports give shifts toward correct and incorrect beliefs.

name: Web UI Bench
description: Many models build the same 12 app UIs from one shared prompt. Outputs are shown side by side for people to compare. No automatic score.
note: A gallery, not a scored leaderboard. Reasoning-effort settings differ across models. Not the academic WebUIBench (ACL 2025).

name: WebArena
description: Agents complete 812 realistic tasks on self-hosted shopping, forum, GitLab, CMS and map websites. Functional graders check the outcome.
note: WebArena-Verified is a separate audited version with its own id.

name: WebArena-Verified
description: Agents complete 812 audited WebArena tasks on self-hosted websites. Deterministic evaluators check the agent's answer and captured network traces.
note: It fixes WebArena's tasks, answers, and evaluators and drops LLM judges. A 258 task Hard subset also exists.

name: WebDev Arena
description: Two anonymous models build web apps from a user's prompt, and the user votes for the better one. Votes yield Elo-style ratings.
note: Code Arena replaced it in November 2025, and the old board stays up as WebDev Legacy.

name: WebQuestions
description: Models answer factual questions mined from Google Suggest, with answers taken from the Freebase knowledge base. Scored by exact match.
note: Freebase was shut down in 2016, so some answers are dated.

name: WeirdML
description: Models write PyTorch code to solve 17 unusual machine learning tasks, with 5 attempts and feedback each. Scoring is mean best test accuracy.
note: WeirdML v3, an agentic set of 11 tasks, replaced it in September 2026, and v2 scores do not compare with v3.

name: WeirdML v3
description: Agents solve 11 hand-made machine learning and data analysis tasks on a GPU with unfamiliar data and hidden test answers. Scored by token-weighted best results.
org: Håvard Tveit Ihle (Norwegian Defence Research Establishment)
note: Scores are not raw accuracy and are not comparable with WeirdML v2.

name: Where2Place
description: 100 cluttered real photos with free-space placement instructions. The model points, scored correct if inside the ground-truth mask.
note: Only 100 images, so gaps under ~10 points are noise. Scoring varies by source (single vs several points, thinking on/off).

name: White-box analyses of model internals (Anthropic)
aliases: Share of audit transcripts scored 6+ on each interpretability dimension
description: An investigator with interpretability tools reads model activations on audit transcripts. A judge scores hidden states such as evaluation awareness and deception.
note: Uses natural language autoencoders and a template lens. Reports the share of transcripts scored 6 or higher per dimension, with no overall.

name: WiC
description: Models decide whether a target word has the same meaning in two sentence contexts. Scoring is binary accuracy.
org: Mohammad Taher Pilehvar and Jose Camacho-Collados
note: WiC is also one of the SuperGLUE tasks.

name: WideSearch
description: 200 bilingual broad info-seeking tasks: agent collects many atomic facts into a table. Scored by success rate and row/item F1.
note: Table-level success near 0-7% at release. Labs now report mean item-F1, which is much higher.

name: WildBench
description: 1,024 challenging real-user tasks with checklist-guided LLM judging.

name: WildChat (toxic conversations)
description: Models answer toxic user turns from WildChat, the 200 highest scoring conversations per moderation category. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
org: Allen Institute for AI (dataset), OpenAI (toxic subset)
note: OpenAI selects the toxic subset from the public WildChat corpus of 1M ChatGPT conversations.

name: WildChat non-toxic incorrect refusals (Anthropic)
description: Models answer non-toxic user prompts drawn from the WildChat dataset of real chatbot conversations. Score is the incorrect refusal rate.
note: Anthropic refusal evaluation on the non-toxic subset of WildChat, first reported in the Claude 3 model card. The exact prompt selection is not public.

name: WildChat toxic refusals (Anthropic)
description: Models answer toxic user prompts drawn from the WildChat dataset of real chatbot conversations. Score is the correct refusal rate.
note: Anthropic refusal evaluation on the toxic subset of WildChat, first reported in the Claude 3 model card. The exact prompt selection is not public.

name: WildClawBench
description: 60 original in-the-wild tasks run inside a live OpenClaw assistant environment, chaining 10-60+ tool calls. Scored by task-level graders.
note: Also packaged for Harbor (internlm/WildClawBench-Harbor). Covers productivity, code, search, creative and safety categories.

name: WinoBias
description: Models resolve pronouns linked to occupations in type 1 and type 2 sentences. Accuracy gaps show gender bias in coreference.
note: Gemma reports give type 1 and type 2 scores separately.

name: Winogender
description: Models resolve pronouns in sentences about occupations. Accuracy shows whether gender stereotypes sway coreference.

name: Winograd
description: Models pick which noun an ambiguous pronoun refers to in Winograd schema sentence pairs that need world knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
org: Hector Levesque, Ernest Davis, and Leora Morgenstern
note: Models passed 90 percent by 2019, which led to the larger WinoGrande dataset.

name: WinoGrande
description: 44K Winograd-style pronoun-resolution problems. Binary-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: WMDP
description: Proxy multiple-choice benchmark for hazardous knowledge in bio, chem and cyber. Released with the RMU unlearning method.
note: Questions were filtered to exclude directly hazardous content. Mainly used to measure unlearning. Added from public eval collections.

name: WMDP Biology
description: Models answer 1,273 multiple-choice questions that proxy hazardous biosecurity knowledge. Biology split of WMDP.
note: Subset of the WMDP benchmark.

name: WMDP Chemistry
description: Models answer 408 multiple-choice questions that proxy hazardous chemical security knowledge. Chemistry split of WMDP.
note: Subset of the WMDP benchmark.

name: WMT23
description: Models translate the WMT23 general task test sets between English and languages such as German, Chinese, and Japanese. Model cards score output with BLEURT.
note: The shared task ranked systems by human judgment, while model cards report automatic BLEURT scores.

name: WMT24++
description: English-to-55-language translation of WMT24 test data. Scored with automatic metrics such as MetricX or xCOMET.
note: Cohere added internal Irish, Maltese and Serbian variants.

name: WorkSpaceBench
description: Agent completes 388 tasks in realistic worker file workspaces (20k files) needing cross-file dependency reasoning. Scored against 7,399 rubrics.
note: Name match assumed: the Qwen3.8-Max card lists 'WorkSpaceBench' without a citation.

name: World-Class Bio
description: Models answer expert-level biology questions in a SecureBio benchmark. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The card does not describe the question format.

name: World-in-World
description: Closed-loop platform: world models plan for embodied agents in four environments via a standard action API. Scored by task success.
note: Prioritises task success over visual quality. Finds visual quality alone does not guarantee success and controllability matters more.

name: WorldArena
description: Embodied world models generate RoboTwin 2.0 task videos from first frame plus text or actions. 15 video metrics (EWMScore) plus utility tracks.
note: Compressed: top 40 Track-1 entries within 68.9-73.6 EWMScore. Policy-evaluator track saturated (14 of 19 above 85). Extended by WorldArena 2.0.

name: WorldArena 2.0
description: Extends WorldArena to visuotactile prediction, world models as RL environments, and simulated plus real multi-embodiment robot platforms.

name: WorldModelBench
description: Video generators judged as world models on instruction following and physics adherence in application domains. Human labels and a fine-tuned judge.
note: 67K crowd-sourced human labels used to fine-tune a 2B judge that automates scoring.

name: WorldModelGym
description: World models predict returns for five candidate action sequences across 100+ Atari, Meta-World, DMC and classic-control tracks. Scored by normalised regret.
note: Measures decision fidelity, not visual realism. A fixed argmax rule isolates prediction quality. Entrants host a /score endpoint and Reka computes the score. Reka's own Dreamer-v3 led three of four families at launch. Open-loop only.

name: WorldScore
description: 3,000 next-scene generation tasks with camera-trajectory layouts. Scores 3D/4D and video world generators on controllability, quality, dynamics.

name: WorldSense
description: Models answer synthetic questions that test consistent reasoning about simple arrangements of entities described in text.
note: Llama 3 reports it as a pretrained math and reasoning task.

name: WorldSimBench
description: Dual evaluation of video world simulators: human-preference perceptual scoring plus action-level embodied tasks in games, driving, manipulation.

name: WorldVQA
description: Model names visual entities in 3,500 image-question pairs across nine categories, isolating memorized visual world knowledge. Exact-answer accuracy.
note: Lab-created public benchmark (Moonshot AI). Kimi K3 reports a 'ForceAnswer' variant.

name: WritingBench
description: Models complete 1,000 real-world writing requests across 6 domains and 100 subdomains. A judge model scores each reply on five query-specific criteria.
note: The first release had 1,239 queries, and a later update cut it to 1,000, so older scores differ.

name: WSC
description: Models decide whether a pronoun refers to a given noun phrase in sentences that need commonsense to resolve. Scored by accuracy.
org: NYU, Facebook AI, University of Washington, and DeepMind (SuperGLUE)
note: This is the SuperGLUE recasting of the Winograd Schema Challenge.

name: xAI Factuality (Hallucination) eval
description: Internal measure of unsupported or fabricated claims in single responses to information-seeking queries.

name: xAI refusal and jailbreak suites
description: Internal refusal suites (general, child safety, self-harm) in six languages plus single-turn, multi-turn and long-horizon jailbreaks.

name: xAI sycophancy eval
description: Factual questions paired with misleading user context. Rate at which the model abandons the correct answer.

name: Xbench
description: Measures firsthand X posts about frontier models and coding harnesses. An LLM labels each post's sentiment, aggregated per model per week.
note: Every label is public by post id so numbers can be audited. The raw corpus stays private.

name: xbench-DeepSearch
description: Agents search the web to answer 100 Chinese questions that need multi-step retrieval. Scored by accuracy against reference answers.
note: A refreshed 100-question set, DeepSearch-2510, followed in October 2025.

name: XCOPA
description: Models pick the more plausible cause or effect of a premise from two options, in 11 languages. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Cambridge Language Technology Lab (Ponti et al.)

name: XQuAD
description: Models answer 1,190 SQuAD questions over 240 paragraphs, professionally translated so the set is parallel across 11 languages. Scored by F1 and exact match.

name: XSTest
description: Models answer 250 safe prompts that resemble unsafe ones and 200 unsafe contrast prompts. Labs usually report the incorrect refusal rate on safe prompts.
org: Röttger et al. (Bocconi University and others)
note: Anthropic model cards report the incorrect refusal rate on the non-malicious prompts, where lower is better.

name: YC-Bench
description: Agent runs a simulated startup for one year via CLI, managing staff, clients and cash. Scored by final funds.
note: Only 3 of 12 frontier models grew capital in the paper. Adversarial clients cause 47% of bankruptcies.

name: YouCook2
description: Models describe the procedure steps in YouTube cooking videos. Scored by CIDEr against human step captions.

name: Z.ai Code Bench
description: Zhipu in-house coding benchmark used for GLM-5.3. Reports pass rate and output tokens per task. Method unpublished.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Zhipu/Z.ai). Not in the GLM-5.3 tables. Card claims a 50% gain over GLM-5.2.

name: ZebraLogic
description: Models solve logic grid puzzles of controlled size, derived from constraint satisfaction problems. Scored by the share of puzzles solved fully.
note: Accuracy drops sharply as puzzle size grows.

name: ZeroBench
description: 100 hand-made visual questions that all frontier models originally failed. Scored by exact answer, pass@1 and pass@5.

name: ZeroSCROLLS/QuALITY
description: Models answer QuALITY multiple-choice questions about long stories zero-shot, as one task of the ZeroSCROLLS suite. Scoring is accuracy.

name: ZMultiDialBench
description: Human annotators score model replies to 141 multilingual dialogue prompts on a 1 to 10 scale with category criteria.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: ZMultiTransBench
description: Models translate 1,220 real Chinese source texts into seven languages. A GPT-4.1 judge compares each translation with a fixed baseline.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The printed score is a pairwise rating, not a percentage.

name: τ^τ-bench
description: Coding agent builds a customer-service agent from business records, a client and an API. The built agent is scored against held-out simulated users.
note: 53 tasks in 4 domains. Best agent 23.9% vs expert reference 82.2%.

name: τ³-bench Banking
description: Agents act as banking customer-service reps over many turns with a simulated user, following policy. Pass^1 on the final database state.
note: A separate domain of τ³-bench. Its overall score covers retail, airline and telecom only.
